We revisit this regime and identify two token-level redundancy patterns: cross-frame redundancy from static content shared across adjacent frames, and cross-step redundancy from tokens that converge early during denoising. Crucially, we find that early clean estimates along the model's own denoising trajectory provide an effective online signal for locating both patterns, requiring no retraining, auxiliary predictor, or reference video. Based on these findings, we propose PreSTP (Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning), a training-free framework that constructs a unified token-wise redundancy mask from cross-frame similarity and cross-step convergence. Tokens marked as redundant skip subsequent computation under a consistent last-computed-value restoration rule, and a content-adaptive mask reuse strategy further reduces dense probing cost. On 5-second generation, PreSTP achieves 1.52x-3.20x speedups and a better efficiency-fidelity trade-off than coarse-grained caching baselines such as TeaCache and FlowCache. On 30-second generation, it reaches up to 1.96x speedup while improving VBench-Long and suppressing long-horizon drift. Notably, it continues to reduce inference cost even in the extreme one-step regime, where cross-step redundancy vanishes entirely and coarse step-wise caching is no longer applicable.

authors.name: Jia Li, Xurui Peng, Xing Wang, Hayden Kwok-Hay So

papers.title: Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling with Target-Aware Bounded Optimization for Visual Generation
papers.summary: Post-training aims to enhance desired attributes in visual generative models while preserving their general generation capabilities. Reward-guided post-training faces two challenges: real training data may mismatch the generator's output distribution, and attribute supervision may be confounded by unrelated content. Unbounded reward maximization can also cause overoptimization and degrade generation quality. We propose a framework combining Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling (GARM) and Target-Aware Bounded Optimization (TABO). GARM mitigates distribution mismatch through generator-support matching and reduces content confounding using content-matched real contrasts, yielding generator-relevant, attribute-focused reward supervision. TABO maps the learned reward to a smooth, upper-bounded function calibrated from real target-positive examples. This transformation is independent of the optimization algorithm and supports both direct reward-gradient and policy-based optimization. We further introduce Target-Aware GRPO (TA-GRPO), an adaptation of Flow-GRPO that combines fixed stage-wise advantage scaling, a generator-to-target curriculum, and timestep-balanced credit assignment for flow-based video optimization. Experiments show that GARM improves target-attribute expression while maintaining competitive generation quality. TABO better balances attribute enhancement and visual quality than unconstrained reward maximization, while TA-GRPO improves target enhancement over vanilla Flow-GRPO and reduces unintended attribute leakage on neutral prompts. These results highlight the importance of generator-aligned reward supervision and controlled, data-calibrated optimization for targeted visual generation.

authors.name: Ziqiao Weng, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Weidong Cai, Xuelong Li

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics-Aware Industrial Anomaly Detection and Reasoning
papers.summary: Industrial Anomaly Detection (IAD) is a long-established problem that aims to detect defects in industrial products during manufacturing for quality control. Most existing studies focus on static visual patterns as the basis for detection. However, in real manufacturing environments, many anomalies are dynamics-based, such as irregular movements that cannot be perceived from static cues alone. We observe that even recent Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based approaches fall short in identifying such dynamic anomalies due to limited temporal modeling capability. To address this, we introduce MUSTARD: MUltimodal SpatioTemporal Anomaly Reasoning and Detection, a framework that equips MLLMs with fine-grained spatiotemporal dynamics awareness for detecting and reasoning about dynamics-based defects. MUSTARD introduces optical-flow-guided keyframe selection and augmented modalities to capture critical motion irregularities through local motion patterns and global dynamic evolution. Its normal pattern-based reasoning pipeline requires only a few normal reference samples as the detection basis, avoiding any model updates. This enables efficient adaptation across various products and provides high decision interpretability. MUSTARD is the first MLLM-based framework for dynamics-based IAD. Experiments demonstrate its superior performance in detecting spatiotemporal anomalies and providing plausible explanations. Our code is available at https://github.com/racercode/Mustard

authors.name: S-Wei Chen, Siangyu Yang, Yi-Chen Jan, Chun-Yi Lee, Shao-Yuan Lo

papers.title: A Cytology Dataset for Early Detection of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.summary: Oral squamous cell carcinoma OSCC is a major global health burden, particularly in several regions across Asia, Africa, and South America, where it accounts for a significant proportion of cancer cases. Early detection dramatically improves outcomes, with stage I cancers achieving up to 90 percent survival. However, traditional diagnosis based on histopathology has limited accessibility in low-resource settings because it is invasive, resource-intensive, and reliant on expert pathologists. On the other hand, oral cytology of brush biopsy offers a minimally invasive and lower cost alternative, provided that the remaining challenges, inter observer variability and unavailability of expert pathologists can be addressed using artificial intelligence. Development and validation of robust AI solutions requires access to large, labeled, and multi-source datasets to train high capacity models that generalize across domain shifts. We introduce the first large and multicenter oral cytology dataset, comprising annotated slides stained with Papanicolaou(PAP) and May-Grunwald-Giemsa(MGG) protocols, collected from ten tertiary medical centers in India. The dataset is labeled and annotated by expert pathologists for cellular anomaly classification and detection, is designed to advance AI driven diagnostic methods. By filling the gap in publicly available oral cytology datasets, this resource aims to enhance automated detection, reduce diagnostic errors, and improve early OSCC diagnosis in resource-constrained settings, ultimately contributing to reduced mortality and better patient outcomes worldwide.

authors.name: Garima Jain, Sanghamitra Pati, Mona Duggal, Amit Sethi, Abhijeet Patil, Gururaj Malekar, Nilesh Kowe, Jitender Kumar, Jatin Kashyap, Divyajeet Rout, Deepali, Hitesh, Nishi Halduniya, Sharat Kumar, Heena Tabassum, Rupinder Singh Dhaliwal, Sucheta Devi Khuraijam, Sushma Khuraijam, Sharmila Laishram, Simmi Kharb, Sunita Singh, K. Swaminadtan, Ranjana Solanki, Deepika Hemranjani, Shashank Nath Singh, Uma Handa, Manveen Kaur, Surinder Singhal, Shivani Kalhan, Rakesh Kumar Gupta, Ravi. S, D. Pavithra, Sunil Kumar Mahto, Arvind Kumar, Deepali Tirkey, Saurav Banerjee, L. Sreelakshmi

papers.title: prNet: Data-Driven Phase Retrieval via Stochastic Refinement
papers.summary: Phase retrieval is an ill-posed inverse problem in which existing methods often struggle to balance reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality. We propose a novel Langevin-based framework for phase retrieval that bridges model-driven and data-driven approaches by combining stochastic posterior sampling, learned denoising, and model-based updates to better navigate the perception-distortion tradeoff. The framework consists of three progressively more advanced variants. The first, prNet-Small, provides a theoretically grounded and lightweight pipeline that integrates Langevin dynamics with learned noise and denoising processes and alternating projection-based updates. Building upon this foundation, prNet-Large exploits parallel sampling of diverse reconstructions and aggregates them to approximate the MMSE solution, significantly improving distortion metrics. Finally, prNet-Large-Adversarial enhances perceptual quality by replacing simple averaging with an adversarially trained aggregation network while preserving reconstruction fidelity. In addition, we incorporate test time augmentation to further improve the performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms classical, deep learning-based, and diffusion-based baselines across multiple benchmarks in both reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality. The source code and trained models are available at https://github.com/METU-SPACE-Lab/prNet-for-Phase-Retrieval

authors.name: Mehmet Onurcan Kaya, Figen S. Oktem

papers.title: VLD: Visual Learned Distance as an Interface for Reinforcement Learning Navigation
papers.summary: Training end-to-end policies from image data to directly predict navigation actions for robotic systems has proven inherently difficult. Existing approaches often suffer from either the sim-to-real gap during policy transfer or limited action-labeled training data. To address this problem, we introduce Visual Learned Distance (VLD), a scalable framework for image-goal navigation that decouples perception learning from policy learning. We first train a self-supervised distance-to-goal predictor on about 3,000 hours of internet-scale and simulated video, providing a distance signal that a reinforcement learning (RL) policy can minimize. The RL policy is trained separately in simulation using privileged geometric distances perturbed by GeoNoise, a learned noise model that reproduces the viewpoint- and overlap-dependent errors of the trained distance predictor. At deployment, the policy consumes VLD predictions zero-shot, without retraining, inheriting ``where to go'' from large-scale visual training while retaining the robust navigation behaviors learned in simulation. This error modeling is key to the transfer: with VLD inputs, GeoNoise-trained policies reach $58.7\%$ success on HM3D and $76.2\%$ on Gibson, whereas policies trained with generic temporally correlated noise collapse to $4.9\%$ and $11.5\%$. On a physical robot, the VLD-driven policy succeeds in $88\%$ of trials, compared with $60\%$ for a strong end-to-end image-goal baseline that outperforms it in simulation. Our decoupled design thus provides an alternative and scalable path toward reliable navigation policies that transfer from simulation to the real world.

authors.name: Lazar Milikic, Manthan Patel, Jonas Frey

papers.title: Platonic Representations in the Human Brain: Unsupervised Recovery of Universal Geometry
papers.summary: The Strong Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests that representational convergence in artificial neural networks can be harnessed constructively: embeddings can be translated across models through a universal latent space without paired data. We ask whether an analogous geometry can be recovered across human brains. Using fMRI data from the Natural Scenes Dataset, we propose a self-supervised encoder that learns subject-specific embeddings from brain data alone by exploiting repeated stimulus presentations. We show that these independently learned spaces can be translated across subjects using unsupervised orthogonal rotations, without paired cross-subject samples or intermediate model representations. Synchronizing pairwise rotations into a single shared latent space further improves cross-subject retrieval. These results provide evidence for a shared geometry in learned representations of human visual responses: subject-specific fMRI embeddings can be aligned across individuals within a common coordinate system.

authors.name: Pablo Marcos-Manch\'on, Rishi Jha, Llu\'is Fuentemilla

papers.title: Erase the Mark, Preserve the Motion: Temporally Consistent Removal of Video Watermarks
papers.summary: Recent advances in video generation have increased the demand for reliable watermarking for copyright protection, yet the robustness of video watermarks against removal attacks remains underexplored. Most watermark-removal methods originate from the image domain: signal optimization injects imperceptible pixel-domain perturbations, whereas generative resynthesis produces a visually similar instance through diffusion synthesis. When extended to videos, the former introduces temporally varying noise that causes visible flickering, while the latter regenerates fine-grained structures inconsistently across frames, leading to structural motion inconsistency. To evaluate video watermark robustness, we propose PoseRegen, a pose-consistent reconstruction framework that removes watermarks while preserving the original content and motion. PoseRegen first applies a temporally shared viewpoint transformation to disrupt watermark-bearing spatial patterns and then jointly reconstructs the transformed sequence with a pose-conditioned video model. A frozen video DiT processes the complete sequence with its reference-video latent, and full-sequence Flow Matching supervision keeps identity and background consistent across frames. To further preserve motion structure, we introduce a lightweight Pose-Conditioned Motion Consistency Adapter that adapts the frozen backbone to temporally ordered pose guidance and constrains body-part trajectories throughout reconstruction. Experiments on eleven video watermarking schemes show that PoseRegen reduces the average bit accuracy to 0.505, near random guessing, while outperforming the strongest baseline by 9.34% on motion-related VBench metrics. These results reveal a practical vulnerability of current video watermarks and highlight the need to evaluate robustness jointly with temporal and motion quality.

authors.name: Yifan Liao, Zhen Sun, Zhicong Huang, Jiaming He, Zongmin Zhang, Xi Ai, Cheng Hong, Xinhu Zheng, Xinlei He

papers.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
papers.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 19.4% for the best competing WAM.

authors.name: Huiwon Jang, Suhyeok Jang, Hyeonmo Kang, Seungku Kim, Jinwoo Shin, Sihyun Yu

papers.title: A Novel Conditional Adversarial Diffusion Model for High-Fidelity OCT-to-OCT Image Translation and Precise Anti-VEGF Therapy Response Prediction in Diabetic Macular Edema
papers.summary: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is a leading cause of severe vision loss among working-age adults. Although intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections currently serve as the first-line therapy for DME, a notable subset of patients fails to respond despite the substantial cost and clinical burden, suggesting they may benefit more from alternative interventions. Automated, noninvasive pre-treatment response assessment could therefore spare non-responders from the current trial-and-error treatment paradigm. In this study, we propose a novel conditional adversarial diffusion framework that synthesizes post-treatment optical coherence tomography (OCT) images from baseline scans, enabling the derivation of each patient's initial response to anti-VEGF therapy. The model was developed with subject-level 5-fold cross-validation on a US cohort (n = 127) and externally validated on an independent Iranian cohort (n = 44). Benchmarked against fourteen baseline and state-of-the-art translation models, the proposed model achieved the best treatment-response prediction performance among the methods evaluated for that task on both cohorts, with balanced accuracies of 85.7% and 93.0% on the US cohort and 85.2% and 95.3% on the external Iranian cohort at the 10% and 20% central subfield thickness reduction thresholds, respectively. Ultimately, this framework offers a decision-support tool to help ophthalmologists anticipate initial anti-VEGF outcomes in DME prior to treatment initiation, toward personalized therapy selection. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

authors.name: Reza Rasti, Armin Biglari, Sobhan Mohammadi Hafshejani, Alireza Dehghani, Michael J. Allingham, Sina Farsiu

papers.title: Rotating Black Holes in Perfect Fluid Dark Matter: Horizons, Photon Orbits, and Shadows
papers.summary: We investigate rotating black holes surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter (PFDM), described by the parameter \(k\), and determine the Kerr-connected region of the \((a/M,k/M)\) parameter space that contains an event horizon. The critical value \(k_{\mathrm c}(a)\), obtained from the degenerate-horizon conditions \(\Delta(r_{\mathrm c})=\Delta'(r_{\mathrm c})=0\), defines the boundary between black-hole and horizonless configurations. We derive an exact parametric form of this extremal boundary and show that its near-Kerr behavior includes a logarithmic correction; therefore, \(k_{\mathrm c}/M\simeq2.8828(1-a/M)^{1.5377}\) is only an empirical fit over \(0.90\leq a/M\leq0.999\), not an asymptotic scaling law. For horizon-bearing solutions, we calculate unstable spherical photon orbits and the shadow's mean radius, area, and distortion, finding that increasing \(k/M\) shifts the photon region inward and reduces the shadow size. Backward ray tracing through a phenomenological optically thin disk, tested on independent \(41^2\), \(81^2\), and \(161^2\) image grids, confirms this trend: for \(a/M=0.9\) and an inclination of \(17^\circ\), the \(20~\mu\mathrm{as}\) beam-convolved ridge diameter decreases from \(42.47\) to \(37.88~\mu\mathrm{as}\) as \(k/M\) increases from 0 to \(0.08\), with the two finest grids agreeing to within \(0.5\%\). Thus, PFDM produces a consistent contraction from the horizon and photon region to the geometric shadow and image ridge, although these illustrative images do not provide an Event Horizon Telescope constraint because they lack a self-consistent emission model and interferometric likelihood analysis.

authors.name: G. G. L. Nashed

papers.title: How balloons lose their charge by collecting ions from the air
papers.summary: The air we breathe contains radioactive particles. Each time one of these particles decays, it creates hundreds of thousands of ionized air molecules. These ions make the air conductive, which is one reason insulated surfaces lose charge over time. Here we observe the discharge of two statically charged balloons by measuring the repulsive force between them over time. The initial rates of charge loss are relatively large, especially at higher humidities. This large rate of charge loss is likely dominated by the emission of water ions from the balloons surface. Approximately 1 hour after charging, the charge loss rates are much smaller and agree with predictions calculated from the radon concentration in the air and the size of the room, for reasonable aerosol concentrations.

authors.name: J. Pantaleone (University of Alaska Anchorage)

papers.title: $\cal{PT}$-Symmetric GUP-Modified Single- and Double-Well Quartic Oscillators
papers.summary: We study the GUP-deformed quartic oscillator $H_\eta=p^2+\eta p^4+x^4$ and distinguish its real-axis realization from complex-contour realizations. A contour chosen to remain in the decay sectors compatible with the undeformed quartic oscillator gives low-lying eigenvalues that approach the ordinary quartic spectrum as $\eta\to0^+$. This limiting-compatible contour does not, by itself, produce a low-level $\PT$-symmetry-breaking transition. To investigate exceptional points while retaining the same quartic leading behavior, we then introduce the explicitly $\PT$-symmetric extension $H_{\eta,a,g}=p^2+\eta p^4+x^4-a x^2+\ii g x^3$ and fix $a=4$, for which the real part of the potential has a double-well form. Harmonic-oscillator-basis diagonalization with basis dimensions up to $N=100$ yields a converged exceptional-point branch: the critical coupling increases from $g_{\mathrm{EP}}\simeq0.10222364$ at $\eta=0$ to $g_{\mathrm{EP}}\simeq0.15603309$ at $\eta=0.1$. Across the transition, the two lowest real eigenvalues coalesce and continue as a complex-conjugate pair. The exceptional-point results belong to this stated double-well extension, not to the original single-well Hamiltonian alone.

authors.name: Saber Zarrinkamar

papers.title: Predicting next-week VIIRS fire detections in Bolivia: a reproducible benchmark with temporal and geographic evaluation
papers.summary: Weekly detection forecasts could help prioritize fire monitoring across Bolivia. We estimate the probability of at least one fire detection by the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership satellite in each 0.05-degree cell during the following 7 days. Primary models were fixed before test scoring. Calibrated LightGBM, a gradient-boosted decision-tree model, reaches 2023-2025 temporal-test average precision (AP) of 0.323 (95% block-bootstrap interval 0.222-0.383), compared with 0.167 for climatology and 0.143 for persistence. Its paired AP gain over climatology is 0.1567 (0.0998-0.2179). A separately selected geographic model reaches AP 0.384 versus 0.181 for persistence in regions excluded from fitting. In the temporal-test population, reviewing the highest-ranked 5% and 10% of eligible area would have covered 38.4% and 55.8% of cell-weeks with detections. Probabilities still overestimate detection frequency in the highest-probability group. Retrospective rainfall provides no clear AP improvement; the primary validation comparisons for vegetation, land cover and their combination are inconclusive. Positive secondary or exploratory intervals do not change those decisions. Evaluation requires complete target and recent-history observations and measures satellite detections, not individual fires, causes or burned area. Prospective evaluation should archive inputs at each weekly issue and measure ranking, calibration and the usefulness of selected cells for monitoring decisions.

authors.name: Victor Hugo Cuellar Flores

papers.title: Revisiting Routh's Classification of the Heavy Symmetric Top: A Correction
papers.summary: The classification of the motion of a heavy symmetric top when conserved angular momenta are different is studied by considering modern method and Routh's geometrical method. It is shown that Routh's method provides correct classification for four cases; however, it fails in two cases.

authors.name: Vedat Tanriverdi

papers.title: An Analytical Model for Laser-Activated Two-Phase Choking and Microfluidic Suction on Surface Boundary Layers
papers.summary: We present a predictive fluid mechanics model to calculate pressure drops (0.25 atm) and fluid velocities (2.50 m/s) governed by localized phase change and choking phenomena in a capillary-constrained, coaxial microfluidic actuator. Driven by near-infrared thermal absorption, the analytical framework describes how energy deposition drives vapor cavity growth and subsequent cavitation bubble collapse, inducing a transient suction force across a curved, two-radii Young-Laplace capillary boundary. Velocity drops are derived from closed-form analytical equations that explicitly couple vapor volume dynamics with non-linear flow area restriction and fluid drag. The model predicts a maximum boundary layer wall shear stress of 30.06 Pa at the target interface. Crucially, this shear magnitude matches the physical threshold required to mechanically strip surface contaminant boundary layers while remaining below the damage threshold of underlying target substrates. Finally, we formulate a closed-form expression for the maximum allowable liquid inlet temperature required to prevent thermal saturation and sustain stable, continuous microfluidic suction cycles. These equations establish direct engineering design rules for optimizing phase-change microfluidic actuators and next-generation coaxial fluidic systems.

authors.name: D. Tsiklauri

papers.title: An Overview of Classical Scattering by a Lennard-Jones Potential
papers.summary: We present a numerical and conceptual overview of classical scattering under a Lennard-Jones potential. All results were obtained by direct integration of particle trajectories in the two-dimensional plane for varying impact parameters and energies. From these trajectories, we compute deflection functions, identify critical values associated with unstable circular orbits, and visualize non-monotonic behavior in the angular deflection. We construct color maps representing the deflection angle and interaction delay time as functions of energy and impact parameter, and determine the differential cross section from the deflection function, accounting for multi-valued contributions. These results are displayed both as individual plots and as a full color map in the energy-angle plane, providing a detailed picture of the scattering behavior in this central potential.

authors.name: Tiago Kroetz

papers.title: Reconstruction of Global Groundwater Storage Anomaly from GRACE Satellite Gravimetry Using a Physics-Constrained Decomposition LSTM
papers.summary: Groundwater is the largest accessible store of freshwater on Earth, yet its depletion has been difficult to quantify globally, because satellite gravimetry senses total water storage rather than groundwater alone, the record is coarse and interrupted, and the models used to isolate groundwater underestimate the largest trends. Here, a continuous and physically bounded record of global groundwater storage change was reconstructed for April 2002 to December 2022 at half-degree resolution. Total water storage from the GRACE and GRACE-FO missions was separated from its land-surface components, and a physics-constrained decomposition network learned the groundwater signal as the sum of a trend, a seasonal cycle, and a residual. The trend of every cell was held within the net moisture that the atmosphere can supply, and the mass balance of each river basin was enforced during training, so the learned field could not violate water availability. The reconstruction reproduced withheld observations with a root mean squared error of 6.97 centimeters and a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.69, and against an independent network of monitoring wells it achieved a lower trend error than an independent hydrological model and a data-assimilation product at every aggregation scale tested. Gross groundwater depletion over significantly declining cells was estimated at 358 +/- 12 cubic kilometers per year, while net storage change across all land cells was -36 +/- 18 cubic kilometers per year, equivalent to 0.10 +/- 0.05 millimeters per year of sea-level rise. The associated mass redistribution implies a drift of the Earth's rotational pole of 6.9 centimeters per year toward 68.6 degrees East, within 4.5 degrees of the direction inferred in an earlier study.

authors.name: Arpon Sarkar, Showmitra Kumar Sarkar, Mafrid Haydar

papers.title: Tailoring resonator geometry for astigmatism compensation with structured light in birefringent optical cavities
papers.summary: In this work, we experimentally investigate the astigmatism induced by a birefringent crystal inside an optical cavity and demonstrate a geometric compensation strategy for structured modes carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM). We show that the astigmatism observed in the semimonolithic configuration can be fully compensated by introducing a third mirror to fold the cavity, thereby exploiting the geometric astigmatism arising from oblique incidence on the curved mirror. By performing a study of the resonator geometry, both theoretical and experimental results confirm that this approach enables the preservation of OAM between the pump beam and the converted signal and idler modes, providing an effective design strategy for birefringent optical cavities.

authors.name: J. C. de Carvalho Jr., R. F. Barros, A. Z. Khoury, C. E. R. Souza, G. B. Alves

papers.title: Modulation Induced Memory Resonances in Dynamically Driven Optical Cavities
papers.summary: Temporal modulation of optical cavities provides a powerful mechanism for controlling photonic states beyond the static cavity paradigm. Here, we investigate the dynamics of periodically driven optical cavities using a time-dependent cavity-field model with modulated resonance frequencies. We demonstrate modulation-induced tuning of cavity resonances and analyze the resulting intracavity field evolution in both amplitude and phase. The interplay between periodic modulation and cavity dissipation gives rise to pronounced hysteretic behavior, revealing memory effects associated with the finite photon lifetime of the cavity. By quantifying the hysteresis area as a function of modulation frequency, we identify distinct memory resonances characterized by enhanced field-history dependence at specific driving frequencies. Furthermore, we examine the time-resolved local density of optical states (LDOS) and show that temporal modulation enables dynamic spectral redistribution of photonic states, with the degree of confinement governed by the cavity loss rate. Our results establish a simple framework for understanding and engineering memory effects in dynamically driven optical resonators and provide new opportunities for tunable photonic environments, dynamic LDOS control, and reconfigurable light-matter interactions.

authors.name: Faizan H. Lone

papers.title: The Re-Foundation of Radar Meteorology
papers.summary: Since the early development of radar meteorology in the 1940s, rainfall retrieval has traditionally relied on empirical scaling relationships between radar variables and rainfall rate. Here, we revisit the premise that horizontal and differential reflectivity sufficiently constrain the rainfall rate despite the variability of the underlying drop size distribution. Motivated by evidences that this variability requires at least three degrees of freedom, we develop a nonparametric statistical retrieval algorithm that considers different combinations of drop count and distribution shape compatible with the same radar observations. The method separates the contributions of drop count and distribution shape. It then empirically estimates how the shape factors for rainfall rate and horizontal reflectivity, as well as differential reflectivity, vary with the mean and skewness of the drop diameter distribution. These relationships identify compatible combinations of drop count and shape, from which rainfall rates are calculated and their median returned as the estimate. Neither a prescribed analytical drop size distribution nor a scaling rainfall estimator or explicit classification of precipitation regimes is required. We evaluate the method using a worldwide database (149 disdrometer datasets from 76 locations), with radar observables calculated from measured drop spectra. In cross-dataset validation, the method achieves lower median dispersion of relative retrieval errors across all 16 combinations of training and validation instrument types with respect two benchmark methods consisting of the traditional scaling law relationship, and a direct nonparametric fit. These findings motivate a reassessment of the foundations of radar rainfall retrieval by incorporating the range of rainfall rates compatible with radar observation.

authors.name: Massimiliano Ignaccolo, Carlo De Michele

papers.title: Medical Radioisotopes: Clinical Demand, Production Physics, and Untapped Pathways
papers.summary: Over 40 radioisotopes are currently in use or under development across virtually all fields of modern medicine. Their availability relies on a complex interplay of nuclear physics, radiochemistry, and nuclear medicine. This review provides an isotope-by-isotope map of medically important radioisotopes from the perspective of these disparate yet complementary fields. We address the landscape grouped into three tiers: the established clinical core, including, familiar workhorses such as Tc-99m, F-18, Lu-177; an under-leveraged middle tier including Re-186, Re-188, and Sm-153, and the emerging frontier, radioisotopes with demonstrated but underutilised clinical promise such as Ac-225, At-211, Cu-67, and Sc-47. We discuss the properties of these radioisotopes with respect to clinical applications and their production pathways, as well as the associated nuclear and radiochemical challenges. We synthesise these disparate perspectives to identify situations in which alleviating production-side bottlenecks may improve access and patient outcomes.

authors.name: Jarrett Moon, Claire Huchthausen, Jose R Alonso, Shadi A Esfahani, Faraz Farhadi, David McClain, Hamid Sabet, Pedram Heidari, Janet M Conrad, Daniel Winklehner

papers.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
papers.summary: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 $\mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, this low-loss HfO$_{2}$ metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.

authors.name: Be\'ata Idesov\'a, Alexander A. Antonov, Lina Rohrer, Leonardo de Souza Menezes, Andreas Tittl, Tom\'a\v{s} \v{S}ikola, Filip Ligmajer

papers.title: Medical Radioisotopes: Supply-chain Resilience, Distributed Production, and Access
papers.summary: Over 50 million diagnostic procedures involving medical radioisotopes are performed per year and the number of therapeutic and theranostic agents continues to climb. Yet, the global supply chain is far from stable and many regions are underserved. This is the second of a Series of two review papers providing a comprehensive overview of the landscape of medically relevant radioisotopes. This paper focuses on the supply chain. It presents a critical overview of the 2025-2026 status quo, case studies of acute stressors and disruptions they caused, and methods in place to secure a stable supply. A literature-based analysis is paired with expert interviews. We argue that the ageing fleet of nuclear reactors currently used for the centralised production of many isotopes should be complemented by regional accelerator-based centres, alleviating single-point failures and cross-border logistics complications, and increasing access to short-lived isotopes in harder-to-reach regions and low- and middle-income countries.

authors.name: David McClain, Daniel Winklehner, Faraz Farhadi, Jose R Alonso, Shadi A Esfahani, Claire Huchthausen, Jarrett Moon, Hamid Sabet, Pedram Heidari, Janet M Conrad

papers.title: Immobilisation and remobilisation of surfactant-covered drop interfaces in electric fields: Simulations
papers.summary: Fluid--fluid interfaces are seldom clean due to the presence of surfactants, which can strongly modify their dynamics. Interfacial flow redistributes surfactant, creating concentration gradients whose Marangoni stresses can immobilise the interface. By contrast, surface diffusion or exchange with the bulk can reduce these gradients and restore interfacial motion. We study this competition using a two-dimensional model of a surfactant-covered leaky-dielectric drop in a uniform electric field. Electric stresses drive the classical Taylor circulation, in which the drop remains non-rotating. At stronger fields, convection of interfacial charge can destabilise this state and produce the Quincke regime, characterised by spontaneous mean rotation. Using a fully nonlinear model on a fixed circular interface, we show that weak surfactant diffusion allows Marangoni stresses to suppress the Taylor circulation almost completely. Quincke rotation remobilises this nearly arrested interface and restores a substantial straining circulation, whose orientation varies with the applied field. Surfactant also shifts the critical field for rotation and can change the onset from subcritical to supercritical. Surface diffusion and exchange with a well-mixed bulk reservoir can produce similar flow responses and rotation thresholds despite different surfactant distributions. The spatial variation of surfactant concentration therefore provides additional information for distinguishing the two transport mechanisms.

authors.name: Debasish Das

papers.title: Laser-Direct-Written polymer WGM microring laser integrated on a fiber tip for refractive index sensing
papers.summary: Whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microlasers are promising for refractometric sensing, but their practical implementation can be limited by the need for stable resonator-coupler alignment. Here, we demonstrate a Rhodamine B-doped polymer WGM microring laser directly fabricated on an optical-fiber tip, eliminating the external resonator-fiber coupling interface at the sensing head. Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined for fabrication, while finite-difference time-domain simulations guide the microring laser design. The microlasers operate in air and water with thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively. Refractometric measurements in aqueous glucose solutions yield a bulk refractive index sensitivity of 364.95 nm/RIU and a detection limit of 2.47 x 10^(-4) RIU. Water-induced polymer changes and photobleaching are also investigated. This fiber-tip architecture provides a basis for probe-based refractometric sensing in environmental and biochemical applications.

authors.name: Mobin Yaghoobi, Seyedeh Mahshad Hosseini, Leila Hajshahvaladi, Gholam-Mohammad Parsanasab, Mohammad Ismail Zibaii

papers.title: Electrohydrodynamic interactions of two Quincke rotors: asymptotic theory and boundary element simulations
papers.summary: Weakly conducting spheres suspended in a leaky dielectric fluid can undergo spontaneous Quincke rotation when the applied electric field exceeds a critical value. We investigate how electric and hydrodynamic interactions modify this instability and the subsequent rotation of two spheres at fixed separation and orientation. Starting from electric dipole and hydrodynamic rotlet interactions, we develop a systematic far-field asymptotic theory. Away from onset, slow drift of the rotation axes makes a regular expansion fail at long times. A multiple-scale expansion gives slow phase equations that select the axes according to pair orientation and field strength. Near onset, weak interactions produce corrections comparable to the isolated rotation magnitude. A detuned multiple-scale expansion gives coupled equations for the transverse dipole amplitudes. Their linearization identifies four collective rotation modes, whose critical fields and steady branches with one active mode are determined together with their stability. At leading order near onset, electric interaction shifts all four modal thresholds equally, whereas hydrodynamic interaction makes counter-rotation appear first for pair angles below $\cos^{-1}(1/\sqrt3)\simeq54.7^\circ$ and co-rotation above it. Away from onset, the angle separating stable counter-rotation from stable co-rotation increases with field strength. Boundary element method (BEM) simulations place onset within a field interval for each configuration and resolve the growth and relaxation of rotation. Steady-speed comparisons show how pair orientation changes the balance between electric and hydrodynamic effects. We compare the unexpanded dipole-rotlet model of Das and Saintillan [Phys. Rev. E 87, 043014 (2013)] with our asymptotic theory and BEM simulations.

authors.name: Debasish Das

papers.title: Dual-energy cardiac DSA imaging using a dual-layer flat-panel detector: in vivo validation study
papers.summary: Background: The temporal misregistration in conventional X-ray digital subtraction angiography (DSA) remains a key challenge for its practical application in cardiac catheterization, leading to incomplete separation of cardiac vessels from background anatomical structures. Purpose: In this study, the X-ray spectral information is unveiled for DSA imaging to generate better visualization of cardiac vessels with negligible anatomical background. Methods: A dedicated dual-energy DSA imaging model is proposed based on the subtraction residuals between pre-contrast and post-contrast spectral projections, enabling accurate material decomposition without requiring precise scatter correction. Specifically, a dual-layer flat-panel detector (DL-FPD) is assumed to acquire the needed temporally registered low-energy and high-energy projections. Moreover, a penalized likelihood material decomposition algorithm is proposed to enhance the material decomposition performance. To validate, in vivo swine experiments were conducted for the first time on a clinical DSA system equipped with a DL-FPD. Results: Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrated that the impact of scatter on the subtraction residuals can be reduced by more than 80%, substantially improving material decomposition accuracy. Compared with analytical material decomposition, the penalized-likelihood material decomposition algorithm significantly improves image contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), enabling the visualization of small vessels and even the myocardial blush effect. Furthermore, compared with conventional dual-energy subtraction, the penalized-likelihood approach provides more quantitative material maps with fewer overlapping anatomical background artifacts. Conclusion: This preliminary study verifies that dual-energy DSA imaging method is able to generate high-quality cardiovascular imaging results.

authors.name: Yuhang Tan, Jiongtao Zhu, Xin Zhang, Haodi Wu, Xiao Xuan, Mang Feng, Mingzhi Cui, Hairong Zheng, Dong Liang, Yongshuai Ge

papers.title: Differential chiral sensing at exceptional points in intrinsically chiral metastructures
papers.summary: Discriminating opposite enantiomers through their weak chiroptical responses remains a fundamental challenge in optical sensing. Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian singularities at which eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, offer a route to enhanced spectral responses through their characteristic square-root eigenvalue splitting. However, their potential for chiral discrimination remains largely unexplored. We demonstrate exceptional points in an intrinsically chiral hybrid metamaterial and reveal strongly asymmetric responses to enantiomeric perturbations. The interplay between intrinsic chirality and non-Hermitian degeneracy is realized through the coupling of a chiral plasmonic nanoantenna array to a photonic crystal slab. We observe characteristic complex-square-root scaling, with both resonance frequencies and loss-rates exhibiting pronounced handedness dependence. Remarkably, opposite enantiomers produce complex mode splittings that differ by more than an order of magnitude. Our findings establish intrinsic chirality as a new degree of freedom in non-Hermitian physics and reveal a fundamental route toward topological singularities enhanced discrimination of chiral matter.

authors.name: Suzit Hasan Nayem, Zhanni Wu, Mariusz Drong, Kamyar Behrouzi, Boubacar Kant\'e

papers.title: Self-injection-locked dark-soliton Kerr optical frequency combs with high even-order normal dispersion
papers.summary: We numerically investigate dissipative dark-soliton (DDS) microcombs under the action of pure high even-order normal (HEON) dispersion in a microresonator with the self-injection locking (SIL). Pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion can support DDSs formed by interlocked switching waves, directly excited through a SIL-based turnkey scheme without detuning sweeps. Compared to the pure 4th-order case, the switching-wave tail oscillation period increases and its decay rate decreases with the increase of the dispersion order. Although the overall comb bandwidth narrows, the number of non-pump comb lines above a common absolute power threshold increases. Furthermore, the feedback phase controls the DDS duty cycle and intracavity comb-line power distribution, while the increase of the pump power improves the estimated pump-to-comb output conversion efficiency.

authors.name: Lei Shi, Rujiang Li, Shilong Liu, Dumitru Mihalache, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li

papers.title: Fortuitous Cancellation of Competing Effects in the Free Energy of Water Autoionization: Long-Range Electrostatics, System Size, and Nuclear Quantum Effects
papers.summary: Few molecular processes are more fundamental to chemistry than the autoionization of water, whose equilibrium constant, $K_w \approx 10^{-14}$, underlies acid-base equilibria and the chemistry of life. Yet the molecular origins of the free energy cost of forming and separating ions remain incompletely understood. Efforts to explain it have been limited by the difficulty of modeling water reactivity in sufficient detail. Here we combine machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with spectral adaptive biasing force enhanced sampling to connect proton transfer and water wire configurations to the underlying free energy landscape. We identify competing influences of long-range electrostatics, system size, temperature, and nuclear quantum motion on the predicted ionization thermodynamics. The free energy surface extends from neutral water to ions separated beyond the solvent-separated ion pair (SSIP). It reveals a transition state in which a proton is shared between the second and third molecules of a three-membered water wire. The contact ion pair is unstable and the SSIP only weakly metastable, so determining pK$_w$ requires sampling longer wires. Long-range electrostatics raise the free energy at ion separations beyond $3\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. Models with comparable force errors give substantially different free energy profiles in this region. Increasing system size lowers the calculated pK$_w$, while nuclear quantum effects bring it closer to experiment and reproduce the higher pK$_w$ of D$_2$O relative to H$_2$O. These results establish a baseline for interpreting thermodynamic results from MLIP simulations in which charged and polar groups react and diffuse in finite cells. Our analysis also explains how cancellation among competing effects can yield ionization constants close to experiment even when simulations omit several physical contributions.

authors.name: Samuel Varner, Yinan Xu, Yezhi Jin, Gustavo R. P\'erez-Lemus, Pablo F. Zubieta Rico, Zhiying Yi, Joan M. Montes de Oca, Paul F. Nealey, Seth B. Darling, Zhen-Gang Wang, Juan J. de Pablo

papers.title: A Jump-Diffusion Model of Home Price Dynamics and Neighborhood Change
papers.summary: We develop a dynamical model that links the fluctuations of individual home prices to changes in the full distribution of home prices in an urban area. We model the price of an individual home as a jump-diffusion stochastic differential equation. To capture the dynamic and hyper-local economic conditions that drive the residential real estate market, we allow all parameters to depend on both time and neighborhood. In the mean-field limit, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) governing the evolution of the home price distribution in a neighborhood. We quantify spatial heterogeneity within a city by using the Wasserstein-2 distance to compare home price distributions across the city's neighborhoods. We validate our model using data from Boston, Massachusetts as a case study.

authors.name: Ashley Peake, Adam Gilbert-Diamond, Anette E. Hosoi

papers.title: Sub-filter-scale stress and heat flux in hypersonic Couette flow and a flat-plate boundary layer
papers.summary: A comparative study of sub-filter-scale (SFS) quantities in hypersonic Couette flow and flat-plate boundary layer turbulence under strongly cooled-wall conditions is carried out using filtered direct numerical simulation (DNS) data to characterize the differences in SFS dynamics between internal and external wall-bounded turbulence. The two flows exhibit similar near-wall behaviour in the mean velocity profiles and SFS stress components; however, marked differences emerge in the outer layer and thermal structure. The two configurations also exhibit different thermal fields, leading to different temperature-velocity relations. The SFS behaviour shows strong sensitivity to the filtering operation: the top-hat filter yields larger SFS magnitudes, whereas the sharp spectral filter preserves a distinct spectral separation near the cutoff, leading to characteristic SFS features. Decomposition of the SFS terms shows that the residual component provides the dominant contribution to the mean SFS shear stress and heat flux. Differences between the two flows are primarily associated with the interaction terms between the resolved and residual components, which contribute with opposite signs in the two configurations, consistent with their different thermal structures. The different thermal structures also lead to distinct SFS heat-flux behaviour, including a sign change in the flat-plate boundary layer. Instantaneous SFS fields further reveal that local extrema arise from the combined contributions of multiple decomposed terms. Although these terms exhibit large local fluctuations, their net contributions to the averaged SFS quantities are relatively small. The trace of the SFS stress exhibits local negative values, reflecting local energy redistribution across the filter scale rather than a loss of physical energy.

authors.name: Raagvendra Singh, Sabbir Ahmed, Lian Duan, Carlo Scalo, Takahiko Toki

papers.title: Smart Spectral Doppler Ultrasound Imaging using Motion Tracking based on Wide-beam transmission and Neural Networks: Preliminary Results
papers.summary: Ultrasound spectral Doppler imaging provides quantitative blood flow information for vascular diagnosis, but its accuracy is limited by the one-dimensional (1D) sample volume (SV). Motion from respiration, patient movement, and probe manipulation can move the target vessel out of the SV, causing spectral broadening, signal reduction, or loss of the spectrum. A two-dimensional (2D) SV can address this, but sequential focused-beam transmission reduces the pulse-repetition frequency (PRF), and plane-wave transmission lowers the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In this study, we propose a wide-beam transmission method that acquires a 2D SV from a single transmit event while preserving the PRF. A Hamming network, which requires no prior training, tracks axial and lateral motion within the 2D SV and updates the position of an adaptive 1D SV for each frame. Field II simulations showed that the wide-beam transmission had a spectral SNR comparable to that of focused-beam transmission and approximately 10 dB higher than that of plane-wave transmission. The motion tracking correctly detected the target position in over 93% of frames for vessel radii greater than 1 mm, and in 100% of frames for radii greater than 2 mm. In vivo studies of a carotid artery (linear array) and a hepatic vein (convex array) showed that the proposed method recovered obscured spectra and increased the spectral SNR by 9.3 dB and 4.5 dB, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed wide-beam transmission with Hamming network-based tracking can improve the accuracy of spectral Doppler imaging under tissue motion. Moreover, we anticipate that the proposed approach can be implemented in real-time due to its single transmission and simple two-layer architecture with low computational complexity.

authors.name: Jihye Baek, Allison Lee, Jinbum Kang, Yangmo Yoo

papers.title: Optical microscopy for pathological imaging: past, present, and future
papers.summary: Histopathology, the microscopic examination of stained tissue sections, remains the gold standard for pathology imaging, but its bright-field imaging is largely morphological. Advanced optical microscopy techniques move beyond this by exploiting diverse light-matter interactions, and are increasingly applied to pathological imaging. By capturing signals such as refractive index, polarisation, harmonic generation, Brillouin shift, and molecular vibrations, these microscopy techniques can provide quantitative or semi-quantitative information on tissue structure, mechanics, and chemical or molecular composition. In this review, we summarise the physical principles, key quantitative parameters, and representative pathological applications of seven modalities--optical diffraction tomography, polarisation microscopy, second-harmonic generation microscopy, third-harmonic generation microscopy, Brillouin microscopy, Raman microscopy, and fluorescence microscopy. We also discuss progress in artificial intelligence that supports reconstruction, analysis, and interpretation across these modalities, together with emerging trends in multimodal integration. Overall, this review shows how different optical contrasts can complement routine histopathology, while outlining the challenges and opportunities that will shape their clinical translation.

authors.name: Runchen Zhang, Xiaoyi Shang, Liangyu Deng, Jingyu Wang, Xiaoyu Zheng, Lanyu Cui, Yao Du, Jiaxin Zhuang, Yifei Ma, Wanying Liu, Limei Guo, Lin Luo, Zhiyi Liu, Stephen M. Morris, Honghui He, Chao He

papers.title: Domain-Adapted Deep Optical Flow for Multiphase Velocimetry in Unsteady Cloud Cavitation
papers.summary: Time-resolved velocimetry inside cloud cavitation remains a fundamental measurement problem. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) requires uniform tracer seeding and undistorted particle images, and cavitating flow violates both, because tracers do not penetrate vapor structures and refractive index mismatch across deforming interfaces produces spurious vectors. We present a domain-adapted deep optical flow framework for two-phase velocimetry, built on a Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms (RAFT) architecture fine-tuned on synthetic image pairs rendered from multiphase OpenFOAM simulations (RAFT-CloudCav). It is evaluated against a pre-trained generalist RAFT model, Farneb\"ack and OpenPIV on 130,000 frames/s recordings of a Venturi test section at 30 and 48 L/min. As no experimental ground truth exists, validation uses three quantities that require none, namely the integrated flow rate against a turbine meter, the liquid-phase velocity divergence, which mass conservation requires to vanish, and the station-to-station spread of the flow rate. RAFT-CloudCav recovers 47.75 L/min against a metered 48.0 $\pm$ 0.5 L/min, the closest of the four methods, and its flow rate varies by 2.0% across four streamwise stations, versus 6-7% for the classical methods. It returns a coherent near-wall reverse flow of -0.71 m/s, the time-averaged signature of the upstream-propagating re-entrant jet, where OpenPIV returns none. In the non-cavitating control, at 51 $\mu$m/pixel only three grid points fall inside a 0.68 mm boundary layer and the peak wall-normal gradient is under-predicted more than thirtyfold, while 13 and 19 $\mu$m/pixel agree with each other. The mean field is recovered without tracer particles at roughly three times the per-frame uncertainty. Uncertainties are estimated a posteriori from the image residual and propagated conservatively.

authors.name: Naga Nitish Chamala, Sanjay Vasanth Kethanur Balasubramaniam, Olivier Coutier-Delgosha

papers.title: Raytracing and quantifying the inferior mirage
papers.summary: Using custom raytracing code, we explore several features of the inferior mirage that are not widely discussed, such as the blurring in the mirage image, and what happens to the light in the direct image region that is replaced by the mirage image. The raytracing model also clarifies how to quantify the mirage, and we provide expressions to calculate the angular extent of the mirage under given thermal conditions and measurement geometry.

authors.name: Nathan Hagen, Lucas Reyes Bentancor, Kakeru Tanaka, Norimasa Hanaya, Momo Shoda, Hiroki Maki, Takuma Ando, Keisaku Yoshizawa, Kayo Suzuki, Yume Yamada, Asana Kumakura

papers.title: An acousto-optic colorimeter for color psychophysics
papers.summary: A complete model of human color perception requires the ability to present any color as a stimulus.Most existing measurements were collected with physical color samples, and current laboratory generators, such as displays and multi-primary LED systems, work with a small number of fixed primaries. Published color-difference data therefore cover about 40\% of the CIE~$xy$ chromaticity diagram, while commercial wide-gamut displays already reach two thirds of it and need difference metrics there. We describe an acousto-optic colorimeter that lets the experimenter choose the primaries. The device selects up to four narrow bands from a supercontinuum (white-light) laser, each with electronically set wavelength and intensity, and covers 95\% of the CIE~$xy$ chromaticity diagram. Threshold-scale color differences, presented in alternation as in a discrimination experiment, are reproduced with a mean error of 0.08--0.12 CIEDE2000 units ($\Delta E_{00}$) at five CIE-recommended color centers. Because one color can be built from many combinations of narrow bands, the bands are chosen for the task: the finest adjustment for color matching, the least disagreement between observers for color-difference measurement. In simulations with 151~individual observers from a published dataset, with these bands observers see colors 0.6--1.9~$\Delta E_{00}$ from the intended one on average, against 1.2--2.5~$\Delta E_{00}$ on a calibrated wide-gamut LCD, lower at every center. The approach applies to any narrowband source and lets experimenters use saturated colors while limiting the effect of individual differences in color vision.

authors.name: Sergey Korchagin, Georgiy Lobarev, Pavel Aksentsev, Pavel Maximov, Maria Gracheva, Olga Polschikova, Egor Ershov

papers.title: Low-Rank Iteration for Efficient Calculations of Topological Surface States
papers.summary: Surface states are hallmarks of topological phases, and their efficient computation is crucial for topology characterization. Conventional supercell methods (SCM) approximate semi-infinite systems as finite periodic ones, but suffer from high computational cost, artificial inter-surface coupling, and slow convergence near band edges. Recently, boundary problems for semi-infinite systems have been recast as block-tridiagonal equations and solved by the cyclic reduction method (CRM) and the transfer matrix method (TMM). However, these approaches remain resource-intensive, as fine-mesh discretization produces very large matrices. Recognizing the intrinsic sparsity and low rank of these matrices, we develop a low-rank iterative method (LIM) with stochastic trace estimation that substantially reduces complexity and memory without sacrificing accuracy, while remaining straightforwardly parallelizable. Benchmarks on 2D and 3D topological systems show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over CRM and TMM. LIM extends readily to heterostructures, defective interfaces, and non-Hermitian systems, providing an efficient platform for topological and plasmonic surface phenomena.

authors.name: Kaiqi Liu, Changsheng He, Zihan Xie, Shulin Sun, Lei Zhou, Shaojie Ma

papers.title: When is an Optical Design Problem a Mass Transfer Problem?
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether optical design problems can be represented as Monge--Kantorovich mass transfer problems with some cost function. An optical problem is specified by a function defining a particular family of supporting surfaces for the optical element. We introduce the notion of geometric equivalence between optical and transport problems, which is directly related to the possibility of formulating an optical design problem as a mass transfer problem. A necessary condition for such equivalence is derived in the semi-discrete setting. It allows a transport representation to be ruled out without choosing a cost function in advance. The condition is applied to the near-field refractor problem and to the design of two refracting surfaces transforming a spherical beam into a spherical or collimated beam. For these problems, the necessary condition is shown to fail in physically admissible configurations. We also study an optical element with a single working surface and an arbitrary regular incident wavefront. In the far field, geometric equivalence to a mass transfer problem requires a planar or spherical wavefront, whereas in the near field with a planar target, the necessary condition fails for an arbitrary smooth wavefront.

authors.name: Albert A. Mingazov

papers.title: Independent nuclear charge radius determinations: bound-electron $g$ factor versus muonic atom spectroscopy
papers.summary: We present an alternative method to determine absolute nuclear charge radii competitively via the bound electron $g$ factor of H-like ions. The method is demonstrated for $^{118}$Sn by extracting its radius with a precision of 0.1%. This is the second most precise radius ever determined from an electronic system. We benchmark our result against a state-of-the-art value derived from the spectrum of muonic $^{118}$Sn. This comparison reveals a 3.2$\sigma$ tension, prompting a careful reexamination of the calculations and calling for additional measurements. Crucially, after decades, we now have two independent methods to measure absolute charge radii with similar precision.

authors.name: F. Hei{\ss}e (Max-Planck-Institut f\"ur Kernphysik, Heidelberg, Germany), I. A. Valuev (Max-Planck-Institut f\"ur Kernphysik, Heidelberg, Germany), J. Solanki (Max-Planck-Institut f\"ur Kernphysik, Heidelberg, Germany), V. A. Yerokhin (Max-Planck-Institut f\"ur Kernphysik, Heidelberg, Germany), B. Ohayon (The Helen Diller Quantum Center, Department of Physics, Technion-Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel), N. S. Oreshkina (Max-Planck-Institut f\"ur Kernphysik, Heidelberg, Germany)

papers.title: Redetermination of the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BaMgF4
papers.summary: BaMgF4 (BMF) has the potential to serve as a platform material for vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) nonlinear optics owing to its ferroelectricity and high UV transparency down to 130 nm. However, the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients reported for BMF span approximately one order of magnitude, hindering a reliable assessment of its potential for nonlinear optical applications. Here, we redetermined these coefficients by combining Maker fringe, wedge, and single-pass second-harmonic-generation measurements at a fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm. Our results establish that all the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BMF lie in the range of 0.01-0.04 pm/V. We determined d31 to be 0.035 pm/V, which is among the largest coefficients of BMF, while it has been underestimated relative to the other coefficients in previous studies. Although d31 is not the largest coefficient, the use of its long corresponding coherence length is beneficial for quasi-phase matching, particularly for VUV generation, where the fabrication of lower-order quasi-phase-matching structures is crucial.

authors.name: Shoichi Ui, Simon J. Herr, Gaetano G. M. Bonetti, Ingo Breunig, Fraunk K\"uhnemann, Matthias Bickermann, Hiroki Tanaka

papers.title: Absolute Calibration of a Broadband Transmission Grating Spectrometer from 5 to 400 nm with Uncertainty Estimates
papers.summary: We present the absolute calibration of a transmission grating spectrometer (TGS) with uncertainty estimates in the 5--400 nm range using synchrotron radiation at the BEAR beamline at Elettra light source in Trieste, Italy. Firstly, the spectral responsivity of a Si photodiode in the spectrometer was absolutely calibrated with respect to the absolutely-calibrated beamline photodiode. Subsequently, this photodiode was used to calibrate the transmittance of Zr and Al thin-film filters, along with bulk MgF$_2$ and UV-grade fused silica windows at their operating positions in the spectrometer to minimize mounting-induced uncertainties. Next, the quantum efficiency of the spectrometer's CCD camera was calibrated over the 5--400 nm range. Lastly, three gratings with line densities of 10000, 3000, and 1000 lines/mm were calibrated for spectroscopy in the ranges extending from soft X-ray to extreme-, vacuum- and deep-ultraviolet (DUV) wavelengths, respectively. The combination of various filters and gratings enables absolutely calibrated spectroscopy with high versatility across a broad wavelength range from soft X-rays to DUV.

authors.name: E. Chebykin, A. E. H. Gaballah, R. van der Horst, A. Giglia, N. Mahne, M. van de Kerkhof, M. D. Ackermann, M. Bayraktar

papers.title: Role of E-F Coupling on Low-latitude Ingression of Mid-latitude MSTIDs over the Indian Subcontinent
papers.summary: This study provides the first observational evidence that E-F region electrodynamic coupling regulates the southernmost latitudinal extent of nighttime mid-latitude medium-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances (MSTIDs) over the Indian subcontinent. We have analyzed multiple MSTID events using total electron content (TEC) measurements from a dense network of dual-frequency GNSS receivers across India, GNSS radio occultation (RO) profiles, and ionosonde observations from New Delhi during May-July 2025, a high solar activity period. The lowest geographic latitude, at which MSTIDs wavefronts reached, varied between 17{\deg}N and 25{\deg}N. Their low-latitude extension showed no significant correlation with background TEC, but was positively correlated with the geomagnetically mapped southernmost latitude of sporadic-E (Es) layers identified from GNSS-RO measurements. These events occurred during high solar activity, when F-region MSTID growth is generally suppressed. Therefore, our results suggest that electrodynamic coupling with the underlying Es-layers is essential for sustaining MSTIDs and enabling their low-latitude penetration during solar maxima.

authors.name: Jeevan Upadhyaya, Dipjyoti Patgiri, Mehta Harsh Jayeshkumar, Rahul Rathi, Virendra Yadav, Satarupa Chakrabarti, Arun K. Upadhayaya, Sumanta Sarkhel

papers.title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
papers.summary: Material architecture can evolve during loading, yet its mechanically expressed symmetry depends on both the structural state and the constitutive coupling. We connect these quantities through one parent-invariant free energy with a symmetric traceless internal tensor $\mathbf Q$. Its stabilizer distinguishes isotropic, uniaxial, and biaxial states, and projected gradient kinetics satisfies the structural dissipation inequality. Parent invariance generally guarantees only symmetry inheritance. For an explicit two-coupling elastic potential, we derive a stiffness-contraction reconstruction of $\mathbf Q$ and prove equality of the structural and tangent rotational symmetries for every nonzero coupling pair. The associated acoustic tensor links residual symmetry to protected transverse degeneracies. For a small uniaxial state, the leading squared-speed gap is $|\gamma_2s|\sin^2\vartheta/(2\rho_0)$; coupling selectivity and residual protection can suppress this term. We also derive a directional acoustic-trace reconstruction and state calibrated and nuisance-aware inverse conditions. Dimensionless structural-field, acoustic, transient finite-element, and synthetic inverse examples illustrate the predictions. The framework connects state evolution, mechanically expressed symmetry, and conditional observability without assigning independent dynamics to a group label.

authors.name: Pengfei Zhu, Leiming Du, Guoqi Zhang

papers.title: Complex Hyperspin Machine and Symmetry Quenching: Benchmark and scaling up to millions of degrees of freedom
papers.summary: Driven-dissipative oscillator networks have been proposed to simulate spin models on physical hardware, mostly focusing on systems of binary (Ising) spins, or systems of spin vectors in low dimensions. The equalized hyperspin machine was recently introduced to provide a single platform to simulate general models of $N$ coupled spin vectors with tunable dimension $D$, realizing dynamical annealing protocols to vary the spin dimensionality in time. These schemes are limited to real spins coupled via real coupling matrices. We propose a generalization of the hyperspin machine that works with complex fields and deals with complex Hermitian coupling matrices, implementing an amplitude equalization scheme. This system, which we name complex hyperspin machine, can work on optimization problems with complex valued hyperspins that can be cast on complex $D$-vector Hamiltonians. We benchmark the machine against a differential evolution (DE) algorithm on complex $D=2$ hyperspins up to $N=80$, showing that the fraction of instances where a lower-energy solution is found grows with system size and coupling density, reaching $92.5\%$ at the largest considered sizes. When the DE finds a lower-energy solution, the machine still reaches a median relative energy deviation that lies between $10^{-15}$ and $10^{-12}$ while running at substantially lower computational cost. Using the complex nature of the field, we introduce a new dimensional reduction protocol that we name symmetry quenching, which collapses complex variables that map to XY spins onto real Ising spins by switching on the parametric pump. We show on Max-Cut instances with known ground states that symmetry quenching outperforms a fixed-pump Ising machine, reaching exact ground states in the presence of equalization. We scale the system to $N=10^6$ hyperspins, or $8\times10^6$ dynamical variables, on a Hermitian sparse two-dimensional lattice.

authors.name: Tommaso Piacenti, Marcello Calvanese Strinati, Claudio Conti

papers.title: Stable, High-Charge, Laser-Driven VHEE Beams for Preclinical Applications
papers.summary: Laser-driven plasma accelerators (LPAs) are promising sources of very-high-energy-electron (VHEE) beams for medical applications, but increasing charge per pulse while maintaining pointing stability remains challenging. We demonstrate laser-accelerated beams with total charge per pulse reaching (559 $\pm$ 56) pC using an 80 TW laser system. The spectra have a dominant component at 40-60 MeV and a high-energy tail extending to approximately 200 MeV. Pointing jitter measured in air at the irradiation target plane reaches as low as 0.7 mrad. The beams were used for VHEE irradiation experiments involving a 10 mm region of interest through a 40 mm depth at 400 $\pm$ 20 mGy/pulse. Spectral reproducibility is quantified over fixed-setting shot sequences. Particle-in-cell simulations produce a peak-and-tail spectrum through acceleration in successive bubbles associated with a strongly modified plasma wake, providing a plausible mechanism for maintaining substantial accelerated charge despite strong beam loading. Dose-weighted time-of-flight calculations indicate an effective pulse dose rate of $10^{12}$ Gy/s and average dose rates of tens of Gy/min. These results establish an LPA operating regime relevant to preclinical VHEE irradiation.

authors.name: Chaitanya Varma, Camilla Giaccaglia, Julien Gautier, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, Pascal Rousseau, Alessandro Flacco

papers.title: TwinLight: A Multi-Timescale Physical-Layer-Aware T-API-Compliant Optical Domain Controller Digital Twin
papers.summary: We demonstrate TwinLight, an open-source optical-network digital twin acting as an optical domain controller. Its T-API REST and telemetry streaming interfaces expose a physical-layer engine that combines a GNPy steady-state baseline with four analytical transients.

authors.name: Carlos Natalino, Piotr Lechowicz, Renato Ambrosone, Enrico Miotto, Vittorio Curri, Paolo Monti

papers.title: Different exact-law formulations to calculate the energy cascade rate in magnetohydrodynamic turbulence with and without mean magnetic fields
papers.summary: At scales much larger than the ion inertial length and ion-gyroscale, space-plasma turbulence is often described within the framework of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Using high-resolution direct numerical simulations with $1024^3$ grid points, we perform the first systematic numerical comparison of three exact-law formulations for the total energy cascade in homogeneous, but not necessarily isotropic, MHD turbulence: the Yaglom-Monin (YM), Banerjee-Galtier (BG), and two-point correlator formulations. Despite directional variations, the angle-averaged energy transfer rates for all three formulations show excellent agreement for zero, moderate, and strong background magnetic fields. These results clearly suggest the usefulness of alternative BG and correlator formulations for estimating the energy cascade rates in turbulent space plasmas when the required spatial derivatives are accessible through multi-spacecraft measurements. We also argue that the isotropic Politano-Pouquet (PP) formulation does not provide a true directional transfer rate and therefore its application as a single-direction energy transfer rate estimator leads to inaccurate values, especially under anisotropic conditions. Decomposing the exact formulations into RMHD and non-RMHD contributions, we also show that the RMHD cascade rates cannot be obtained merely by increasing the strength of the mean magnetic field in incompressible magnetohydrodynamic turbulence. Finally, a term-by-term analysis of different formulations reveals how different nonlinear interaction channels coexist and collaborate with each other to maintain the same energy cascade rate across the inertial scales.

authors.name: Ramesh Sasmal, Supratik Banerjee

papers.title: Reconstructing intracell polarization with calibrated sapphire-window optics for collimated blue-light generation in a rubidium cell
papers.summary: We study the polarization dependence of collimated blue light (CBL) generated near 420~nm by resonant four-wave mixing in thermal rubidium vapor in a sapphire-window cell driven at 780 and 776~nm. Sapphire windows can transform the polarization of pump light before it reaches the vapor, complicating the interpretation of polarization-dependent nonlinear emission. We measured the 780-nm pump Stokes state at an external before-cell reference plane to calibrate the common HWP/QWP preparation optics and recorded 266 off-resonant external output Stokes states after the complete sapphire-window rubidium cell at 90, 100, and 110~$^\circ$C in two propagation orientations. Direct paired-wavelength measurements show a mean before-cell 780/776 separation of $4.29^\circ$ and temperature- and orientation-specific complete-cell rotations of $22.20^\circ$--$32.02^\circ$, with rms residuals of $4.83^\circ$--$12.87^\circ$. Using this calibrated co-prepared pump description, we analyzed 2574 measurements of total spectrally filtered 420-nm CBL intensity. Across the six temperature--orientation data sets, a complete nine-coefficient second-order response yielded cross-validated $R^2$ values of 0.636 to 0.828. These paired-wavelength measurements establish, for each temperature--orientation data set, a fixed relative Stokes-space map between the two co-prepared pump trajectories, with the residual of this mapping defining the experimental uncertainty of the correlated two-pump reduction used in the response model. Thus, the resulting framework combines a reconstructed vapor-entrance polarization coordinate with direct two-wavelength calibration of the assembled cell and provides a practical basis for polarization-controlled nonlinear-optical experiments in sapphire-window vapor cells.

authors.name: Sarah Ashby, David Bostanjyan, Mikayel Khanbekyan

papers.title: Increased Crystal Nucleation in the Glassy State of a Polymer/Water Mixture
papers.summary: Within classical nucleation theory, crystal nucleation requires sufficient supersaturation, but is suppressed at low temperatures due to reduced molecular mobility, leading to a maximum nucleation rate typically above the glass transition temperature $T_g$. Here, we experimentally show that this conventional picture breaks down in a biocompatible polymer poly(2-methoxyethyl acrylate)(PMEA)/water mixture. We find that the number of nuclei increases dramatically below $T_g$, with the effective nucleation rate exhibiting an unusual maximum at approximately $T_g-10$ K. Calorimetric experiments reveal a strong temperature-history dependence of cold crystallization of water in hydrated PMEA, which is explained by the observed nucleation behavior. We propose that the unusual enhancement of nucleation below $T_g$ provides a key mechanism linking high glass-forming ability and cold crystallization upon heating, thereby explaining the striking asymmetry in crystallization behavior between cooling and heating. Our findings suggest that a hidden nucleation-rate maximum below $T_g$ may also underlie cold crystallization in other glass-forming liquids.

authors.name: Mika Kobayashi, Shingo Kobayashi, Kazuyoshi Shiga, Hiroaki Yamada, Masaru Tanaka

papers.title: Interface-driven second harmonic generation in indium tin oxide/gold nanolayers: density and mass discontinuities matter
papers.summary: Second harmonic generation from transparent conductive oxides and metals is traditionally attributed to Coulomb, magnetic Lorentz, and convective sources. We show that this picture is incomplete in deeply subwavelength indium tin oxide/gold bilayers.
