papers.summary: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity. These results establish cavity-enhanced SHG spectroscopy as a valuable tool for studying Rydberg excitons in microcavities and provide a pathway towards exploiting optical nonlinearities in Rydberg exciton polariton systems.

authors.name: Horatio Q. X Wong, Krzysztof Sawicki, Madeleine Fisher, Stephen A. Lynch, Wolfgang Langbein, Sai Kiran Rajendran, Hamid Ohadi, Matthew P. A. Jones, Liam A. P. Gallagher

papers.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
papers.summary: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

authors.name: Usman Khan, Daniel Lopez, Venkat Aneesh Padmasola, Nirmal Dangi, Santosh Kumar, Yuping Huang

papers.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
papers.summary: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

authors.name: Joohyung Song, James I. Kwon, Edo Waks, Saikat Guha, Chaohan Cui

papers.title: Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data
papers.summary: Efficient encoding of data into quantum states remains a fundamental bottleneck in many quantum computing protocols, which would otherwise offer advantages over their classical counterparts. Here, we introduce deterministic and scalable amplitude-encoding methods with low two-qubit gate costs and tunable trade-offs between circuit depth and encoding fidelity. Our approaches require no amplitude amplification or mid-circuit measurement and are capable of encoding arbitrary complex data or queryable functions by using tensor-networks to go beyond what can be held in classical memory. Our principle contributions are two complementary algorithms for simplifying fully controlled multiplexer circuits to one- and two-qubit gates. In the first, we formally map the elimination of redundant gate controls to a Boolean logic minimization problem, while in the second we utilize a single ancilla qubit to map the multi-controlled rotation gates to a sequence of one- and two-qubit operations via the Walsh-Hadamard spectrum of the gate angles. We benchmark these methods across a broad range of function classes, characterizing their total depth in an all-to-all connectivity graph against system size and target fidelity. Hybridizing our methods gives up to orders of magnitude improvement in circuit depth at equivalent state fidelity compared to the default state-preparation method in the Qiskit package. We furthermore demonstrate our method on IQM hardware with a square lattice connectivity, finding excellent fidelity, even with minimal noise mitigation. By significantly reducing gate depth for encoding, this work enables the experimental execution of applications on current and near-term hardware which would otherwise be reduced to noise before the first calculation step, shortening the time horizon to robust quantum utility.

authors.name: Vittorio Pagni, Peter K. Schuhmacher, Michael Felderer, Michael Epping, Kevin Lively

papers.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
papers.summary: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

authors.name: Elias R. Koch, Albert Gallem\'i, Cl\`audia L\'opez, Finn Petersen, Julien Javaloyes, Svetlana V. Gurevich

papers.title: The effect of limb kinematics on the speed of a legged robot on granular media
papers.summary: Achieving effective locomotion on diverse terrestrial substrates can require subtle changes of limb kinematics. Biologically inspired legged robots (physical models of organisms) have shown impressive mobility on hard ground but suffer performance loss on unconsolidated granular materials like sand. Because comprehensive limb-ground interaction models are lacking, optimal gaits on complex yielding terrain have been determined empirically. To develop predictive models for legged devices and to provide hypotheses for biological locomotors, we systematically study the performance of SandBot, a small legged robot, on granular media as a function of gait parameters. High performance occurs only in a small region of parameter space. A previously introduced kinematic model of the robot combined with a new anisotropic granular penetration force law predicts the speed. Performance on granular media is maximized when gait parameters minimize body acceleration and limb interference, and utilize solidification features of granular media.

authors.name: Chen Li, Paul B. Umbanhowar, Haldun Komsuoglu, Daniel I. Goldman

papers.title: Controlled spin-torque driven domain wall motion using staggered magnetic nanowires
papers.summary: The growing demand for storage, due to big data applications, cannot be met by hard disk drives. Domain wall (DW) memory devices such as racetrack memory offer an alternative route to achieve high capacity storage. In DW memory, control of domain wall positions and their motion using spin-transfer torque are important challenges. In this paper, we demonstrate controlled domain wall motion using spin-transfer torque in staggered magnetic nanowires. The devices, fabricated using electron-beam lithography, were tested using a magneto-optical Kerr microscopy and electrical transport measurements. The depinning current, pinning potential and thermal stability were found to depend on the device dimensions of the staggering nanowires. Thus, the proposed staggering configuration helps to fine-tune the properties of domain wall devices for memory applications.

authors.name: H. Mohammed, S. Al Risi, T. L. Jin, J. Kosel, S. N. Piramanayagam, R. Sbiaa

papers.title: Universal Hamiltonian learning with rotational and basis equivariance
papers.summary: Deep learning has the potential to transform computational materials research by making electronic-structure calculations more efficient and scalable. The Hamiltonian matrix in the localized atomic-orbital basis is a promising target for deep-learning electronic structure, yet enforcing rotational equivariance can be computationally costly, and the matrix depends on the choice of basis set. Here we introduce DeepH-2, a physics-guided neural-network framework that reduces the computational cost of enforcing rotational equivariance through a local-coordinate formulation and incorporates basis equivariance by mapping a shared latent Hamiltonian to the target atomic-orbital basis. DeepH-2 achieves sub-meV test-set error on a diverse materials dataset and demonstrates transferability across material dimensions. These results highlight the value of encoding physics priors into deep-learning electronic structure models, and pave the way for developing the electronic-structure foundation models.

authors.name: Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Zechen Tang, Yang Li, Honggeng Tao, Yanzhen Wang, Zilong Yuan, Zezhou Chen, Wenhui Duan, Yong Xu

papers.title: Orientation-Resolved Scaling Relations for Mass Transport and Pressure Drop in Spacer-Filled Reverse Osmosis Channels
papers.summary: Feed spacers in spiral-wound reverse osmosis modules enhance mass transport but increase the flow resistance. Both effects depend on the spacer orientation, i.e. the flow attack angle $\alpha$, which has so far been characterized only at selected angles. This work derives continuous scaling relations for the Sherwood number ($Sh$) and the friction factor ($f$) as functions of $\alpha$ and the Reynolds number ($Re$) from high-resolution CFD simulations of two commercial overlapped spacers. The coefficients are obtained by an analytic least-square fit. Mass transport follows $Sh = 6.65(1 + 0.244 \sin(2\alpha)) (d_h/L)^{1/2} Re^{1/2}$ and the flow resistance follows $f = 11.63(1 + 0.19 \sin(2\alpha)) Re^{-1/2}$ for $Re > 80$. The relations hold for overlapped spacers with circular filaments at $Sc \approx 670$ and $Re$ up to about 210. The effects of $Re$ and $\alpha$ are separable with one set of coefficients for both spacer sizes. Rotating the spacer from $0^\circ$ to $45^\circ$ increases $Sh$ by 24\% and $f$ by 19\% at constant cross-flow velocity. Combined with an algebraic water flux model, the relations give closed-form estimates of water flux and pressure drop. For typical seawater and brackish water conditions, orientation increases the water flux by only 1\% to 2\% because concentration polarization is weak, but the gain grows with membrane permeability.

authors.name: Fynn Jerome Aschmoneit, Claus H\'elix-Nielsen

papers.title: Reconciling advective upwelling with diapycnal downwelling: A transient kinematic perspective on Munk's conundrum
papers.summary: Bottom-intensified turbulent fluxes observed near the seafloor drive abyssal densification and diapycnal downwelling through their vertical divergence. This appears paradoxical under steady stratification because dense bottom waters continuously enter from Antarctic sources. Motivated by evolving Indo-Pacific stratification, we use idealized simulations to examine abyssal overturning under transient and steady-state conditions. Using a kinematic rather than thermodynamic water-mass-transformation approach, we diagnose advective overturning, isopycnal volume tendency, and diapycnal transport in two cooling experiments with different mixing intensities, one warming experiment, and one quasi-equilibrium experiment. Advective upwelling occurs in all four, whereas diagnosed diapycnal transport varies in direction. In Type-I cooling, the isopycnal volume tendency exceeds advective overturning in magnitude, yielding downward diapycnal transport; in Type-II cooling, advective overturning exceeds the isopycnal volume tendency, yielding upward diapycnal transport. The warming and quasi-equilibrium experiments also exhibit upward diapycnal transport. These relationships persist qualitatively in potential-temperature coordinates. Type-I cooling also spontaneously produces an observationally documented bottom-intensified buoyancy-flux profile with an e-folding scale comparable to previous estimates. Thus, cooling alone does not determine diapycnal transport direction; it depends kinematically on the relative strengths of advective overturning and isopycnal volume tendency. Within this idealized framework, the results provide a transient kinematic interpretation of the interior-downwelling conundrum: abyssal waters can rise through the basin interior while undergoing diapycnal downwelling, without requiring an upslope return pathway within the bottom boundary layer.

authors.name: Lei Han

papers.title: On the Role of Color Temperature and Color Rendering Index of White-Light LEDs on the Theoretical Efficiency Limit of Indoor Photovoltaics
papers.summary: As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to grow, the demand for sustainable indoor power sources is increasing. Indoor photovoltaics (IPVs), which are currently in development, present a renewable solution but must be designed to match specific light sources to maximize efficiency. While previous studies have emphasized the role of white-light LED correlated color temperature (CCT) in determining IPV efficiency and optimum bandgap energy, the role of color rendering index (CRI) remains less understood. In this study, we employ detailed-balance calculations to assess the theoretical maximum efficiency and optimal bandgap energies of IPVs under commercial white-light LED illumination varying in both CCT (2200 K to 6500 K) and CRI (70, 80, and 90). Our results confirm that lower CCTs yield higher efficiencies and lower optimal bandgaps; however, contrary to prior assumptions that CRI has negligible impact on IPV material choice and performance, we demonstrate that commercial high-CRI LEDs, where said high CRI was achieved by extending the emission into the red, can necessitate the use of materials with significantly lower bandgap energies for optimum efficiency. We also evaluate the performance of various IPVs at fixed bandgaps, revealing that while optimal IPV performance is achieved with wide-bandgap materials under lower CRI lighting, mature technologies like silicon and CdTe can benefit from high-CRI illumination. These findings underscore the need to consider color characteristics beyond CCT when evaluating solar cells for indoor IoT applications.

authors.name: Aditi Sharma, Ian Yum, Alexander A. Guaman, Gavin A. Akmam, Jason A. R\"ohr

papers.title: Active learning and explicit electrostatics enable accurate modeling of electrolytes
papers.summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) combine near-ab initio accuracy with the computational efficiency of classical force fields, making them promising tools for modeling molecular liquids and electrolytes. Their predictive accuracy depends strongly on the diversity of the training set, while the explicit treatment of electrostatics is increasingly recognized as an important factor in improving their performance. In this work, we assess the impact of incorporating explicit electrostatics and environment-dependence of atomic charges by comparing short-ranged Moment Tensor Potentials (MTPs) with electrostatics-augmented MTPs, including fixed-charge and environment-dependent charge models. To this end, we employ D-optimality-based active learning (AL) to train short-ranged MTPs and extend the AL procedure, previously unavailable for long-range electrostatics-augmented MTPs, to these models, enabling largely automated generation of diverse training sets for pure ethylene carbonate (EC) and ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), their mixtures, and LiPF6 solutions. For EC, EMC, and their mixtures, electrostatics-augmented MTPs achieve accuracy comparable to or better than that of their short-ranged counterparts while requiring fewer machine-learned parameters. For LiPF6 solutions, however, a notable improvement in accuracy is achieved only with environment-dependent charges, which also enhance stability in large-scale molecular dynamics simulations, unlike the fixed-charge model. The resulting short-ranged MTPs and environment-dependent-charge models reproduce experimental densities with mean absolute deviations of 0.2-6% and ionic conductivities with deviations of 11-15%, while capturing the experimentally observed temperature dependence of conductivity.

authors.name: Olga Chalykh, Mikhail Polovinkin, Dmitry Korogod, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev

papers.title: Turning Old Anomalies Into New Evidence: Evidential Reconfiguration and Dark Matter in 1974
papers.summary: The 1974 papers by Ostriker et al. (1974) and Einasto et al. (1974) are regarded as pivotal in establishing the evidential case for dark matter, although both relied on already existing observational data. By what means did they transform known observational anomalies into evidential support for dark matter? I argue that this transformation arose through evidential reconfiguration: extended galactic halos supplied a physical connection between galaxy rotation curves and cluster mass discrepancies, expanding the context of assessment so that results previously investigated locally could constrain one another. The significance of this connection was assessed against differing cosmological commitments and unresolved local dynamical assumptions, which help explain both the emphases of the two papers and their reception. To explicate its contribution to confirmation, I draw on Myrvold's Bayesian account of unification and use a toy model in which taking one result into account changes the assessment of a shared halo parameter, thereby altering expectations about the other. Comparison with an uncoupled model makes the resulting support explicit, while variations of the model show why a shared parameter alone is insufficient: the contribution depends on the connecting assumptions and what competing models predict. The novelty relevant to the old-evidence problem thus lies in what familiar observations became jointly capable of supporting. This reconstruction assesses that support once the connection is specified, while leaving a full account of historical belief change open.

authors.name: Simon Allz\'en

papers.title: Jacobi's principle of stationary full action and its implications
papers.summary: The purpose of this article is to extend the applicability of the principle of stationary Jacobi action to non-conservative natural systems and to derive the equations of motion corresponding to this generalized principle. To this end, in addition to the well-known variation of the Jacobi action with respect to coordinates, we introduce an independent variation of time. Small variations in both coordinates and time are considered at points along the actual trajectory, subject to standard boundary conditions.

authors.name: Vitaliy Voytik

papers.title: Forced Reconnection in Voigt-Regularized MHD
papers.summary: Forced reconnection in Voigt-regularized MHD is investigated in the Hahm-Kulsrud-Taylor problem. It is shown that Voigt regularization introduces an early linear phase of reconnection that partially bypasses the ideal current sheet formation phase. Three distinct regimes of Rutherford-like island growth and saturation are elucidated, including the braking effects of regularization and viscosity. It is conjectured, with numerical justification, that the inclusion of drag in the momentum equation does not inhibit the relaxation to steady state in the long-time limit.

authors.name: Andrew Brown, Yi-Min Huang, Amitava Bhattacharjee

papers.title: Predictive Modeling for High Impact Active Learning Classrooms
papers.summary: Over the past several decades, a large body of research has shown that undergraduate science students learn more and more equitably in active learning classrooms; however, the term "active learning" lacks definition and little research has examined which types and combinations of associated strategies are most effective. This study uses data from 69 courses, 3 scientific disciplines, and 24 institutions to create a predictive model that maps classroom time spent on different activities to student conceptual learning. We find that a model using four classroom variables -- time spent on lecture, group worksheets, group clicker questions, and student questions -- can make predictions that account for 49\% of the variance in effect sizes, as measured by $R^2$. We identify one type of class that is predicted to have exceptional student learning gains (effect sizes greater than 2): those that spend 10-20% of class time on group worksheets, 20-40% of class time on group clicker questions, and 10\% or more of class time on student questions. We also find that classes that do not utilize group worksheets have learning outcomes comparable to fully lecture classes. These results provide testable recommendations for future controlled studies to investigate effective active learning implementation in undergraduate physics courses.

authors.name: Olive Ross, Meagan Sundstrom, N. G. Holmes

papers.title: A Low-Complexity 200 Mbit/s Full-Duplex Digital Link Over a Single Coaxial Cable for Laboratory Instrumentation
papers.summary: Modern full-duplex communication systems, such as Gigabit Ethernet, enable high data rates over challenging transmission media but require sophisticated circuitry and non-trivial digital interfaces. For laboratory instrumentation, the objective may instead be to achieve moderate-bandwidth full-duplex communication over short, well-controlled coaxial cables with minimal circuit and interface complexity. We present a low-complexity bidirectional digital interconnect that enables simultaneous transmission and reception of baseband logic signals over a single coaxial cable. The circuit combines a discrete passive resistive hybrid providing line termination and directional separation, a single logic gate as line driver, and a commercial differential receiver used as a comparator. No modulation, transformer coupling, adaptive calibration, or active analog or digital echo cancellation is required. The design target is full-duplex operation at 200 MBit/s over 10 m of standard RG-178 cable. An analytical treatment of the hybrid network determines the system parameter that maximizes the differential signal amplitude at the receiver, while circuit simulations predict the deterministic timing errors resulting from imperfect directional separation. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted deterministic jitter and show good agreement with the simulation results. For typical laboratory coaxial cables up to 10 m, the measured peak-to-peak edge timing error remains below 1.2 ns. A bidirectional transmission experiment with randomized data demonstrates a clearly open eye diagram. It was found that the transceiver inherently provides loopback functionality when the transmission line is left open. The proposed approach provides a simple, protocol-independent bidirectional physical link which may be useful in laboratory instrumentation where cable routing is constrained.

authors.name: Michael Wiebusch

papers.title: Nonlocal Energy Transfer Mechanism in Three-dimensional Quantum Turbulence
papers.summary: We investigate the kinetic energy cascade in zero-temperature quantum turbulence. Using simple theoretical arguments and unprecedented numerical simulations, we unveil an universal mechanism transferring energy directly from large to very small scales, thus bypassing the Kolmogorov-like local energy cascade and resulting in steepening of the energy spectra at scales larger than the typical distance between quantum vortices. This mechanism rests both on the vast separation of scales typical of superfluid helium-4 flows and on the alignment between quantum vortices and large-scale velocity gradients, in direct analogy with vortex stretching in classical turbulent flows.

authors.name: Elliot Bes, Guillaume Balarac, Juan Ignacio Polanco

papers.title: Solar Wind Classifications at Mars using Machine Learning Techniques
papers.summary: Understanding solar wind variability throughout the heliosphere is essential for fundamental space physics and future exploration of the Moon and Mars. The Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN) spacecraft has provided upstream solar wind measurements at Mars spanning Solar Cycles 24 and 25, enabling a statistical investigation of solar wind regimes at this heliocentric distance. In this work, we apply an unsupervised machine-learning framework combining Principal Component Analysis and K-Means clustering to a normalized, multi-dimensional solar wind dataset to identify recurrent solar wind regimes in a physically interpretable, data-driven manner. The resulting classification reveals distinct slow, fast, intermediate, and compressed solar wind regimes whose relative occurrence and temporal organization are strongly modulated by solar activity. This manuscript is part of the Heliophysics Summer School Machine Learning Special Collection.

authors.name: Silvia Ferro, Catherine E. Regan, Austin M. Smith, Alvin J. G. Angeles, Nicholas A. Gross, Farzad Kamalabadi, Marco Velli, Jasper S. Halekas

papers.title: Asynchronous Barter, Periodic Reconciliation: Evidence for a Scale-Free Commercial Network in the Indus Valley Civilization
papers.summary: The Harappan Civilization (c.\ 2600--1900 BCE) achieved extraordinary standardization across a vast region without clear evidence of centralized rule. We propose that it was a merchant commonwealth organized as a scale-free commercial network, with AP2PBS (Asynchronous Peer-to-Peer Barter Settlement) and the Unicorn Logistics Cartel (ULC) serving as inferential model labels for its coordinating institutions. Four lines of evidence support this interpretation. (1) \textbf{Statistical}: Unicorn $\alpha \approx 1.8$, offering stand with a power-law distribution with $\alpha \approx 2.3$--$2.6$, while seal counts at sites follow $\alpha \approx 1.55$; all fit heavy-tailed power-law better than exponential alternatives. (2) \textbf{Attribute correlations}: non-random associations between offering stands and anatomical attributes, including Cram\'er's V patterns across market tiers, are consistent with deliberate institutional design of visual confirmation bundles. (3) \textbf{Archaeological}: seal evolution, contextual distributions, and warehouse logistics support the operational requirements of long-distance asynchronous exchange. (4) \textbf{Architectural}: Mohenjo-daro's halls, bath, warehouses, and cart-compatible gridiron are consistent with infrastructure for commerce and coordination. Taken together, these findings are consistent with AP2PBS and ULC as models of how independent participants could standardize authentication, exchange value asynchronously, and coordinate across distance without a hierarchical state. Scale-free topology also offers a testable explanation for both Harappan longevity and its vulnerability to hub failure and cascading decline. The argument is inferential: the archaeological record does not directly identify AP2PBS or ULC by name, but its statistical, material, and architectural patterns are compatible with this decentralized commercial model.

authors.name: Mahesh T C

papers.title: Photoluminescence of resin-based solder flux residue under ultraviolet excitation from 120 nm to 310 nm
papers.summary: Nuisance photoluminescence is a potential source of background in particle detectors that use noble liquids as target material for galactic dark matter particles and neutrinos. Liquid argon and xenon scintillate in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) wavelength range in response to particle interactions. Photoluminescent materials that absorb these photons can cause unexpected signals that may impede event reconstruction in these detectors. We illuminated residue from different types of commercial solder flux commonly used in liquid xenon detectors with ultraviolet and VUV light and measured their photoluminescence spectra and intensities. We find that all tested flux residues photoluminesce in the visible spectral region when exposed to VUV light.

authors.name: Anna Hurhina, Marjolein Troost, Andreas Leonhardt, Tina R. Pollmann

papers.title: Electron Coherence and Dephasing by Quasi-Static Coulomb Fluctuations in Classical Ionic Media
papers.summary: We develop a microscopic theory of quantum-particle propagation through quasi-static electrostatic fluctuations of a classical one-component plasma. The RPA potential is Gaussian but has an unscreened $1/r$ correlation tail, which makes the disorder-averaged retarded Green function infrared sensitive. Its eikonal attenuation scale is $\ell_{\rm w}=k^2/G$ for $g=G/k^3\ll1$, with the formal strong-saddle asymptote $\ell_{\rm s}=(4\sqrt[3]{2}/3)G^{-1/3}$ for $g\gg1$. For a slab of thickness $d$, the retarded--advanced mutual-coherence kernel is infrared finite: the coherence decays algebraically for $\lambda_D\ll\rho\ll d$ and saturates at larger transverse separation. Thus equilibrium ionic-density fluctuations constitute a distinct quasi-static dephasing channel with a nonexponential coherence law. A finite coherence radius exists only when the saturation threshold is crossed. Relativistic paraxial reduction gives $a_{\rm rel}=1/(\hbar v)$ and the finite high-energy limit $1/(\hbar c)$. The ionic contribution is very small at conventional TEM energies for a $100\,\mathrm{nm}$ water-like layer. Within the quasi-static model it grows for thicker samples and lower-energy electrons, while sub-keV transmission through liquid water is strongly limited by inelastic scattering.

authors.name: Yury A. Budkov

papers.title: Effective skyrmion number for mixed polarization states of light
papers.summary: Polarization skyrmions are usually characterized through a unit Stokes vector field, which defines a map from the transverse plane to the Poincar\'e (Bloch) sphere and allows one to assign a skyrmion number under appropriate boundary conditions. This description assumes complete polarization. In many optical situations, however, the local polarization state is partially polarized and is therefore described by a spectral polarization matrix rather than by a single Jones vector. We formulate a density-matrix-based effective extension of the skyrmion-number construction for statistically stationary, quasi-monochromatic paraxial fields in terms of the normalized spectral polarization matrix. Its eigenvectors define two orthogonal polarization eigenstates, corresponding to antipodal points on the sphere, while the eigenvalue imbalance is fixed by the local degree of polarization (DoP) $P(\mathbf r)$. Averaging the opposite skyrmion-density contributions of these two eigenpolarizations leads to an effective skyrmion number in which the usual pure-state density is weighted by $P(\mathbf r)$. The resulting quantity reduces to the conventional skyrmion number for fully polarized fields and assigns zero weight to locally unpolarized regions. In general, it is not an integer topological invariant; rather, it is an integrated effective measure, constructed from local Stokes parameters, which can be interpreted geometrically as a DoP-weighted signed solid-angle integral of the polarization eigentexture on the Poincar\'e sphere. We illustrate the construction with a regular analytic family of polarization eigentextures with winding order $m$ and fixed radial DoP profiles, showing how the effective number depends jointly on the winding order and on the spatial overlap between the DoP and the skyrmion density.

authors.name: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

papers.title: A phase space electronic structure theory beyond Born-Oppenheimer: Geometric forces and Moody-Shapere-Wilczek revisited
papers.summary: We revisit the three-body problem in quantum mechanics in two and three dimensions, generating both exact eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Hamiltonian and a series of approximate solutions as calculated with a variety of different schemes to separate heavy ("nuclear") and light ("electronic") particles. We show that, with minimal extra cost, one can go beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation by performing electronic structure calculations parameterized by both the nuclear position (${\mathbf X})$ and the nuclear momentum ($\mathbf{P}$), a so-called phase space theory of electronic structure. In particular, we demonstrate that such phase space electronic structure calculations correctly incorporate the non-inertial Coriolis and centrifugal forces felt by electrons in a moving nuclear frame, thus leading to far more accurate eigenenergies and electronic angular momenta than has been possible before. We also demonstrate that our approach naturally incorporates and generalizes the Moody-Shapere-Wilczek magnetic monopole for the non-abelian Berry curvature (now allowing for vibrational motion rather than a diatomic of fixed length). We argue that the resulting approach should be extremely useful for propagating dynamics where angular momentum flows between nuclei and electrons; in particular, if extended to include spin degrees of freedom, the present approach will offer a practical means to study chiral induced spin selectivity through the lens of chiral phonons and coupled nuclear-electronic motion.

authors.name: Mansi Bhati, D. Vale Cofer-Shabica, Jonathan I. Rawlinson, Robert G. Littlejohn, Joseph Subotnik, Nadine C. Bradbury

papers.title: A toy model for understanding the space-point resolution of silicon pixel detectors with digital readout
papers.summary: Silicon pixel detectors are widely used in high-energy physics experiments as tracking detectors close to the primary interaction vertex. They provide excellent space-point resolution together with fast electronic readout. Many of them employ only digital (binary) readout which makes the applicability of centre-of-gravity algorithms less obvious. Charge sharing between neighboring pixels improves the resolution beyond the single-pixel limit, but in practice there is a lack of quantitative understanding of the achievable gains. This work provides a simplified analytical and numerical model with which the maximum improvement achievable through charge sharing is quantified for both one and two-dimensional pixel geometries. A phenomenological parameterisation of the resolution as a function of the average cluster size is derived and compared to experimental data from several detector technologies.

authors.name: Marianna Mazzilli, Alexander Kalweit

papers.title: Influence of DFT Functionals on Low-Energy Electron Scattering Cross Sections of Nitric Oxide
papers.summary: Nitric oxide (NO) is important in biological, atmospheric, plasma, industrial, and astrophysical environments, where reliable electron-collision data support modelling charged-particle interactions with matter. Its well-known experimental properties make it suitable for assessing how the target electronic-structure description affects low-energy electron scattering calculations. In this work, NO properties were evaluated using B3LYP, M06-2X, PBE0, and $\omega$B97X-D3, with basis sets ranging from minimal to quadruple-zeta quality. Bond length, dipole moment, ionisation potential, and polarisability were compared with experiment to assess the sensitivity of the target description to the functional and basis set. The aug-cc-pVQZ basis set was then used to generate target models for ab initio R-matrix calculations over 0.1--20 eV. The total cross sections show low-energy resonance features, with the strongest functional dependence around the broad peak near 0.8--1.0 eV. A sharper, higher-energy structure is also observed below 2 eV, shifting from 1.74 to 1.82 eV depending on the functional. Differential cross sections show modest functional sensitivity, with more noticeable angular differences at 7.5 and 10 eV. These results show that the DFT functional and basis set affect the target properties, with the resulting target description influencing low-energy electron-scattering observables of NO. The comparison supports $\omega$B97X-D3/aug-cc-pVTZ geometry optimisation followed by aug-cc-pVQZ target-property calculations as a practical protocol for R-matrix modelling of NO.

authors.name: Ashutosh Yadav, Felipe Fantuzzi, Nigel J. Mason, Bobby Antony

papers.title: Duty-cycle modulation of the self-sustaining process by spanwise wall oscillation
papers.summary: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent channel flow at Re_tau,0 = 200 examine the modulation of the near-wall self-sustaining process under sinusoidal and shape-optimised spanwise wall oscillation, with the same peak wall velocity and oscillation period. At a period close to the reported sinusoidal optimum for the prescribed peak velocity, the shape-optimised waveform gives a relative increase of approximately 6% in gross drag reduction over the sinusoidal signal, at a higher actuation cost; it is therefore used as a probe of the physical mechanisms underlying drag reduction. Phase-resolved stresses, vorticity variances and component-enstrophy budgets quantify the concurrent action of two tilting paths for the wall-normal vorticity of the near-wall streaks: towards the streamwise direction by the mean shear, and towards the spanwise direction by the Stokes strain. The magnitude of the Stokes strain orders the two paths: the spanwise path prevails over most of the cycle, and the streamwise path only while the strain is small, around its change of sign. Within 5 <= y+ <= 12, under the interval criterion q = 0.5, the shape-optimised waveform holds the strain at a nearly constant level for about 2/3 of the cycle, against 1/3 for the sinusoidal waveform, and so approximately halves the duration of the Reversal interval. The mean-shear production of streamwise enstrophy occurs mainly during Reversal: for the shape-optimised waveform its conditional rate is higher in every interval, whereas its time average is 23% lower, as Reversal is shorter. The lift-up production of wall-normal enstrophy is lower at every sampled phase. These observations support a duty-cycle description of the near-wall activity, in which the duration of each interval and the production rate within it are distinguished.

authors.name: Lionel Agostini

papers.title: U3DWind: A Low Altitude Wind Field Dataset and Benchmark for Urban Air Mobility
papers.summary: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) requires reliable assessment of low-altitude wind hazards, because winds, gusts, and building-induced turbulence have been recognized as critical factors affecting vehicle stability, route feasibility, vertiport siting, and airspace management. While wind-tunnel experiments, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), multiscale downscaling, reduced-order models, and UAV planning datasets have advanced wind-aware analysis, public resources for data-driven, city-scale UAM planning remain limited in geographic coverage, scenario diversity, vertical extent, building realism, and task-oriented benchmarking. To address this gap, we introduce U3DWind, a building-resolved low-altitude wind-field dataset generated using our GPU-accelerated Lattice Boltzmann Method--Large-Eddy Simulation (LBM-LES) framework for rapid urban flow simulation. U3DWind covers five megacities in China: Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong. It contains 720 simulations, with 16 inflow directions, three reference wind speeds, and three seasonal atmospheric scenarios (annual, summer, and winter) for each city. At a 10 m grid resolution, the dataset provides three-dimensional three-component (3D3C) velocity, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), flow density, and fluid--solid masks. To support operationally relevant evaluation, we further define five baseline tasks: wind-field prediction, sparse-sensor wind-field reconstruction, site wind-exposure ranking, airworthiness wind-compliance risk scoring, and noise propagation modeling. As a multi-city, building-resolved 3D urban wind-field dataset, U3DWind enables systematic evaluation of wind-induced impacts in low-altitude traffic scenarios and provides an open benchmark for urban airspace management and data-driven high-fidelity urban flow simulation.

authors.name: Shixiong Zhou, Huanxia Wei, Chao Xia, Yingying Xing, Changmin Jiang, Hai Yang, Shuai Jia

papers.title: A Thermodynamically Consistent Manifold Model for Premixed Deflagrations & Detonations
papers.summary: Accurate modeling of compressible premixed flames, encompassing both deflagrations and detonations, remains a significant challenge for predictive Large Eddy Simulation (LES) due to the strong coupling between the thermochemical state and the local thermodynamic state. This work presents a manifold-based turbulent combustion model that ensures a fully consistent thermodynamic state between model and flow solver through an iterative procedure. The framework reproduces critical quantities including temperature, radical species, and source term profiles, addressing limitations of existing approaches that rely on low-Mach perturbations or tabulated ZND detonations without thermodynamic consistency. Validation is performed against one-dimensional and high-fidelity RDE-like data, demonstrating that the thermodynamically consistent model consistently outperforms existing approaches across a broad range of compressible flame regimes - including both deflagration and detonation. The results highlight the importance of fully accounting for the thermodynamic state to achieve accurate predictions. By capturing both deflagrative and detonative behavior within a single framework, the model provides a unified, versatile tool for LES of high-speed reacting flows and offers a foundation for future studies of compressible reacting flows, including applications to rotating detonation engines and other supersonic combustion systems.

authors.name: John B. Boerchers, Laura T. Thompson, Matthew X. Yao, Michael E. Mueller

papers.title: Emergent Non-Equilibrium Emission Profiles via Luminescent Angle Restriction for Photovoltaic Energy Conversion
papers.summary: The detailed-balance method determines photovoltaic conversion efficiencies by relating non-equilibrium converter operation to an equilibrium reference state. Conventionally, the angular and spectral radiative channels are assumed to be defined by the equilibrium absorptivity and emissivity, with the photon chemical potential setting their occupation. The spatial distribution of emission must also be considered when radiative energy is redistributed within a complex nanophotonic converter architecture. Here we analyze this redistribution with a proposed luminescent angle restrictor, in which a flat-plate photovoltaic absorber is coupled to an overlayer with vertically aligned nanorods. The nanorod layer is nearly transparent to near-normal sunlight, while oblique photovoltaic luminescence can be absorbed, re-emitted, and partially returned to the absorber. To calculate the operating emission profile, we develop a Markov-chain transport model with an absorbing-chain formulation that enforces microscopic reversibility for local optical transitions while determining the spatially distributed steady-state emission rates. The model recovers the flat-plate detailed-balance limit and predicts voltage-dependent external emission profiles from the coupled architecture. Under idealized conditions, this non-equilibrium angular redistribution increases conversion efficiency relative to the conventional flat-plate reference. We further evaluate nanorod photoluminescence quantum yield, angular restriction, orientational disorder, and Auger recombination to identify practical constraints on the proposed architecture. These results show how detailed-balance limits for photovoltaic structures can depend on internal radiative energy redistribution and the resulting non-equilibrium emission profile, beyond what can be inferred from the macroscopic equilibrium optical response alone.

authors.name: Jonathan McTague (Department of Chemistry, University of California, Irvine), Rivi Ratnaweera (Department of Chemistry, Texas A&M University), Matthew Sheldon (Department of Chemistry, University of California, Irvine, Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of California, Irvine)

papers.title: Full 3D Maxwell solver for Inertial Electrostatic Confinement devices
papers.summary: Results of a full 3D electromagnetic plasma fusion simulator are presented. It will enable investigations into the influence of structured electromagnetic potentials, anomalous magnetic moments, or charge cluster structures on the fusion yield. The simulator calculates fusion yields similar to those found in real world fusors. In addition, the ion energy and density are accurately simulated. Given that the ion properties arise from a full Maxwell solver there is ample evidence that this part of the simulation is accurate. Concluded with a recommendation for continued research.

authors.name: Victor-Otto de Haan

papers.title: Undulating Diamond Photonic Crystal in the Royal Jewel Butterfly: Circumventing Refractive Index Limits to Defy Iridescence
papers.summary: The modest refractive-indices of biomolecules place fundamental constraints on the optical performance of natural photonic organisms. To overcome this limitation, organisms reshape basic optical structures into hierarchical architectures, exhibiting performance rivals that of high-index materials. Here we show how the Royal Jewel butterfly (Hypochrysops polycletus) employs such a strategy to circumvent the low refractive-index of chitin to achieve an unusual combination of intense structural colouration and remarkably weak angular dependence. A single-diamond photonic crystal, which was hailed as the 'holy grail' and documented only in beetles and weevils, has now been discovered in the butterfly. It deforms into a hierarchically undulated superstructure guided by basal lamina and correlated with quasi-twinning boundaries with mirror symmetry. The scale surface is thus fully terminated by inclined {111} facets essential for fundamental bandgap, producing bright specular Bragg reflection at intermediate to high angles and low-angle radiation enabled by simultaneously coupling localised resonances populated through anisotropic Bloch transport, thereby transforming an otherwise strongly angle-dependent photonic crystal into a vivid, angle-robust optical structure. Following this optical concept, an artificially angle-insensitive optical prototype was fabricated through two-photon polymerisation, validating the mechanism as a transferable design principle at the intersection of fundamental nanophotonics and bio-inspired engineering.

authors.name: Yuanbo Li, Shuo Huang, Xi Wang, Congcong Cui, Hao Chen, Yuqin Xiong, Wang Zhang, Matthias Saba, Xueyan Feng, Bo Chen, Yuanyuan Cao, Lu Han

papers.title: Hidden transverse-flow topology in partially coherent structured light
papers.summary: Partial coherence is commonly viewed as a mechanism that reduces contrast or smooths intensity structure. Here we show that it can also encode hidden transverse-flow topology. Starting from the cross-spectral density, we formulate a generalized transverse flux, an effective velocity field, and the associated flux trajectories for quasi-monochromatic partially coherent paraxial beams. This construction converts two-point correlation phases into local transport information and reduces to the usual coherent energy-flow picture in the single-mode limit. Because the generalized flux is obtained through a local differential operation on the cross-spectral density, the proposed trajectories are, in principle, reconstructible from sufficiently resolved phase-sensitive measurements of the complex second-order coherence function, subject to the regularization required by numerical differentiation. Two analytical beam families expose this hidden topology. In twisted Gaussian Schell-model beams, a Gaussian intensity hides a distributed rotational flow with nonzero vorticity. In Laguerre-Christoffel-Darboux beams, sources with identical intensity profiles can have different flux topology, producing either spiral or purely radial trajectories. Thus, intensity and coherence magnitude do not exhaust the physical information contained in the cross-spectral density: partial coherence can reorganize the hidden topology of transverse optical transport.

authors.name: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

papers.title: Giant strongly biconnected components of directed networks: a generating function approach
papers.summary: Strongly connected components (SCCs) characterize modular structure in directed networks but are fragile to single node failures. We study strongly biconnected components (SBCs), which are the set of nodes in which every node pair remains mutually reachable after the removal of any single node, as a more robust notion of connectivity. Using a generating function formalism, we derive the size of the giant SBC and analyze its percolation behavior under random node and link removal. We show that the giant SBC emerges at the same threshold as the giant SCC but grows more slowly, consistent with previous findings for undirected networks. We also applied our theoretical framework to real-world biological networks including gene regulatory networks and neural connectome. Our framework provides insight into the interplay between connectivity, redundancy, and robustness in complex directed systems.

authors.name: Minsoo Yang, Reinhard Laubenbacher, Byungjoon Min

papers.title: Two preregistered datasets on production-type labelling in the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform: multi-fuel reporting, register vintages, persistent misclassification, and cross-product consistency
papers.summary: The ENTSO-E Transparency Platform is the single mandated publication point for European electricity market data, and three of its data items carry a production-type label. Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013 Article 16(1)(a) requires actual generation output per generation unit but does not mention production type; the label on that item is ENTSO-E's own addition through the schema, and Article 5(d) delegates the classification of production types to a Manual of Procedures. This data descriptor documents two preregistered datasets that measure what that classification does in practice, along four axes: simultaneous multi-fuel reporting, type change between capacity-register vintages, persistent misclassification without type change, and cross-product consistency between the per-unit and the aggregated series. Criteria were locked and checksummed before measurement, thresholds are derived from measured noise rather than chosen, and what did not survive is recorded: six claims are withdrawn, three of them from published versions of the datasets themselves. Across 2191 documents covering 199 generation units in three bidding zones where biomass co-firing is documented in a dated primary source, no unit carries two production types in the same document. One practical warning applies to every user of the hourly series: all of it carries curveType A03, a step curve in which a missing position means the previous value holds rather than that data are absent. A parser that sums only the points listed under-reports energy unevenly, by 22.6 percent for one Finnish unit in 2021.

authors.name: Eirik Botten Nicolaysen (EcoDeco AS)

papers.title: The NewMag crystal-field code for f-element systems: Implementation for extended active spaces, second-order correlated energies, and generalisation to fn configurations
papers.summary: We report a massive update of the NewMag program, which enables to extract Stevens crystal-field parameters (CFPs) after relativistic and multiconfigurational calculations are performed. The code can now post-treat ORCA and OpenMolcas outputs that contain state-average complete active space self-consistend field (SA-CASSCF) calculations with minimal or extended active spaces, second-order NEVPT2 or CASPT2 calculations, and spin-orbit configuration interaction (SOCI) calculations. Stevens parameters are extracted following the original Stevens convention with the so-called "extended" parameters. Rotation invariant indicators are also computed, after applying a correction of the parameter values to ensure normalization, following Rudowicz. At the SOCI level, the spin-orbit coupling (SOC) constant is also extracted within a spherical approximation of the SOC operator. For all the reference calculation levels, the model spectrum is reconstructed, allowing a direct assessment of its quality. The reported implementation is successfully applicable to f-element systems with a non-void, non-half-filled/empty or non-full f shell, that is for f^n configurations with n != 0, != 7 and != 14. Similarities and differences with the SINGLE_ANISO and AILFT codes are discussed. With selected examples, we showcase the interest of determining CFPs in f-element systems to understand their magnetic and optical properties in general, and more specifically the added value of NewMag. Finally, application of this approach to d-element systems is discussed, to reveal when it readily and successfully applies and when it may fail in reproducing satisfactorily the ab initio energies.

authors.name: Gwenha\"el Duplaix-Rata, Dumitru-Claudiu Sergentu, Boris Le Guennic, R\'emi Maurice

papers.title: Implementation and verification of a new free boundary module for Resistive Wall Modes simulations with the nonlinear 3D full MHD code SpeCyl
papers.summary: Self-consistent numerical simulations of free boundary instabilities, such as resistive wall modes (RWMs) and external kink modes, require special attention given their relevance on the path towards magnetic fusion based nuclear reactors. In this work, a new implementation and a verification benchmark are presented for the nonlinear three-dimensional (3D) full magneto-hydrodynamics (MHD) code SpeCyl, which self-consistently combines a free flow 3D treatment for the edge plasma velocity with double resistive wall thin shell magnetic boundary conditions, capable of capturing the essential features of common setups in experimental devices. Two coaxial resistive shells surround the plasma. Vacuum conditions are assumed between and outside the resistive shells, whose relative positions and time constants can be varied on purpose. The implementation is extensively verified against Shafranov's analytic theory, valid for a circular cross section large aspect ratio tokamak and assuming a flat current profile. The correctness of newly implemented Boundary Conditions (BCs) is confirmed by the good agreement obtained for the linear growth rates of (m=2,n=1) RWM and external kink, over a wide range of wall positions, resistive shell time constants, and for different initial reference equilibria. The (m=2,n=1) RWM growth rates are also benchmarked against previous different RWMs modelling and successful validation studies for RFX-mod tokamak plasmas. The new BCs make SpeCyl a flexible and robust tool to investigate free boundary MHD modes in large aspect ratio magnetic confinement configurations, such as those achieved with the RFX-mod machine and expected in RFX-mod2.

authors.name: Francesco Galeazzi, Daniele Bonfiglio, Luca Spinicci, Susanna Cappello

papers.title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
papers.summary: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.

authors.name: Angelina Liu, Mengqiu Cao, Sen Pei, Qing Yao

papers.title: Stabilization of counter propagating currents by energy conservation in collisions
papers.summary: Current filamentation generates magnetic fields and shapes electron transport in dense plasmas, where collisions can either suppress or enhance its growth. Here we show that conserving electron kinetic energy in a collisional model can change both the dominant instability and its characteristic wavelength. We develop a linear kinetic theory for drifting, anisotropic electron populations with a relaxation operator that conserves particle number and laboratory-frame kinetic energy while allowing momentum transfer to a stationary ion background. For counterstreaming currents, energy conservation maintains the stabilizing influence of charge separation over a broader range of collision frequencies than a model conserving particle number alone. At intermediate collision rates, the resulting suppression of transverse filamentation allows a nearly aperiodic oblique mode to dominate, reducing the maximum growth rate and shifting the wavelength of the fastest-growing perturbation. Two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations support predicted growth rates of up to more than a magnitude lower than expected without energy conserving collision.

authors.name: Thomas Kluge, Jannis Schulz, Arthur Hirsch-Passicos, Pawel Ordyna, Ulrich Schramm

papers.title: Observation of pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
papers.summary: Photonic pseudospins enable selective excitation and routing of light, but perturbations that mix opposite pseudospins can induce backscattering in helical edge channels. Here, we experimentally demonstrate pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals, combining pseudospin selectivity with nonreciprocal unidirectional propagation. By jointly engineering lattice deformation and magnetic bias, we control dipolar-quadrupolar band inversions and construct interfaces supporting pseudospin-selective chiral channels. Microwave near-field and transmission measurements reveal a single chiral edge branch that is selectively excited by only one source handedness and exhibits pronounced nonreciprocal transport. Extending this mechanism to multidomain structures, we combine two pseudospin channels into a common waveguide, separate them into distinct outputs, and route them through intersecting interfaces. These configurations realize a nonreciprocal photonic pseudospin multiplexer and demultiplexer, together with a waveguide crossing exhibiting average measured crosstalk of -14.1 and -15.8 dB for its two input channels. Our results present an experimental route to integrating pseudospin-selective channel control with chiral edge transport, providing a foundation for nonreciprocal photonic networks that use pseudospin to organize and route multiple wave channels.

authors.name: Chengle Fan, Kaizhou Shi, Xiang Xi, Zhen Gao

papers.title: Correlated non-perturbative electron dynamics with quantum trajectories
papers.summary: An approach to electron correlation effects in atoms that uses quantum trajectories is presented. A comparison with the exact quantum mechanical results for 1D Helium atom shows that the major features of the correlated ground state distribution and of the strong field ionization dynamics are reproduced with quantum trajectories. The intra-atomic resonant transitions are described accurately by a trajectory ensemble. The present approach reduces significantly the computational time and it can be used for both bound and ionizing electrons.

authors.name: Ivan P. Christov

papers.title: Quantum trajectory perspective of atom-field interaction in attosecond time scale
papers.summary: Here the ionization and high harmonic generation in Hydrogen and Helium by using quantum (hydrodynamic) trajectories is analyzed theoretically. The quantum trajectories allow a self-contained treatment of the electron exchange and correlation effects without introducing ad hoc potentials into the Schrodinger equation. Our approach predicts the correct high harmonic spectra and the attosecond pulses generated by the Helium atom beyond the single active electron approximation. It can be used to study complex multi-electron systems and their interaction with laser field of both high and low intensity.

authors.name: Ivan P. Christov

papers.title: Time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo: preparation of the ground state
papers.summary: We study one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) Helium atoms using a new time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo (TDQMC) method. The TDQMC method employs random walkers, with a separate guiding wave attached to each walker. The ground state is calculated by a self-consistent solution of complex-time Schroedinger equations for the guiding waves and of equations for the velocity fields of the walkers. Our results show that the many-body wavefunction and the ground state energy of the model atoms are very close to those predicted by the standard diffusion quantum Monte Carlo method. The obtained ground state can further be used to examine correlated time-dependent processes which include, for example, interaction of atoms and molecules with external electromagnetic fields.

authors.name: I. P. Christov

papers.title: Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulations of Monster Shocks in Neutron Star Magnetospheres
papers.summary: Waves launched from the neutron star surface or inner magnetosphere propagate through the magnetosphere as small perturbations, but can grow relative to the background magnetic field and steepen into ``monster shocks'' -- ultra-relativistic magnetized shocks which can power high-energy emission. Such shocks can develop around isolated magnetars, merging binaries, and collapsing neutron stars. They occur in magnetically dominated plasma and are described by relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). We present global relativistic MHD simulations of monster shocks in unperturbed and perturbed (``wrinkled'') backgrounds with a global dipolar geometry. Our simulations confirm analytical predictions for equatorial shocks and provide new insight into the behavior of oblique shocks off the equator. Simulations where the shock is formed through Alfv\'{e}n mode to fast mode conversion are also presented, demonstrating the generic nature of the monster shock mechanism. We explore how the presence of additional modes in the magnetosphere modifies the shock behavior. Modes of comparable amplitude can fragment the shock front, substantially reduce the magnetization, produce localized enhancements in the Lorentz factor relative to an unperturbed dipole background, and intermittently generate additional shocks along a line of sight.

authors.name: Michael P. Grehan, Bart Ripperda, Andrei M. Beloborodov, Christopher Thompson, Elias R. Most

papers.title: The Baryon Budget of Galaxies across the First Billion Years
papers.summary: We provide a complete census of the baryons in early galaxies to investigate the phases in which gas and stars reside, their corresponding budgets, depletion times, and stellar return fraction as a function of redshift and stellar age. We use the ColdSIM hydrodynamical time-dependent non-equilibrium chemistry simulations and perform a detailed analysis of the cold, warm, hot, and stellar phases for both bound structures (galaxies/CGM) and the diffuse IGM. We investigate in depth the cold HI and H2 components, explicitly computed in our simulations, and their relations with host mass, SFR, metallicity and depletion times. We also provide observational insights and discuss the implications for stellar mass functions, PopIII star formation and changes in the IMF. We find that cosmic gas prior to reionisation is mostly cold, while at later epochs the warm phase becomes dominant due to enhanced star formation activity and increasing UV reionising radiation. Stellar return fractions at these times are ~0.15-0.20, a factor of two lower than the values usually adopted. Cold, warm, and hot gas masses as well as HI and H2 components show increasing trends with mass and SFR, while depletion times decrease down to 0.01-0.1 Gyr with a weak metallicity dependence. The resulting star formation efficiency remains at the level of a few per cent and gas-to-star fractions decline with mass, influenced by local feedback and environment. Our findings are consistent with ALMA, VLA and IRAM surveys at later epochs, including ALFALFA, xCOLDGASS, GASS, xGASS, EDGE-CALIFA, PHIBBS, and ASPECS. Gas phases are quantitatively related to the underlying stellar populations and can be used to infer unknown quantities. In the appendix we provide fit functions describing the trends of the stellar return fraction, the main sequence, phase mass relations, gas-to-star fractions and depletion times.

authors.name: Umberto Maio, C\'eline P\'eroux

papers.title: Operational impact of quantum resources in chemical dynamics
papers.summary: Quantum coherence and other non-classical features are widely discussed in chemical dynamics, yet it remains difficult to quantify when such resources are operationally relevant for a given process and observable. While quantum resource theories provide a comprehensive framework for comparing free and resourceful settings, existing approaches typically rely on resource monotones or on performance bounds under free operations, and do not directly quantify the maximal influence a chosen resource can exert on a fixed chemical dynamics. Here, we introduce task specific, process level quantifiers that upper bound the largest change a quantum resource can induce in a target figure of merit. Central is a resource impact functional $\mathcal{C}_M(\Lambda)$, defined by comparing a state with its paired resource-free counterpart under the same quantum channel $\Lambda$, which admits an operational interpretation in binary hypothesis testing. We derive variation and time bounds that constrain how rapidly a resource can modify a target signal, providing resource-aware analogues of quantum speed limits. Moreover, we show that open system dynamics can be decomposed into free and resourceful components such that only the resourceful component contributes to $\mathcal{C}_M(\Lambda)$, thereby isolating the parts of a generator responsible for resource-induced changes in the observable. We illustrate the framework exemplary for energy transfer in a donor-acceptor dimer in two analytically solvable regimes. Our results provide a general toolbox for diagnosing and benchmarking quantum resource effects in molecular processes.

authors.name: Julia Liebert, Gregory D. Scholes

papers.title: Operational bounds and diagnostics for coherence in energy transfer
papers.summary: Excitation energy transfer in light-harvesting aggregates is highly efficient, yet whether quantum coherence plays an operational role in transport remains debated. A central challenge is that coherence is usually inferred from spectroscopic signatures, whereas transport performance is assessed through specific observables and depends on both the open system dynamics and the initial state preparation. Here we develop a resource theoretic approach that quantifies the maximum change that initial site-basis coherence can induce in a chosen readout under fixed reduced dynamics. The central quantity is the resource impact functional, which yields state independent, readout specific bounds on coherence-induced changes in signals and transport figures of merit. We apply the framework to two models. For a donor-acceptor dimer, we analyse coherence sensitivity across coupling and bath-timescale regimes and bound trapping efficiency and average transfer time in terms of the impact functional. For a multi-site chain with terminal trapping, we derive rigorous criteria that distinguish population placement from sensitivity to initial state site-basis coherence. These include upper bounds on the largest advantage over incoherent preparations, necessary delocalization requirements for achieving a prescribed improvement, and a simple pairwise sufficient condition that can be checked from local information. For quasi-local reduced dynamics, we further obtain a Lieb-Robinson-type bound that constrains when coherence prepared in a distant region can influence a localized readout at finite times. Together, these results provide operational diagnostics and rigorous bounds for benchmarking coherence effects and for identifying regimes in which they are necessarily negligible or potentially relevant in excitonic transport models.

authors.name: Julia Liebert, Gregory D. Scholes

papers.title: Feedback percolation on complex networks
papers.summary: Traditional percolation theory assumes static microscopic rules, limiting its ability to describe real-world complex systems where macroscopic order actively regulates local interactions. Here, we introduce feedback percolation, an unified framework that dynamically couples the microscopic activation probability to the macroscopic size of the giant component. We show that this simple feedback mechanism produces a rich variety of behaviors both analytically and numerically. Depending on the feedback functions, the system exhibits explosive discontinuous jumps, hybrid transitions, limit-cycle oscillations, and routes to chaos, absent in classical percolation. Our findings establish that macroscopic feedback provides a unifying physical mechanism for phenomena ranging from self-regulating oscillations to systemic infrastructure collapse.

authors.name: Hoseung Jang, Ginestra Bianconi, Byungjoon Min

papers.title: Kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and Landau fluid closure in relativity
papers.summary: Diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. In such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. Modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations. We present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic Landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. Unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates Landau damping in a fluid closure. The model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.

authors.name: Abhishek Hegade K. R., James M. Stone

papers.title: Predicting accurate solid-state thermodynamics is easier than you think
papers.summary: Materials underpin modern technologies, from energy harvesting, storage, and conversion to information and communication technologies. Their functionality is often governed by the interplay between competing phases, and thermodynamic behavior shapes microscopic properties and ultimately determines technological performance; for instance, the light absorption of inorganic metal-halide perovskites in solar cells. Accurately predicting crystal thermodynamics, however, remains a major challenge for computational approaches because strong anharmonic effects require extensive sampling of the potential energy surface. Here, we present an on-the-fly Bayesian framework, combined with the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation, for learning first-principles potentials. This approach enables the prediction of thermodynamic properties over a broad temperature range with first-principles accuracy while requiring training on only a few atomic configurations. A relevant finding is that the majority of the required structures are obtained from a single inexpensive dataset generation step, demonstrating that the relevant physics for accurately predicting solid-state thermodynamics is encoded in a few physically meaningful configurations. We investigate the thermodynamic and dynamical properties of Li$_2$O, $\alpha$--CsPbI$_3$, and $\delta$--CsPbI$_3$, requiring only 44, 256, and 50 total-energy calculations, respectively. Notably, we show that this framework accurately captures the extreme thermal expansion of \ce{Li2O}, and the phase diagram of CsPbI$_3$ with a predicted transition temperature within 20 K of experiment. More broadly, the method presented opens an interesting route toward accelerated materials engineering under realistic conditions for a wide range of technologically relevant applications, including batteries, photovoltaics, and memristors.

authors.name: Lorenzo Bastonero, Gabriel Joalland, Chiara Cignarella, Lorenzo Monacelli, Nicola Marzari

papers.title: Broadband molecular dynamics simulation of confined Brownian motion
papers.summary: Molecular dynamics with an explicit solvent resolves the hydrodynamic response of a Brownian colloid in bulk and near a rigid wall over acoustic, inertial, and diffusive time scales. Bulk spectra establish a continuum reference and reveal departures associated with discrete-solvent dynamics. Under confinement, thermal spectra provide a measurement of the space-dependent added mass, while velocity autocorrelations determine space-dependent, anisotropic hydrodynamic memory and diffusion. All together, these measurements connect the enhanced added mass and reduced mobility near a wall, and probe the discrete-continuum crossover.

authors.name: Quentin Thomas, Clara Mefo Sop, Maxime Lavaud, Yacine Amarouchene, Thomas Salez, Pascal Damman

papers.title: Spin Femtoscopy: A Framework for Revealing Genuine Spin Correlations
papers.summary: Spin correlations are among the most fundamental quantum observables in many-body systems, yet they remain difficult to access experimentally in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Existing spin measurements, including hyperon polarization and vector-meson spin alignment, have revealed important single-particle spin phenomena, but genuine two-particle spin correlations in the produced hadronic system remain largely unexplored. Here we propose spin femtoscopy, a framework for accessing genuine two-particle spin correlations through spin-resolved femtoscopic measurements. The key principle is that different two-particle spin configurations can give rise to different femtoscopic correlation functions because of quantum statistics and spin-dependent final-state interactions. Using $\Lambda\Lambda$ pairs as a proof of principle, we exploit the self-analyzing weak decay of $\Lambda$ hyperons to construct spin-sensitive femtoscopic correlation functions with different singlet and triplet admixtures. We show that these observables provide experimental access to the spin-state populations of the pair and allow genuine spin correlations to be separated from spin-dependent femtoscopic mixing caused by quantum statistics and final-state interactions. This work extends femtoscopy from a probe of source geometry and final-state interactions to a framework for revealing the quantum spin structure of strongly interacting matter.

authors.name: Kehao Zhang, Xuan Wang, Xiaofeng Luo

papers.title: The Quantum Pendulum of Turbulent Flow: Decaying turbulence as a thermal state of an integrable system
papers.summary:
We present a theory of decaying turbulence in which the statistics of a classical flow becomes quantum mechanics in loop space. The loop functional, the average of $e^{\mathrm{i}\Gamma/
u}$ for the circulation $\Gamma$ around a loop, is the wave function, and the Navier-Stokes equation becomes the linear loop equation. An exact operator identity represents the functional as the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/
u$, with the loop parameter as time and viscosity as Planck's constant. The turbulent state is the equal-weight density matrix on a decaying trajectory, a quantum form of the ergodic hypothesis. As in quantum field theory, turbulence at infinite Reynolds number is defined by regularization and renormalization; the loop equation regularized on $N$-sided polygons has an exact manifold of decaying solutions, the Euler ensemble, labeled by rational angles and spins. As a fermionic trace, its partition function and conditional vorticity correlations become, in the local limit, Gibbs averages of two Mathieu quantum pendulums, an integrable system. The energy spectrum, given by explicit quadratures, falls as $k^{-1}\log(1/kL)$ at small $k$ and as $k^{-7/2}$ at large $k$, with $L=\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$ and turbulent viscosity $	ilde
u$. At $kL=\sqrt2$ its slope diverges as a double logarithm: the decay at fixed $k$ is singular at a finite time, and the vorticity correlation oscillates with period $\sqrt2\,\pi L$. The reduction to the pendulums, with the continuum and grand canonical limits at every nonzero separation, is formally verified in Lean 4 in forthcoming work by Y. Jiang, A. Migdal et al. The theory rests on stated physical hypotheses, as statistical mechanics rests on the Gibbs distribution; its comparison with simulations and experiment is so far qualitative.

authors.name: Alexander Migdal

papers.title: Analytical Markov Chain for Spatiotemporal Flux Evolution of the Inner Filter Effect in Fluorescent Media
