The bulk geometry is constructed from exact black-brane solutions characterized by the fine-tuned Lovelock coupling $\alpha$ and the highest power of curvature in the Lagrangian K. We then analyze the condensation of scalar and vector operators dual to minimally coupled matter fields, focusing on two bulk-field mass prescriptions, which significantly affect the superconducting phase. Our results demonstrate that higher curvature terms significantly modify the phase structure of both s-wave and p-wave systems and enhance the sensitivity of the condensates and critical temperatures to the gravitational couplings. In both cases, the critical temperature generally increases with the maximal curvature order K, leading to higher-$T_c$ phases compared to Einstein gravity, particularly for negative $\alpha$. The coupling $\alpha$ effectively governs the strength of higher curvature interactions in the bulk: positive $\alpha$ suppresses condensation and lowers $T_c$, whereas negative $\alpha$ enhances superconducting order and promotes higher-$T_c$ phases relative to Einstein gravity. We further study the optical conductivity and find that both the gap frequency and the ratio $\omega_g/T_c$ exhibit a strong dependence on $\alpha$ and $K$, deviating from the universal Einstein-gravity result. Higher curvature effects enhance the superconducting gap scale. Notably, the p-wave system shows a stronger sensitivity to the mass-fixing prescription compared to the s-wave case.

authors.name: Soodeh Zarepour, Ali Dehghani

papers.title: Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras
papers.summary: We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.

authors.name: Vin\'icius Bernardes, Theodore Erler, Atakan Hilmi F{\i}rat, Igor Khavkine

papers.title: A Note on a High-Energy Limit of Gravitational Perturbation Theory
papers.summary: The post-Minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in Newton's constant G around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. A regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. We show that this is an asymptotic expansion. Although the series diverges we give evidence that it is Borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. As a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.

authors.name: Poul H. Damgaard, Ludovic Plante

papers.title: Wormhole-induced gravi-axion mass distributions and the second-harmonic crossover
papers.summary: We compute the distribution of the wormhole-induced gravi-axion curvature mass across baby-universe sectors when the first two harmonics are retained. For independent complex Gaussian coefficients, with an optional displacement of the first channel, an exact global-minimum condition gives the mass distribution and its threshold coefficient. At fixed nonzero second-harmonic width, the cumulative probability below mass $M$ scales as $M^5$. For a weak second harmonic, the unit-harmonic $M^4$ behavior is recovered in an intermediate low-mass range above the crossover scale. We also distinguish the actual relative mass-squared error from the probability that a phase-independent bound fails to certify the unit-harmonic approximation. In the common-background quadratic correlator with unit residues, the lower threshold remains zero and the two-harmonic tail produces an $s^{3/2}$ nonanalytic term in the Euclidean momentum squared $s$. The results are conditional on the chosen state and effective wormhole coefficients.

authors.name: Amin Rezaei Akbarieh

papers.title: Dimensional reduction and thermodynamics of a non-local scalar field theory
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the dimensional reduction of a non-local scalar field theory from $1+3$ to $1+2$ dimensions. The bulk theory is governed by an entire-function non-local form factor $e^{-\Box_E/\Lambda^2}$, where $\Lambda$ sets a fundamental high-energy scale. By constraining external classical sources to a bidimensional plane, we perform the exact dimensional reduction, derive the effective planar Green's function in terms of the complementary error function, and propose the corresponding effective non-local pseudo-differential planar Lagrangian. Using the static propagator, we determine the interaction energy between two point-like planar charges, proving that the non-local scale regularizes the short-distance singularity at the origin while smoothly recovering the standard Yukawa potential at long distances. Furthermore, we obtain the retarded, advanced, and Feynman Green's functions in coordinate space, demonstrating that macroscopic causality and tree-level unitarity are preserved. Finally, implementing the Matsubara formalism, we investigate the finite-temperature regime and evaluate the exact thermal free energy, pressure, entropy, and heat capacity. We show that the effective planar theory exhibits a fractional effective number of degrees of freedom ($g_{\rm eff}=1/2$ for $m \ll T \ll \Lambda$, crossing over to $g_{\rm eff}=1$ for $T \gg \Lambda$) originating from kinematic bulk leakage and that pressure, entropy, and heat capacity remain positive at all temperatures.

authors.name: S. Duque Cesar, M. J. Neves

papers.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
papers.summary: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model with gauge and Higgs fields regulated on a finite bosonic lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This retains the familiar continuum treatment of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes. Standard Model anomaly cancellation permits a consistent, gauge-invariant phase for the massless chiral determinant. Yukawa interactions are incorporated with a gauge-covariant spectral cutoff acting on the interaction vertices, not on the fermion propagator. Under the stated analytic conditions, the cutoff can be removed by the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, yielding a finite, exactly gauge-invariant functional integral at fixed bosonic lattice spacing and spacetime volume, including topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At zero Yukawa coupling and on smooth weak-field backgrounds, we establish agreement between the appropriately chirality-matched overlap and continuum Weyl fermion determinants up to local counterterms. We also establish reflection positivity at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta for a modified gauge-field reconstruction; its continuum equivalence with Craig's original reconstruction is not proved. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

authors.name: Stephen D. H. Hsu

papers.title: The Spectral Edge at Large Central Charge and Black Hole Statistics
papers.summary: We introduce a new approach to high-energy spectra in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, addressing the open challenge of incorporating spectral statistics into the modular bootstrap. Using the analytic theory of $L$-functions attached to two-dimensional CFTs, we leverage modular constraints among high-energy states to derive a sum rule relating the spectral edge to bulk spectral fluctuations. As an application, we establish a refined modular bootstrap bound: letting $\Delta_1$ be the conformal dimension of the lightest excited Virasoro primary of a unitary CFT of central charge $c$, we show that $\Delta_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq o(c)$, with at most one exceptional value of the scalar gap at each sufficiently large $c$. The result applies to theories with logarithmic rigidity of spectral counting fluctuations, as in random matrix theory. We exhibit circumstances under which the bound is strengthened further.

authors.name: Eric Perlmutter

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.summary: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple U(1) model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an SU(2) Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.

authors.name: Arash Arabi Ardehali

papers.title: Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
papers.summary: In the extended phase space of Donnelly and Freidel, the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole are dynamical reference frames whose phase space is the cotangent bundle of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Gluing the two exterior regions at the bifurcation point leaves a single canonical pair. Within the extended phase space, this pair can be described either by Kucha\v{r}'s mass and difference of asymptotic times or by the area and the relative rapidity of the two frames, which are two gauge choices of the same system. The latter is the pair of Carlip and Teitelboim, and the relative rapidity is the time shift of the crossed product construction. We quantize the frames in this gauge and construct the gravitational entangling product of the two exteriors. Requiring the frames to be causal restricts them to the semigroup $\mathrm{SL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, whose Plancherel measure yields the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the entanglement entropy between the two exteriors, together with a logarithmic correction, both independent of the ultraviolet cutoff.

authors.name: Ludovic Varrin

papers.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
papers.summary: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflation. We construct the Hamiltonians from the quadratic actions and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing parameters. Although the tensor propagation speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We then calculate the Nielsen circuit complexity of the corresponding two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation between the squeezing amplitudes, while the squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Therefore, the circuit complexity is mainly controlled by the evolution of the squeezing amplitudes. For the benchmark parameters considered here, a positive coupling increases the preparation cost of the scalar Gaussian state but slightly decreases that of the tensor Gaussian state. The scalar sector is therefore more sensitive to the GB coupling, whereas the luminal tensor sector provides a cleaner probe of the pump-field mechanism. Their opposite responses provide a differential state-space diagnostic of the same EGB background.

authors.name: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu, Lei-Hua Liu

papers.title: Chiral spin symmetry
papers.summary: We review the chiral spin symmetry, which is a symmetry of the color charge and of the confining electric part of QCD. Observation of this symmetry in the vacuum upon truncation of the near-zero modes of the Dirac operator implies that the hadron mass in the light quark sector is not due to the quark condensate of the vacuum and that confinement and chiral symmetry breaking are not directly related. Observation of this symmetry above the chiral symmetry restoration crossover suggests that QCD is still in the confining regime with chirally symmetric quarks bound into the color-singlets by the confining electric field. This regime of QCD was called a stringy fluid. At a temperature T_d that is essentially above T_ch the chiral spin symmetry smoothly disappears suggesting that the confining electric field gets screened and one observes a very smooth crossover to the quark-gluon plasma. The three-regimes picture has been further substantiated by the analysis of the N_c scaling of the energy density, the pressure and the entropy density. In the hadron gas they scale as N_c^0, in the stringy fluid as N_c^1 and in the quark-gluon plasma as N_c^2. We have analyzed the fluctuations of conserved charges that scale as N_c^1 above T_ch thus indicating a transition from the hadron gas to the stringy fluid. When N_c gets sufficiently large the three-regimes picture transforms into the three-phases phase diagram. Finally we discuss a confining and chirally symmetric model in 3+1 dimensions. This model demonstrates the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime and a delocalization of the color-singlet quark-antiquark systems that become very large at T > T_ch. Consequently the stringy fluid matter is a very dense highly collective system of the overlapping very large color-singlet quark-antiquark "mesons" with a very small mean free path.

authors.name: L. Ya. Glozman

papers.title: How Significant are Cosmological Collider Signals in the Planck Data?
papers.summary: The search for primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) is theoretically well motivated but remains observationally challenging. Tight constraints with low significance for the standard non-Gaussian shapes suggest that detection may lie beyond the reach of near-future experiments. However, tests of PNG are highly template-dependent. From a theory perspective, a whole new family of bispectrum shapes arise in the cosmological collider program, with distinct signatures of heavy particles during inflation. In this work, we provide a class of simplified collider templates for these particles that encompasses a broader range of masses, sound speeds, and interactions. We propose that, given the current state of observations, the most effective strategy to search for PNG signals is through orthogonalizing the collider templates, such that they are uncorrelated with the tightly constrained single field predictions. Our results show that removing the single-field contribution enhances the signal across all four templates studied. Using the {\it Modal} pipeline and \textit{Planck} CMB data, we perform a systematic parameter scan of the (\textit{orthogonalized}) collider templates with the most significant result reaching $2.4\sigma$ for spin-0, after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect; indicative results for spin-1 and spin-2 peak around 2$\sigma$. These results indicate that, with refined collider templates and improved data analysis strategies, there are credible prospects with forthcoming observations to detect PNG {\it and also} identify the presence of massive particles during inflation.

authors.name: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E. P. S. Shellard

papers.title: Novel thermodynamic inequality for rotating AdS black holes
papers.summary: We propose a new thermodynamic inequality for stationary, asymptotically Anti-de Sitter rotating black holes, expressed in terms of their angular momentum, mass and thermodynamic volume as $ 4\pi J^2/(3MV)<1 $. For the solutions considered, this inequality follows from the requirement that the thermodynamic identities admit a physical horizon with positive area. We examine Kerr(-Newman)-AdS, Kerr-Sen-AdS, pairwise-equal four-charge AdS black holes, charged rotating AdS black strings, and charged rotating AdS C-metrics, finding strong supporting evidence for the inequality across different horizon topologies. We then reformulate the inequality in terms of the underlying metric parameters and compare the resulting constraints with the corresponding regularity and horizon-existence conditions. This analysis shows that the proposed inequality has different physical content for different geometries. We further examine charged super-entropic black holes, for which the ultraspinning limit leads instead to a lower bound on the thermodynamic ratio. This result is consistent with the violation of the reverse isoperimetric inequality characteristic of super-entropic solutions. Moreover, when combined with the refined reverse isoperimetric inequality, the proposed bound ensures the physicality of the Kerr-AdS reference solution entering the refined bound and thereby yields the conventional reverse isoperimetric inequality. We also extend the proposed relation to higher dimensions and test it for singly spinning thin AdS black ring with nonspherical horizon topology, finding that the corresponding inequalities are satisfied throughout the thin-ring regime.

authors.name: Hamid R. Bakhtiarizadeh

papers.title: Asymmetric Dark Matter from Low-Scale Spontaneous Leptogenesis
papers.summary: We investigate a novel type of asymmetric dark matter (ADM) model in which the dark matter asymmetry and the baryon asymmetry in our universe (BAU) are produced simultaneously via low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis, where the mass scale of right-handed neutrino is much lower than the Davidson-Ibarra bound $M_1 \ll 10^{9}~\rm{GeV}$. In our scenario, both asymmetries are predominantly sourced by a dynamical $CP$ phase, namely the majoron. Its kinetic misalignment provides a sufficiently large, time-dependent effective $CP$ phase, allowing efficient asymmetry production even for low-scale right-handed neutrinos. In our framework, the sources of $CP$ violation responsible for the BAU and ADM are correlated with each other, leading to a predictive relation for the dark matter mass. In particular, when the dark matter asymmetry reaches its equilibrium value before freeze-out, the dark matter mass is typically predicted to lie in the range $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_{\chi} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(100)~\mathrm{GeV}$, which lies within the sensitivity of direct detection experiments. On the other hand, if the dark matter asymmetry does not reach its equilibrium value due to weak coupling, the allowed mass range extends over a broader interval, $\mathcal{O}(0.1)~\mathrm{GeV} \lesssim m_{\chi} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10)~\rm{TeV}$.

authors.name: Hiroki Takahashi, Juntaro Wada

papers.title: Varying Newton constant, entropy and the black hole evaporation law
papers.summary: We assume that the Newton potential of a spherically symmetric body of mass $M$ is $V=-G(M)Mr^{-1}$, where the Newton constant $G$ may depend on $M$. We insert this assumption in the Schwarzschild solution. We discuss varying $G$ in the black hole thermodynamics and black hole evaporation law. We extend the Bekenstein-Hawking formula $\hbar GS=\frac{1}{4}A$, where $S$ is the entropy and $ A$ the area, to a varying $G$. It is shown that if $G(M)$ is of the form of a power-law $G\simeq M^{-\Gamma}$ then $G(M)S\simeq A$ is still preserved but the evaporation law substantially depends on the function $G(M)$.

authors.name: Julia Haba, Zbigniew Haba

papers.title: Challenging the Weak Cosmic Censorship with Phantom Fields
papers.summary: Penrose's weak cosmic censorship conjecture asserts that spacetime singularities produced by gravitational collapse are generically hidden behind event horizons, thus preventing them from causally influencing distant observers and preserving the predictability of the exterior region. In this work, we probe this conjecture in a setup that deliberately violates one of its central assumptions - the dominant energy condition - by considering the spherical collapse of a phantom scalar field with negative energy density. In principle, such a field could produce a Schwarzschild geometry with negative mass and therefore no event horizon. Our aim is to assess whether, once the dominant energy condition is abandoned, the fully coupled evolution of matter and geometry can dynamically generate or expose naked singularities, thereby probing the robustness of cosmic censorship. To this end, we perform high-accuracy numerical relativity simulations based on fourth-order finite-difference schemes. Starting from smooth, asymptotically flat initial data representing regular phantom scalar wave packets, we follow their fully nonlinear evolution through collapse or dispersion. While an ordinary (positive-energy) scalar field exhibits the standard Choptuik critical behavior at the threshold of black-hole formation, the phantom field displays qualitatively different dynamics. For all amplitudes considered, we find no evidence for trapped surfaces, naked singularities, or alternative stationary end states. Instead, the phantom scalar field disperses in all the configurations studied. Within the parameter space explored, we find no dynamical violation of cosmic censorship.

authors.name: Giovanni Caridi, Fabrizio Corelli, Paolo Pani

papers.title: On deforming and breaking integrability
papers.summary: In this paper we study nearest-neighbour deformations of integrable models. After expanding in the deformation parameter, we identify four possible types of deformations. First there are deformations that simply break or preserve integrability. Then we find two different subtle cases. The first case is where the deformation is only integrable if all orders of the deformation parameter are taken into account. An example of these are the long-range deformations that appear in holographic models. The second case is when the deformation is perturbatively integrable to some order in the deformation parameter but can not be extended to an integrable model. In this paper we work this out for the XXZ spin chain and discuss the level statistics of each of these cases. We find numerical evidence that the onset of chaos occurs differently in each of these models. For the perturbatively integrable models, we find that the deformation strength at which chaos appears demonstrates a volume-scaling intermediate between strong and weak integrability breaking models.

authors.name: Ysla F. Adans, Marius de Leeuw, Tristan McLoughlin

papers.title: Stationary solutions in the small-$c$ expansion of GR
papers.summary: We study the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity in ADM variables up to next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). We show that, in the stationary sector, this formulation renders the field equations more tractable for explicit solution building. The stationary equations acquire a structure, in which the leading lapse and spatial metric are determined by a closed subsystem, the NLO rotational field satisfies a linear equation on that background, and the NNLO fields satisfy a linear system sourced by the NLO data. The stationary sector exhibits both strong-gravity and weak-field branches, whose structure becomes richer at NNLO. In the strong-gravity branch, we first obtain exact vacuum solutions of NLO Carroll gravity, including the Lense--Thirring and rotating C-metric backgrounds. At NNLO, we then construct the corresponding Lense--Thirring-type and C-metric-type exact vacuum geometries. These solutions also arise from the small-$c$ expansion of the Kerr and rotating C-metric geometries around the strong-gravity background, up to $\mathcal{O}(J)$ at NLO and up to $\mathcal{O}(J^3)$ at NNLO. In the weak-field branch, we find exact Hartle--Thorne-type solutions with an independent quadrupole moment, together with exact spin-squared corrections and a mixed quadrupolar-rotating solution. We further extend the $\ell=0,2$ sector by including higher multipoles up to $\ell=4$, where $\ell$ denotes the multipole index. These results show that the full NLO/NNLO theory admits a richer stationary vacuum sector than the magnetic Carroll truncation. More broadly, the ADM formulation provides a practical framework for constructing and analyzing stationary backgrounds in the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity, and may also offer a useful framework for organizing rotational and higher-multipole deformations motivated by relativistic compact-object geometries.

authors.name: Enes Bal, Ertu\u{g}rul Ekiz, Emre Onur Kahya, Utku Zorba

papers.title: Renormalization-group improved Schwarzschild black hole: shadow, ringdown, and strong cosmic censorship
papers.summary: A renormalization-group (RG) improved Schwarzschild-like black hole (BH) is studied here, with a lapse that interpolates between a classical Schwarzschild exterior and a quantum-smoothed interior set by a cutoff scale $\xi$ and an interpolation parameter $\gamma$. We work out the horizon structure together with the photon sphere and shadow radius $R_{\mathrm{sh}}$, set up the scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli problems in a single treatment, and compute the fundamental and overtone quasinormal modes by sixth-order WKB, cross-checked against time-domain ringdown. For $\xi>0$ and $\gamma>0$ the geometry is regular, with a de Sitter core. Strong Cosmic Censorship (SCC) is examined at the inner Cauchy horizon, which the improved geometry generates without charge or rotation. The quasinormal spectral gap $\beta=|\mathrm{Im}\,\omega|/\kappa_-$ stays multipole-independent at the $6\%$ level and follows $\beta\simeq\lambda_{L}/(2\kappa_{-})$. It remains below the de Sitter Christodoulou bound across the parameter range, and the asymptotically flat late-time tail places the geometry in the SCC-respecting class. A thermodynamic analysis identifies a Davies-type phase transition of the outer horizon, with the Schwarzschild $T_{H}\propto 1/r_{+}$ decay replaced by a bell-curve profile peaking at $T_{H}^{\max}\simeq 0.062$. A scan of the $(\xi,\gamma)$ plane gathers the joint behavior of the shadow, the scalar barrier, the SCC ratio, and $T_H$. Set against Bardeen, Hayward, and Bonanno-Reuter BHs at matched perturbation scale, the improved Schwarzschild BH is the most Schwarzschild-like of the regular-BH family, its static shadow radius degenerate with Hayward and Bonanno-Reuter at the percent level. The closing analysis takes up the sparsity of the Hawking flux and the energy-emission rate, both tied to the outer-horizon surface gravity through a single auxiliary function.

authors.name: Ahmad Al-Badawi, Faizuddin Ahmed, \.Izzet Sakall{\i}

papers.title: Canonical quantization of all minisuperspaces with consistent symmetry reductions
papers.summary: We present the quantization of all symmetry reductions of the Einstein--Hilbert Lagrangian that correctly reproduce the reduced Einstein's field equations -- i.e., characterized by the infinitesimal group actions obeying the principle of symmetric criticality. These correspond to the spacetime symmetries of spherical/hyperbolic/planar Schwarzschild/Taub--NUT, BI/BII/BIII-metrics, near-horizon extreme Kerr geometry, swirling universe, closed/open/flat FLRW cosmologies, other FLRW-type metrics, and Bianchi type I, II, VIII, and IX spacetimes. We derive the Hamiltonian and the conformal symmetries of the superspace metrics (the conditional symmetries), promote them to operators, and solve the Wheeler--DeWitt equation with and without imposing these symmetries.

authors.name: Poula Tadros, Ivan Kol\'a\v{r}, Otakar Sv\'itek

papers.title: Cancellation of one-loop time dependence in superhorizon curvature perturbations from all scales
papers.summary: We show the conservation of the superhorizon curvature perturbations at one-loop level in spatially-flat gauge, including contributions from loop wavenumbers on all scales in the decoupling limit, $\epsilon (\equiv -\dot H/H^2) \to 0$. In contrast to previous works, we do not assume a hierarchy $k \gg q$ between the wavenumber of the loop integral, $k$, and that of the power spectrum, $q$, and we explicitly include the regime $k \lesssim q$. Taking into account the nonlinear relation between the inflaton fluctuation and the curvature perturbation with the $\delta N$ formalism, we show that the apparent time dependence of the one-loop curvature power spectrum cancels once all contributions, including boundary terms, are combined consistently.

authors.name: Keisuke Inomata

papers.title: Perturbative Dissipation in Minimal Warm Inflation
papers.summary: We present an analysis of the perturbative modes of dissipation in the minimal warm inflation model where an axion-inflaton is coupled to a gluon thermal bath through the axion-gauge coupling. The corresponding friction coefficient, which generically is governed by IR physics, for the processes we consider is dominated by Landau damping of soft space-like gluons and the plasmon decay of hard on shell gluons. Since both of these processes are IR dominated, the friction coefficient becomes sensitive to the non-perturbative magnetic mass scale $m_{g}^{-1} \sim (\alpha T)^{-1}$ which in turn leads to the friction coefficient's overall linear proportionality to $\alpha$, which is much less suppressed in $\alpha$ powers compared to the well understood term from Chern-Simons (CS) diffusion $(\propto \alpha^5)$. On the other hand, this contribution to the friction coefficient is suppressed due to slow roll. We show that this can be viewed as a suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation for derivative couplings in general and that time correlations of nonlocal variables which do not fall off at large time separations are what allow an unsuppressed friction coefficient.

authors.name: Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Lian-Tao Wang

papers.title: Revealing the Quantum Signature of Gravity via Gravitational Waves
papers.summary: Can propagating gravitational waves serve as operational probes of the quantum nature of gravity? We address this question by developing a unified theoretical framework that combines spacetime geometry, quantum information, and gravitational-wave physics. Starting from the geodesic deviation equation in linearized General Relativity, we derive the effective detector Hamiltonian directly from spacetime geometry and construct the complete quantum dynamics for detector subsystems interacting with both classical and quantized propagating gravitational-wave fields. This unified formulation enables a direct comparison between classical and quantum descriptions of gravitational radiation within the same physical framework. We demonstrate that classical gravitational-wave backgrounds can induce mixedness in the detector state but cannot generate genuine quantum correlations between the detector subsystems. In contrast, quantized gravitational waves coherently mediate gravity-induced entanglement, quantum coherence, quantum memory, and nonclassical correlations, providing clear operational signatures of the quantum nature of propagating gravitational radiation. We further discuss how mesoscopic quantum mechanical oscillators offer a promising route towards experimentally probing these effects. Our results establish a geometric and quantum-information-based framework for exploring quantum gravity through propagating gravitational waves.

authors.name: Partha Nandi

papers.title: Tidal Love numbers of wormholes as black-hole mimickers
papers.summary: We study the dynamical scalar tidal Love numbers of wormholes that provide viable mimickers for black holes, focusing on thin-shell Schwarzschild and Damour-Solodukhin geometries. Using a matched near- and far-zone expansion, we determine their tidal response in the low-frequency regime. The presence of a long throat introduces an additional characteristic scale and naturally separates the modes into two classes. Super-throat modes probe the global wormhole geometry and are sensitive to both asymptotic regions, whereas sub-throat modes probe only one side of the wormhole and effectively perceive the throat as a black-hole horizon. We derive the scalar tidal Love numbers analytically for both classes of modes and show that their dissipative parts exhibit distinct low-frequency behavior, reflecting whether one or both potential barriers participate in the scattering process. We further find that, as the wormhole approaches the black-hole limit, the super-throat contribution becomes progressively negligible, while the sub-throat response smoothly reduces to that of a Schwarzschild black hole. These results demonstrate that the tidal response of wormholes depends crucially on whether the perturbation probes the global structure of the throat.

authors.name: Sergey N. Solodukhin, Vagif Tagiev

papers.title: Soft-gluon effective coupling for massive quarks
papers.summary: We present a generalisation of the soft-gluon physical coupling, defined in terms of the strength of soft radiation from a hard dipole, to massive hard emitters. We derive the relation between this coupling and the $\overline{\rm MS}$ coupling through two loops, encompassing all configurations in which both, one, or neither of the hard emitters are massive. We show that the presence of massive emitters introduces additional freedom in the definition of the physical coupling scheme, which we characterise at two-loop order. Our results provide new ingredients for precision QCD resummation in processes involving heavy quarks and for the development of higher-order parton-shower algorithms.

authors.name: Luca Bason, Simone Devoto, Andrea Ghira, Simone Marzani, Pier Francesco Monni, Giovanni Ridolfi

papers.title: Observing Transverse Momentum Broadening from TEECs in Heavy Ion Collisions
papers.summary: We study the azimuthal dependence of transverse energy-energy correlators (TEECs) in dijet events in heavy-ion collisions. In the back-to-back region this observable resolves the energy flow around $\phi=\pi$ and is sensitive to medium-induced momentum broadening and the response of the medium. To isolate final-state effects, we consider a quark-antiquark pair produced in a colour-singlet hard process and propagating through a homogeneous background medium. Starting from the vacuum TMD factorization formula, we combine NLL$'$ resummation with medium modifications at first order in the strong coupling. For the parameters studied, (classical) momentum broadening lowers the back-to-back peak and leaves the distribution elsewhere nearly unchanged, while radiative corrections significantly suppress the peak further and enhance larger angular decorrelations. We additionally include the medium response sourced by each jet, as a mean energy flow. This spreads the deposited energy over the whole azimuth, so that the contribution to the TEEC varies slowly across the back-to-back region, is small at the peak and grows toward larger angles.

authors.name: Jo\~ao Barata, Hai Tao Li, Andrey V. Sadofyev, Jo\~ao M. Silva

papers.title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
papers.summary: Simulations on a quantum computer have been propounded as a next-generation tool for studying neutrino flavour oscillations in dense environments like supernovae or neutron star mergers. However, quantum advantage hinges on the presence of quantum entanglement in the neutrino ensemble, and it has been argued that such entanglement becomes negligible in the limit of large neutrino number density. Here, we address this question by explicitly simulating the multiparticle dynamics of entangled neutrino ensembles with a varying number of particles, $N$, on both classical and quantum hardware, and comparing our results to those obtained with conventional ``mean-field'' methods based on Boltzmann-type kinetic equations. For simple toy systems, we demonstrate both analytically and numerically that, indeed, the predictions of full multiparticle simulations agree with those of mean-field methods in the large-$N$ limit. Along the way, we develop novel algorithms for the efficient simulation of entangled neutrino gases on both classical and quantum hardware. We then discuss physical situations in which an entangled neutrino system \emph{cannot} be described through mean-field dynamics alone and quantum entanglement therefore becomes phenomenologically relevant. We comment on the conditions under which these scenarios may be realized in supernova cores or neutron star mergers.

authors.name: Katarina Bleau, Nikolina Ilic, Joachim Kopp, Ushak Rahaman, Xin Yue Yu

papers.title: Opening up derivative baryon-number-violating operators
papers.summary: Baryon number violation is our most sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, typically encoded in higher-dimensional effective operators. Operators involving derivatives are often ignored in phenomenological analyses since they are generically suppressed compared to non-derivative operators. We systematically construct tree-level UV completions of derivative baryon-number-violating operators up to mass dimension 12 in the Standard Model effective field theory (extended by right-handed neutrinos) and show that derivative operators need not be suppressed. Our public code can be used to UV-complete other derivative operators.

authors.name: Julian Heeck, Diana Sokhashvili

papers.title: A Phase-Transition Portal to Enhanced Dark Matter Annihilation
papers.summary: We present a thermal dark matter (DM) scenario in which a phase transition after freeze-out changes both the DM spectrum and the dominant annihilation process, allowing an enhanced present day annihilation rate with suppressed direct detection. We realize this mechanism in a two-Higgs-doublet model extended by a complex scalar singlet, a Majorana fermion, and a heavier Dirac fermion. Before the transition, the Majorana state freezes out through $p$-wave annihilation into singlet scalars. The subsequent transition changes the dark fermion masses and mixing, enabling $s$-wave annihilation through a pseudoscalar portal. The surviving relic differs in mass and composition from the original state. We find relic compatible solutions with present day annihilation rates more than an order of magnitude above the canonical thermal value, without tuning to a mediator resonance, while satisfying direct detection bounds.

authors.name: Peisi Huang, Anibal D. Medina, Carlos E. M. Wagner, Kairui Zhang

papers.title: Exact and hybrid neutrino oscillation probabilities via the evolution operator
papers.summary: We revisit the three-flavor neutrino oscillations in constant-density matter using the evolution matrix expressed in terms of the Lagrange-Sylvester interpolation. Taking advantage of Vieta's formulas for the Hamiltonian of the system, we derive exact closed expressions for the oscillation probabilities $P_{ee}$, $P_{\mu e}$, and $P_{\mu\tau}$, which are concise and simple, and structurally identical to their vacuum counterparts. The CP-violation contribution, proportional to the Jarlskog invariant $\mathcal{J}$, appears as a single, clearly separated term. Our approach does not require introducing neutrino mixing in the medium and avoids using a matter-dependent CP-violation phase, facilitating the separation of genuine CP violation from that induced by matter effects. We explicitly verify that, in the limit $V \to 0$, our expressions for the flavor transition probabilities reduce to the well-known vacuum formulas. The exact structure of the probabilities is preserved if the exact, not very enlightening, trigonometric eigenvalues are replaced by approximate expressions in radicals. We illustrate this hybrid approach with eigenvalues obtained from two successive rotations of the Hamiltonian. For an experiment like DUNE, the hybrid probability values match those of the exact probabilities within absolute errors of about $2\times 10^{-6}$ in all channels and relative errors less than $0.01 \%$ for $P_{ee}$, $P_{\mu e}$, and $P_{\mu\tau}$.

authors.name: Juan Carlos D'Olivo, Jos\'e Arnulfo Herrera Lara, Oscar A. Sampayo

papers.title: Twist-3 and flavor-singlet contributions to $\gamma\gamma\to\pi^{0}\eta^{(\prime)}$ and $\eta^{(\prime)}\eta^{(\prime)}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization
papers.summary: We study two-photon production of the pseudoscalar pairs $\pi^{0}\eta$, $\pi^{0}\eta^{\prime}$, $\eta\eta$, $\eta\eta^{\prime}$, and $\eta^{\prime}\eta^{\prime}$ at center-of-mass energies $2<Q<4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization, including the chirally enhanced twist-3 amplitudes and the two-gluon component of the $\eta^{(\prime)}$. The twist-3 amplitudes raise the hard cross sections by about an order of magnitude in all five channels. They bring $\eta\eta$ close to the Belle data, while $\pi^{0}\eta$ stays 3 to 5 times below and falls too slowly with energy. Varying the two-gluon distribution amplitude within its uncertainty changes the cross sections by about 2% in $\pi^{0}\eta$ and $\eta\eta$ but by up to 24% in the $\eta^{\prime}$ channels, making them its probe. The hard and handbag mechanisms each give nearly constant ratios $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$ and $\sigma(\eta\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$, whereas below $3.2\,\mathrm{GeV}$ the measured $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio lies above both predictions and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below them. Adding the handbag amplitude coherently, with its modulus fixed by the pion and kaon channels and its phase fitted, reproduces the $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio up to $4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below $2.8\,\mathrm{GeV}$, and steepens $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)$ to a $Q^{-n}$ dependence with $n=9.7\pm1.6$, against the measured $10.5\pm1.2\pm0.5$. The energy dependence of the cross section ratios can thus be understood as the interference of two mechanisms of comparable size.

authors.name: Cong Wang, Jun-Kang He

papers.title: Spiral momentum spectra and spin asymmetry in vacuum pair production driven by phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields
papers.summary: We study vacuum electron--positron pair production in phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields using the quantum kinetic equations. We analyze how the modulation amplitude, frequency, ellipticity, and modulation form affect the spin-resolved momentum spectra and the spin asymmetry. Cosine-type modulation can deform ring-shaped momentum distributions into spiral patterns. This deformation depends nonmonotonically on the modulation amplitude and frequency and is most pronounced for circular polarization. In the transverse momentum plane, the spin-resolved yields favor the spin channel along the direction of field handedness. Reversing the field handedness would reverse the favored channel while leaving the total yield unchanged. Sine-type modulation preserves ring-shaped and mirror-symmetric spectra approximately, however, it leads to a stronger dependence of the spin asymmetry on the modulation amplitude than cosine-type modulation does. These results show that phase modulation and ellipticity can control the momentum spectra patterns in vacuum pair production. Moreover, phase modulation can also affect the degree of spin asymmetry.

authors.name: Li-Yi Yang, Hong-Hao Fan, Jing-He Huang, Shuo Yang, Bai-Song Xie

papers.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos

authors.name: Ki-Young Choi, Ankhbayar Tugssaikhan

papers.title: Production of hidden-charm molecular candidates with hidden strangeness in $B_s^0$ decays
papers.summary: We study the production of spin-one $D_{s0}^*(2317)\bar D_s^*$, $D_{s1}(2460)\bar D_s^*$, and $D_{s1}(2536)\bar D_s^*$ molecular candidates in $B_s^0$ decays with an accompanying $\eta$, providing a complementary probe of their structure and production mechanisms. The meson-loop rescattering amplitudes are constructed from factorized weak sources and heavy-hadron chiral interactions. Constituent couplings are estimated using threshold-dependent compositeness relations, and the associated input uncertainties are propagated to the predicted rates. Opposite-$C$-parity partner hypotheses are included with inherited benchmark parameters. We calculate the branching fractions for two relative signs. Over the cutoff range $2\leq\alpha\leq5$, the larger central branching fractions reach several $10^{-6}$ to several $10^{-5}$, suggesting potential accessibility in future experimental measurements.

authors.name: Yue Su, Ying-Bo He, Xiao-Yun Wang, Xiao-Hai Liu

papers.title: Renormalon-chain contributions to two-point correlators of nonlocal quark currents and light-meson distribution amplitudes
papers.summary: In the framework of QCD sum rules, we study the endpoint slopes of the leading-twist distribution amplitudes in the large-$\beta_0$ approximation for the pion and the longitudinally polarized $\rho$ meson. To this end, we compute the two-point massless correlator of non-local composite vector quark currents with the gluon lines dressed by chains of one-loop fermion bubbles. This correlator depends on the Bjorken fraction $x$ associated with the composite current and, within the large-$\beta_0$ approximation, provides the dominant contribution in each order of perturbation theory. We derive an inequality for the second Gegenbauer moments of these distribution amplitudes that agrees with predictions from lattice QCD.

authors.name: S. V. Mikhailov, N. Volchanskiy

papers.title: Stimulated Axion Decay around Primordial Black Holes and the Diffuse Radio Background
papers.summary: We study stimulated axion decay in dense axion halos around primordial black holes (PBHs), assuming that both PBHs and axions contribute to dark matter. We construct the axion density profile by matching a hydrogenic soliton-like core dominated by the PBH potential to the $r^{-9/4}$ spike produced by secondary infall. We also impose an inner cutoff at the innermost stable circular orbit. We derive local Boltzmann equations for the number densities of photons and axions, including spontaneous and stimulated decay, inverse decay, photon escape, and axion filling. We solve these equations numerically and with a semi-analytic approximation. Stimulated emission occurs within an inner region where photon amplification overcomes escape. We calculate the photon emission from an individual PBH halo and integrate it over the population of PBHs throughout cosmic history. By requiring the resulting diffuse radio spectrum not to exceed the radio background measured by ARCADE~2, we derive upper bounds on the fraction of dark matter in PBHs. The bounds are strongest at intermediate PBH masses and apply over a wider mass range as the coupling between axions and photons increases.

authors.name: Ki-Young Choi, Junghoon Joh, Kenji Kadota

papers.title: Roles of $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ in the process $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$: a clean probe of the $K\bar K$ final-state interaction
papers.summary: Based on the Belle measurement of $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$, we study the contributions of the light scalar mesons $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$, dynamically generated from the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson--pseudoscalar meson interaction within the chiral unitary approach, to the threshold enhancement in the $K_S^0K_S^0$ invariant mass squared distribution, and examine the possible contribution of the intermediate $\Sigma(1620)$ resonance in the $pK_S^0$ subsystem. We first argue that the $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$ channel is a cleaner probe of the $K\bar K$ final-state interaction than the charged channel $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK^+K^-$, since the $\phi$ and $\Lambda^*$ contributions are forbidden and the $\Sigma(1620)$ and $\Sigma(1660)$ couple weakly to the $\bar{K}N$ channel. The threshold enhancement in the $K_S^0K_S^0$ invariant mass squared distribution is well described by the $S$-wave $K^0\bar K^0$ final-state interaction alone, with the $f_0(980)$ contribution dominating while that of $a_0(980)$ is small, supporting the interpretation of $f_0(980)$ as a $K\bar K$ hadronic molecular state. Future high-precision measurements by Belle~II and the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility will help test the roles of the $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ and of the possible $\Sigma(1620)$ contribution in this process.

authors.name: Li-Na Zhou, Le-Le Wei, Li-Juan Liu, En Wang

papers.title: Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ from Chiral Perturbation Theory
papers.summary: We construct effective operators for transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions in Chiral Perturbation Theory. The operators constructed from pion and nucleon fields possess the main properties of the QCD operators, including multiplicatively renormalizable rapidity divergences. Extracting the leading rapidity divergence, we find the expression for the Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ and at the low-energy normalization point, which is model-independent up to an additive constant. In this regime, the Collins-Soper kernel has a nearly constant behavior. We also find that at large $b$ it depends on the isospin channel and on the hadron type, although this dependence is numerically very small.

authors.name: Alexey Vladimirov

papers.title: Spin Correlations in $t\bar{t}$ Production and Decay at the LHC in Perturbative QCD
papers.summary: Among recent developments in top-quark physics at the LHC, the production of top-quark pairs near threshold has attracted considerable attention, partly due to tensions between data and theoretical predictions. We show that reliable predictions for threshold-sensitive observables, such as spin correlations and the differential distribution in the $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass, can be obtained in perturbation theory by retaining the first few powers of $\alpha_s/v$, where $v$ is the relative velocity of the top quarks. Applying this approach to reweight nominal Monte Carlo predictions for spin-sensitive observables, we find good agreement with data. We also discuss how threshold effects, including bound-state contributions, can be incorporated on an event-by-event basis into fully differential Monte Carlo event generators.

authors.name: Emanuele Re

papers.title: Nucleon-resonance contributions to the $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ reaction
papers.summary: Within an effective Lagrangian approach, we investigate the associated charmonium production reaction $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ from threshold up to $\sqrt{s}=5.00\,\mathrm{GeV}$, incorporating intermediate contributions from the ground-state nucleon and the nucleon resonances $N(1535)$, $N(1650)$, $N(1895)$, and $N(1710)$. The effective resonance parameters are constrained by the BESIII measurement of the crossed decay $\eta_c\to p\bar{p}\eta$ for both the constructive (Solution C) and destructive (Solution D) radiative-interference solutions. Using these decay-constrained parameters, we predict the total and differential Born cross sections for the $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ reaction. We show that coherent resonance exchanges dominate the near-threshold production dynamics and significantly enhance the total cross section compared to the pure nucleon-exchange contribution, which suffers from a strong dynamical cancellation. As the collision energy increases, the rapidly growing nucleon contribution progressively dilutes the resonance terms, reducing the relative difference between the total cross sections for Solutions C and D. Furthermore, while the pure nucleon-exchange amplitude exhibits an exact dynamical zero at $\theta=90^\circ$ due to the pseudoscalar coupling structure, resonance exchanges fill this node in the predicted angular distributions, providing an observable test of the underlying exchange mechanisms. These predictions can be tested in future antiproton annihilation experiments at $\bar{\mathrm{P}}\mathrm{ANDA}$.

authors.name: Wen-Ying Liu, Xiang Liu

papers.title: Parton density functions for future electron-positron colliders
papers.summary: Precision QED radiative corrections are critical for the physics programs of future high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders. We review the state-of-the-art QED parton density function (PDF) formalism for resumming collinear photon and pair emissions. Our numerical analysis of initial-state radiation (ISR) highlights the slow convergence of the perturbative series and the growing significance of pair production at higher orders. Finally, we emphasize the need to implement these theoretical refinements into modern Monte Carlo generators to meet the stringent precision demands of upcoming experimental measurements.

authors.name: Andrej Arbuzov, Cecilia Romero, Uliana Voznaya

papers.title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
papers.summary: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $\theta^{}_{23} = \left(\theta^{}_{12} + \theta^{}_{13}\right)/2 + \pi/8$, which predicts $\theta^{}_{23} = 43.46^{+0.51^\circ}_{-0.52^\circ}$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and present a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter as a by-product.

authors.name: Zhi-zhong Xing

papers.title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tan\beta$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
papers.summary: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tan\beta$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tan\beta$, $1\le \tan\beta \le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$. The lineshapes in the four search channels are governed by a simple complex parameter $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant to non-resonant amplitudes at the peak. Because the $H$ and $A$ bosons couple weakly to the considered final states, while being broadened by their decays to top quarks, $|\kappa|$ drops to values of a few for masses of $0.5$--$1$ TeV, even though the total widths remain at the percent level. The interference then increases the signal rates by up to tens of per cent, and distorts their lineshapes. For the present ATLAS (and presumably CMS) Run II exclusion limits, the net effect is nevertheless rather modest, except at the high-mass end of the $H\to hh$ contour, but it becomes important for the masses that will be probed at the high-luminosity LHC.

authors.name: Abdelhak Djouadi, John Ellis

papers.title: Uncovering TeV-scale dark matter with Z-fusion at a muon collider
papers.summary: We demonstrate the advantage of the $Z$-boson fusion channel at a high-energy, high-luminosity muon collider in eliciting signals of a TeV-scale scalar dark matter (DM) particle. The utility of such a set-up lies in (a)the attainability of high centre-of-mass energy ($\approx 10 ~\rm TeV$), (b)the likely availability of large integrated luminosity ($\gtrsim 10~ab^{-1}$), and (c)the facility for efficient detection of very forward tagged muons. Our analysis is based on the process $\mu^+ \mu^- \rightarrow \mu^+ \mu^-$ + missing energy, driven by $Z$-fusion. We present the results in the context of (i) a scenario characterised by dimension-6 effective couplings, and (ii) an inert doublet model. After filtering each scenario through its associated constraints, we find that it is possible to achieve a signal significance of about 6.7$\sigma$ in case (i) and about 5.5$\sigma$ in case (ii), for DM particle masses $\approx$ 1 TeV and an integrated luminosity of $10 ~ ab^{-1}$.

authors.name: Anindya Datta, Jayita Lahiri, Biswarup Mukhopadhyaya

papers.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
papers.summary: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $\phi$ couples via the effective operator $\phi\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $\phi$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.

authors.name: Anish Ghoshal, Alessandro Strumia

papers.title: DarkMatterFM-Registry: A Machine-Readable Registry of Dark-Matter Models Extracted from the arXiv Literature
papers.summary: To use a dark-matter model one needs to know what defines it, which observables it affects, which codes and likelihoods evaluate it, and under what assumptions a published bound applies. That information is scattered across tens of thousands of papers. We present DarkMatterFM-Registry, a machine-readable registry of dark-matter models extracted from arXiv full texts by a staged large-language-model (LLM) pipeline: 6,145 structured model cards, validated against a seven-file JSON Schema suite, ranked by expected value for observational follow-up, and enriched for the top ~2,000 with observables, constraints, and theory-to-observable routes. Schema checks pass 97.8% of cards, and an LLM-judged accuracy study on a stratified card sample finds 81% of section verdicts correct, 18% partially correct, and none hallucinated. As a first application we turn the registry into a priority-weighted roadmap of 25 concrete projects the community could build. The roadmap is built by judging every computational step of every enriched model's theory-to-observable routes as available, partial, or missing, and aggregating the resulting typed gaps weighted by model priority. We find that what blocks the most high-priority models is not missing theory but missing shared infrastructure: model files for existing relic-abundance solvers, a general non-cold Boltzmann-code framework, reusable indirect-detection likelihoods, and a Lyman-$\alpha$ forest likelihood for non-cold dark matter (the largest gap for structure-formation probes). The model cards, schemas, roadmap, and ranking are released making the project reproducible and the cards available for the community.

authors.name: Ioana A. Zelko, Jo Bovy, Nolan Koblischke

papers.title: Primordial or Post-Inflationary: Distinguishing the Origin of Scale-Dependent Features in the CMB
papers.summary: Physics beyond the Standard Model, whether of primordial or post-inflationary origin, can leave scale-dependent signals in the anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, we study how distinguishable these broad classes of signals are and quantify their level of degeneracy. In this initial investigation, for primordial features, we limit ourselves to those of the ``sharp'' and ``resonant'' kinds; for post-inflationary features, we consider two qualitatively distinct models: exotic energy injection, which deposits energy into the primordial plasma and modifies the global thermodynamic history, and early dark energy (EDE), which affects the CMB through the background expansion and gravitational perturbations. By studying representative examples, we find that while primordial features can leave oscillatory signatures in the CMB power spectrum with essentially arbitrary frequency and running, the post-inflationary models considered here produce qualitatively different patterns that cannot generically reproduce the characteristic running of primordial feature oscillations. We verify these findings first with a principal component analysis, and show using only the most significant principal components that there are no significant degeneracies between the primordial and post-inflationary features considered here, and secondly with a full likelihood analysis, which shows that the resulting posteriors do not change significantly when considering individual classes of models or combinations of primordial/post-inflationary features. While the two post-inflationary models probe distinct physical mechanisms and both are implemented in a simplified, phenomenological fashion, the methods used in this work can be generalized to include more realistic signals or other classes of signals.

authors.name: Matteo Braglia, Wenzer Qin, Xingang Chen, Tracy R. Slatyer

papers.title: Nonstandard Dark Matter at Nonlinear Scales
papers.summary: We investigate how two extensions of the standard $\Lambda$CDM scenario affect the evolution of the matter density and velocity divergence fields, from the linear regime to deeply nonlinear scales, using $N$-body simulations. We consider two well-motivated scenarios in which the canonical properties of dark matter (DM) are modified. In the first scenario, DM interacts with dark energy (DM--DE interaction). In the second scenario, we allow the DM equation-of-state parameter to deviate from the canonical pressureless limit, $w_{\rm DM}=0$. For the coupled DM--DE scenario, we find significant and scale-dependent deviations from $\Lambda$CDM of order $50$--$100\%$ in the matter power spectrum, persisting throughout the nonlinear regime, with the velocity divergence spectra providing complementary and partially independent sensitivity. For the $w_{\rm DM} \neq 0$ scenario, we find systematic but remarkably small deviations confined within $5\%$ across all scales probed. Our results identify which scales carry the greatest discriminatory power between these nonstandard scenarios and $\Lambda$CDM. We show that testing these models with current and forthcoming LSS surveys, through the analysis of density and/or velocity fields, will require a deeper theoretical understanding and accurate nonlinear modelling before robust constraints can be derived from observational data.

authors.name: Rafael C. Nunes

papers.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.summary: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.

authors.name: Rafael C. R. de Lima, Luciano de Oliveira Junior, Pedro Martins Bailer

papers.title: Effect of collective nuclear vibrations on initial anisotropies in central Pb+Pb collisions: A comparative study in Glauber and Trento models
papers.summary: We perform a comparison of the Glauber and Trento model predictions for the initial state azimuthal anisotropies $\epsilon_{2,3}\{2\}$ in central Pb+Pb collisions at the LHC energies. We incorporate the quantum collective effects in $^{208}$Pb by sampling nucleon positions with filterings in the quadrupole and octupole moments. We use the data-driven filters adjusted to reproduce the mean squared quadrupole and octupole moments extracted from the experimental strength functions. We find that the collective effects reduce considerably the $\epsilon_2\{2\}/\epsilon_3\{2\}$ ratio. The reduction is more pronounced in the Trento model. We obtain $\epsilon_2\{2\}/\epsilon_3\{2\}\approx 0.75\div 0.79(0.68\div 0.71)$ in the Glauber(Trento) models. These values allow to resolve the $v_2$-to-$v_3$ puzzle.

authors.name: B. G. Zakharov

papers.title: Relativistic analogue of the Kramers-Henneberger transformation and pair creation
papers.summary: In analogy to the Kramers-Henneberger transformation in non-relativistic quantum mechanics, we propose and investigate a spinor transformation for the Dirac equation which allows us to transform space-time dependent vector potentials $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}$_x away. In the mass-less case, we exactly arrive at the free Dirac equation, while for massive Dirac fields, the transformation results in a non-trivial mass matrix containing space-time dependent phases. Special emphasis is placed on the phenomenon of fermion pair creation in the external field $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}_x$ where the spinor transformation allows us to conceptually disentangle the different contributions to pair creation. It can also be used to reformulate the WKB approach and the Riccati equation (which can be advantageous in certain cases) and to obtain additional insight into the mechanism of dynamically assisted pair creation.

authors.name: Johannes Marschall, Christian Kohlf\"urst, Naser Ahmadiniaz, Ralf Sch\"utzhold

papers.title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
papers.summary: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $\nu_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space. In all cases, we obtain remarkably consistent NSM transition densities. Our factorized and nonfactorized cross sections agree, remaining 20% higher than the measured value. In addition, we use NSM single-nucleon transition densities as ansatz and find that solving the anomaly requires fine-tuned densities, with percent-level cancellations and an overall scale orders of magnitude larger than the calculated NSM ones. We conclude that the gallium anomaly is not solved when using realistic nuclear transition densities.

authors.name: D. Castillo, D. Frycz, J. Men\'endez

papers.title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
papers.summary: The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair ($t\bar{t}$) kinematics in the dilepton $t\bar{t}$ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with $t\bar{t}$ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by $7\%$, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of $t\bar{t}$. In addition, two machine-learning (ML) based approaches are developed using a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow. Relative to LKRv3, they improve the resolution of the invariant mass, transverse momentum and rapidity by approximately $30\%$, $20\%$ and $15\%$, respectively. In particular, a resolution of 30 GeV is achieved for the reconstructed invariant mass of $t\bar{t}$ near the production threshold. A dedicated generator-level study and a generator-to-detector transfer test demonstrate that the ML approaches learn a genuine physics-driven correction to the $\nu\bar{\nu}$ approximation, rather than merely exploiting detector-specific effects. These results demonstrate the strong potential of ML-based approaches for improving the reconstruction of dilepton $t\bar{t}$ events, while identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as an important limitation on the achievable resolution.

authors.name: V. Aushev, M. Spitsyn, R. Yermolenko, O. Zenaiev

papers.title: Pomeron Weights in QCD Processes at High Energy and the $S$-Matrix Unitarity Constraint
papers.summary: The pomeron topological cross-section is derived for the eikonal and the $U$-matrix unitarization schemes using a generalized representation of the scattering amplitude at high energy in an effort to examine pomeron characteristics, namely the multiplicity distribution, fluctuation, and correlation, and to reveal the impact of pomeron weights on the $pp$ multiplicity distribution. The results demonstrate that the $U$-matrix inherently incorporates a larger amount of diffraction production into the multi-pomeron vertices, yielding a larger pomerons' variability regardless of the energy range, while such fluctuations become significant only beyond a specific high-energy threshold in eikonal-like schemes. Most importantly, our findings indicate that within the $U$-matrix scheme, an increase in exchanged pomerons results in more pronounced pomeron correlations and that this correlated resummation plays a key role in enhancing multi-parton collisions. We argue that the choice of unitarization scheme is not arbitrary, as it directly dictates the statistical structure of multi-reggeon exchanges. By reflecting the composite nature of hadrons, rational alternatives to eikonal-like schemes, such as the $U$-matrix, offer a compelling theoretical foundation for modeling high-energy hadronic collisions, provided that specific formulations can be identified that strictly satisfy all mathematical and physical constraints.

authors.name: Rami Oueslati

papers.title: Two-loop renormalisation of quark and gluon fields in the SMEFT
papers.summary: We compute the contributions of CP-conserving operators in the dimension-six SMEFT to the two-loop renormalisation constants of quark and gluon fields in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$-scheme. Specifically, we consider the top-quark chromomagnetic operator and the triple gluon operator. We work with the background-field method, which allows us to extract the contribution of these operators to the two-loop running of the top mass and the strong coupling constant. We discuss in detail the mixing with the unphysical operators required for the renormalisation, and we present analytic results for the renormalisation constants of all relevant operators.

authors.name: Claude Duhr, Andres Vasquez, Giuseppe Ventura, Eleni Vryonidou

papers.title: Observation of quantum entanglement in $\Lambda \bar{\Lambda}$ pair production via electron-positron annihilation
papers.summary: Quantum entanglement, a profound feature of quantum mechanics where particles share interconnected states regardless of distance, has been extensively studied in low-energy systems like photons and atoms. Exploring entanglement in high-energy particle collisions offers unique opportunities to probe quantum phenomena under extreme conditions. Here we demonstrate the observation of quantum entanglement between lambda and anti-lambda hyperons ($\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$) produced in electron-positron collisions via the decay of the $J/\psi$ particle. By analyzing the angular correlations of the protons and antiprotons emerging from the subsequent weak decays of the hyperons, we identify clear signatures of entanglement that violate the limits derived for product states. This result confirms that entanglement persists through both the strong interaction production process and the weak decay processes. We further establish a general polar-azimuthal selection rule showing that azimuthal correlations are indispensable for entanglement certification in spin-$1/2$ fermion-antifermion systems. It is also confirmed that a significant majority of these decay events occur at spacelike separation, meaning that no classical signal could connect them. The successful detection of entanglement in this hyperon-antihyperon system establishes a new methodology and platform for measuring quantum properties in relativistic particle physics, complementing traditional approaches and opening avenues for future investigations into decoherence or symmetry violations in high-energy collisions.

authors.name: Junle Pei, Xiqing Hao, Xiaochuan Wang, Tianjun Li

papers.title: Two-loop renormalisation of quark and gluon fields in the SMEFT in the on-shell scheme
papers.summary: We compute the contributions of CP-conserving dimension-six SMEFT operators to the two-loop renormalisation constants of quark and gluon fields in the on-shell scheme. Specifically, we consider the top-quark chromomagnetic operator and the triple gluon operator. We also compute the contribution of four-quark operators to the gluon renormalisation constant and discuss the implications for the running of the strong coupling constant.

authors.name: Claude Duhr, Giuseppe Ventura, Eleni Vryonidou

papers.title: Higgs Signal Strength Estimation with Machine Learning under Systematic Uncertainties
papers.summary: We present a dedicated graph neural network (GNN)-based methodology for the extraction of the Higgs boson signal strength $\mu$, incorporating systematic uncertainties. The architecture features two branches: a deterministic GNN that processes kinematic variables unaffected by nuisance parameters, and an uncertainty-aware GNN that handles inputs modulated by systematic effects through gated attention-based message passing. Their outputs are fused to produce classification scores for signal-background discrimination. During training we sample nuisance-parameter configurations and aggregate the loss across them, promoting stability of the classifier under systematic shifts and effectively decorrelating its outputs from nuisance variations. The resulting binned classifier outputs are used to construct a Poisson likelihood, which enables profile likelihood scans over signal strength, with nuisance parameters profiled out via numerical optimization. We validate this framework on the FAIR Universe Higgs Uncertainty Challenge dataset, yielding accurate estimation of signal strength $\mu$ and its 68.27\% confidence interval, achieving competitive coverage and interval widths in large-scale pseudo-experiments. Our code "Systematics-Aware Graph Estimator" (SAGE) is publicly available.

authors.name: Minxuan He, Claudius Krause, Daohan Wang

papers.title: Two-loop renormalisation of the quark fields in the presence of four-fermion SMEFT operators
papers.summary: We compute the contributions of the dimension-6 SMEFT operators involving four third-generation quarks to the two-loop renormalisation of the quark fields and masses. We perform the computations in both the Naive Dimensional Regularisation (NDR) and the Breitenlohner-Maison-`t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) schemes, and we present results for all relevant field and mass renormalisation constants in the on-shell and MS-bar schemes. We carefully discuss all scheme choices which affect the final results. This completes the computation of field and mass renormalisation constants relevant for two-loop computations in QCD involving dimension-six SMEFT operators.

authors.name: Claude Duhr, Giuseppe Ventura, Eleni Vryonidou

papers.title: Charmonium production at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron and Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research
papers.summary: In this study we apply the Remler formalism to charmonium production at SPS and GSI/FAIR energies in order to investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD). As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in p+p collisions and then applied to p+A collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which $J/\psi$ dissociates near $T_c$. Finally the same formalism is applied to the low CERN/SPS energy and GSI/FAIR energies, where we estimate charmonium production.

authors.name: Taesoo Song, Jiaxing Zhao, Joerg Aichelin, Elena Bratkovskaya

papers.title: Probing TeV-scale Majorana neutrinos at a muon-proton collider via a lepton-number-violating fat-jet signature
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity to TeV-scale heavy Majorana neutrinos at a future muon-proton collider with $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV, based on 1~TeV muon and 7~TeV proton beams. We focus on the lepton-number-violating (LNV) process $\mu^- p \to jN$, followed by $N\to\mu^+W^-\to\mu^+J$, leading to the characteristic final state $j\mu^+J$. Here, $j$ denotes the associated light jet from heavy-neutrino production, while $J$ denotes the fat jet originating from the hadronic decay of the highly boosted $W$ boson. This topology provides a clean experimental signature with strongly suppressed Standard Model backgrounds. A comprehensive signal and background analysis is performed using parton showering, fast detector simulation, and dedicated fat-jet reconstruction. We derive the projected $2\sigma$ exclusion limits on the muon-flavor mixing parameter $|V_{\mu N}|^2$ for integrated luminosities of $100$~fb$^{-1}$ and $1$~ab$^{-1}$. For heavy-neutrino masses in the range $1~\mathrm{TeV}\leq m_N\leq3~\mathrm{TeV}$, the projected upper limits on $|V_{\mu N}|^2$ range from $2.6\times10^{-6}$ to $5.9\times10^{-5}$ at $1$~ab$^{-1}$. These results show that a future $\mu p$ collider can provide competitive and complementary sensitivity to TeV-scale heavy Majorana neutrinos compared with other proposed high-energy facilities.
