The leading correction vanishes when exchanging the two internal states of the excitation reverses the interaction. Varying the source and observation time makes all bond phases locally identifiable near the zero-phase reference setting. We also prove a conditional quantum advantage for distribution-free response prediction.

authors.name: Yuting Lyu

papers.title: Magic Can Superactivate Quantum Capacity
papers.summary: Environmental magic can enable two channels with zero quantum capacity to transmit quantum information jointly. We establish this superactivation within a family of discrete quantum convolution channels with fixed Clifford interactions. For the couplings considered, stabilizer-mixture environments induce entanglement-breaking channels. We construct a mixed magic environment whose induced channel has positive private capacity and a Choi state with positive partial transpose, hence zero quantum capacity. A half-erasure auxiliary activates this channel through the Smith--Yard mechanism. Finite-block encoding and decoding over a self-complementary convolution auxiliary then realize a higher-dimensional erasure channel that still permits activation. We also bound the activated capacity by the modified relative entropy of magic of the main environment. Replacing either environment of the convolution pair by any stabilizer mixture makes the joint quantum capacity vanish, identifying environmental magic as a necessary resource on both sides for this realization.

authors.name: Chunhe Xiong, Sunho Kim, Shunlong Luo, Lin Zhang, Shao-Ming Fei, Junde Wu

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
papers.summary: Free fermions exhibit Eigenstate Typicality (ET) meaning that the reduced density matrix, $\rho$, of a small spatial subsystem of a {\sl single}, typical, excited energy eigenstate is gaussian with a modular hamiltonian, $h \equiv -\log \rho$, asymptotically proportional to the free fermion hamiltonian. In effect, the ET may be thought of as providing an independent route to establishing the Fermi-Dirac (FD) distribution for free fermions. We revisit this argument for fermions belonging to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates. Specifically, we show that the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates in a 1-d free fermion lattice system is interacting, and therefore the reduced density matrix for the subsystem is not gaussian. Measurements of the single particle distribution of a small subsystem would then exhibit non-thermal deviations from the FD distribution. These features may be traced to a violation of Wick's theorem for the chosen excited state. We develop a perturbation theory for the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a weak mixture of degenerate states and study the modular hamiltonian (exactly) computationally. Finally, we speculate that initial conditions in a realistic fermi system evolving towards equilibrium might be encoded in the interaction terms of the modular hamiltonian and consequent correlations of fermions.

authors.name: Gregory C. Levine, Goncalo C. Oliveira

papers.title: Quantum subsets discrimination and key sifting with success probability one
papers.summary: Non-distinguishability of non-orthogonal quantum states is the essential feature of quantum mechanics. In particular, one cannot deterministically orthogonalize the set of quantum states, while probabilistic orthogonalization is possible, including unambiguous state discrimination and discrimination between the subsets. Here, we propose a method for error-free subsets discrimination with significantly increased success probability, which may reach one even for non-orthogonal and linearly dependent input states. This method may be applied in quantum cryptography: An alternative basis reconciliation procedure is described, which may provide unit sifting probability even for a large number of bases and for non-orthogonal states within each basis.

authors.name: D. A. Kronberg

papers.title: Efficient One-Shot Simulation of Network Instruments and Multi-party Purity Distillation
papers.summary: We undertake an information theoretic study of instrument compression problems (ICPs) in {multiple network} configurations, wherein the goal is to design and analyze protocols that simulate specific quantum classical (QC) correlation amidst distributed parties - some holding components of the quantum state and the rest holding classical registers - with minimum communication. We present a \textit{unified framework} of protocols based on likelihood instruments whose analysis yields new inner bounds in the one-shot and asymptotic regimes for the different network configurations we study. Our framework comprises of a common template for designing the instrument simulation protocol and analyzing its information theoretic performance. We also address a related problem of multi-party purity distillation wherein three distributed parties have to distil pure states efficiently via local operations and minimal communication. In regards to the tools, in addition to one-shot purity concentration protocol of \cite{202203arXiv_ChaPadSen} and one-shot quantum simultaneous decoder of Sen \cite{202102SAD_Sen}, we leverage Sen's fully smooth multi-partite covering \cite{202504arXiv_Sen} for all of our covering bounds.

authors.name: Igor Bernard, Arun Padakandla

papers.title: Slices for normal forms in quantum information and a Riccati-type equation
papers.summary: It is known that the normal space to an orbit of a compact group linear action meets each orbit. We show that this yields known normal forms for quantum states. We compute the gradient flow converging to the normal form and find it gives a Riccati type matrix-valued ODE.

authors.name: Ranee Brylinski, Jean-Luc Brylinski

papers.title: A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
papers.summary: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.

authors.name: A. K. Mandal, F. Zhang, J. H. Mikkelsen, M. Shen

papers.title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
papers.summary: In this work, we focus on addressing challenges related to modelling the integration of conventional high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing (QC). We introduce the Quantum Assembly Compiler (QASC) for OpenQASM3.0 files. The compiler produces an executable that leverages the high-performance simulator QuEST to simulate quantum programs. Additionally, we introduce a performance modelling tool, QACC-perf, which can estimate the cost of integrating QC in classical HPC workflows, as well as the execution time of the quantum circuits. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these tools in the context of multiscale quantum chemistry workflows using the ChemShell computational chemistry environment.

authors.name: Mateusz Meller, Joseph C. R. Thacker, Thomas W. Keal, Vendel Szeremi

papers.title: An Adaptive Quantum Search Framework under Unknown Solution-density: Minimizing Expected Queries to the First Solution
papers.summary: Grover's algorithm provides a mathematically optimal quadratic speedup for unstructured search, yet its standard formulation relies on a critical prerequisite: prior knowledge of the target solution count to determine the number of algorithm iterations. Although numerous strategies have been developed to identify or bypass this parameter, comparing them directly is nontrivial. This study investigates and computationally optimizes 3 prominent frameworks: Boyer-Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp, Fixed-Point search, and Density Estimation Methods. Density-specific benchmarks select the best tested method and configuration to minimize expected first-solution queries under 2 initialization-cost conventions. To translate these theoretical benchmarks into practical utility, a hybrid quantum-classical adaptive framework integrating Hill-climbing-assisted Grover Adaptive Search with state-space density estimation modeled via the Wang-Landau algorithm is proposed as a potential use-case. This implementation operates directly on the optimized query methods established earlier. Analytical models support the approach; ideal simulations show 18.8%-63.4% lower mean accumulated query costs than the tested randomized and fixed-point baselines.

authors.name: Wiwat Asawalertsak, Rajchawit Sarochawikasit

papers.title: Witnessing Polarization Entanglement of Annihilation Photons via Compton Scattering
papers.summary: Experimentally certifying polarization entanglement in annihilation photons is challenging because polarizers are unavailable in the high-energy regime and one needs to rely on Compton polarimetry. Previously proposed schemes designed for this task are either experimentally unfeasible or require a specific source state model. We address these issues by reformulating Compton scattering as a continuous-outcome quantum instrument, thereby enabling the prediction of the scattering angles and the post-scattering polarization state. Our framework allows connecting Compton polarimetry with entanglement witnesses by deriving experimentally accessible lower bounds on Bell state fidelities for arbitrary initial two-photon polarization states. We discuss how this witness can be extracted from coarse-grained coincidence measurements with detectors of almost any angular resolution. The presented scheme does not require knowledge of angle-independent empirical factors like detector efficiencies and source activity. Thus, our results provide a feasible route towards experimental entanglement certification in para-positronium decay with current technology.

authors.name: Tobias C. Sutter, Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

papers.title: Differentiable Digital Twins for Optimization, Calibration, and Characterization of Neutral-Atom- and Ion-based Quantum Computers
papers.summary: Quantum technologies based on individually controlled atoms are among the most promising platforms for scalable quantum computing, owing to their favorable coherence properties and controllability. Nonetheless, achieving reliable and high-fidelity gate operations remains challenging due to the sensitivity of these systems to noise and hardware imperfections. In this work, we introduce a comprehensive software toolset designed to model atomic quantum systems with high precision and simulate qubit gate dynamics. By integrating quantum optimal control and benchmarking techniques with automatic differentiation for efficient and accurate gradient-based optimization, the toolset enables significant improvements in gate performance. We demonstrate its capabilities through detailed case studies involving both neutral atoms and trapped ions, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing quantum gate fidelities, and providing valuable insights for experimental implementation.

authors.name: Marco Rossignolo, Lorena C. Bianchet, Anurag Saha Roy, Shai Machnes

papers.title: Beyond the $n/2$ Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
papers.summary: The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every $n$-bit Boolean function with bounded error using $n/2+O(\sqrt n)$ quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using $\lceil n/2\rceil$ queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond $n/2$ is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring $n/2+\Omega(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using $n/2+O(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.

authors.name: Yuan Deng, Zihan Hao, Honghao Lin, Qipeng Liu, Vahab Mirrokni, Jianan Shao, David P. Woodruff

papers.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
papers.summary: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.

authors.name: Yousef Mafi, K. G. S. H. Gunawardana, Kim P\"oyh\"onen, Teemu Ojanen

papers.title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
papers.summary: Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search. However, conventional quantum search formulations typically assume access to an oracle that identifies valid solutions, while standard implementations generally yield probabilistic success. In this work, we propose a generalised quantum oracle construction method for NP problems, together with a deterministic quantum search framework that identifies satisfying assignments using their corresponding classical verifier functions. The proposed framework retains the quadratic query speedup of quantum search over classical exhaustive search. We further establish that constructed oracle can be implemented using a number of gates polynomial in the size (L) of the binary encoding of verification function, consistent with the polynomial-time evaluation of the corresponding classical verifier, while the total qubit requirement remains O(poly(L)). The construction is demonstrated on multiple N-SAT instances, with circuit-level simulations confirming deterministic identification of satisfying assignments. These results establish the applicability of deterministic quantum search to NP problems while retaining the quadratic query advantage over classical exhaustive search.

authors.name: Soumyajyoti Chatterjee, Harishankar Mishra, Asvija Balasubramanyam, S D Sudarsan, Gudapati Naresh Raghava

papers.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
papers.summary: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and R\'enyi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

authors.name: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares, Yevgeniy Kovchegov, Giorgio Torrieri

papers.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
papers.summary: We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.

authors.name: Nada Khogeer, Jerison Parra, Caroline Desgranges, Hugo Ribeiro

papers.title: pfoqcompiler: Efficient Compilation of Quantum Control in Recursive First-Order Quantum Programs
papers.summary: Recursive quantum control allows for simple and concise descriptions of algorithms. However, a naive circuit compilation sequentializes the different branches of the quantum if-statement and results in an exponential increase in circuit depth. Existing techniques can parallelize these branches, but do so at the cost of an exponential number of ancillary qubits. We present pfoqcompiler, a compiler targeting Qiskit for the first-order quantum programming language FOQ that exploits program structure to merge compatible recursive procedure calls across quantum branches. We introduce weaker syntactically-checkable conditions for well-foundedness, recursive halving, and uniformity, while preserving previously demonstrated complexity characterizations. For weakly well-founded bounded-width programs, the compiler produces polynomial-size circuits; weakly recursively halving programs additionally yield polylogarithmic depth, while weak uniformity removes the asymptotic overhead of branch sequentialization.

authors.name: M\'ario Silva (LMF, QuaCS), Alexandre Guernut (MOCQUA), Marco Lewis (LMF, QuaCS)

papers.title: A Complete Calculus for Hamiltonian Quantum Programming
papers.summary: Given the forces acting on a quantum particle, a Hamiltonian models its continuous evolution. Quantum computers evolve Hamiltonians to simulate physical systems, to solve optimisation problems, and to estimate eigenvalues, and even the popular circuit abstraction is compiled to Hamiltonians on the hardware. We introduce Hamilton, a process calculus whose parallel operator is the sum of interactions acting simultaneously. Its operational semantics is the Lie-Trotter product formula, which recovers a sum as the limit of ever finer sequential interleavings; compiling a program means halving it to a chosen precision and unrolling the interleaving into a circuit. The semantics is fully abstract, the expressible Hamiltonians are exactly those whose Pauli coefficients have the form $m/2^k$, the precision that successive halving reaches, and the equational theory is complete and decidable. A full implementation compiles Hamilton programs to circuits and decides their equivalence, and Agda proofs sanity-check the core metatheory.

authors.name: Jacques Carette, Chris Heunen, Robin Kaarsgaard, Neil J. Ross, Amr Sabry

papers.title: Features of Non-Local Quantum Correlations in Nuclei
papers.summary: Classical simulation of quantum many-body systems is challenged by the combined effects of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic). Non-local magic, $M^{\mathrm{NL}}_\alpha$, quantifies the component of non-stabilizerness that cannot be removed by local unitary transformations and provides a measure of quantum complexity beyond entanglement alone. It is bounded from below by the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, ${F}_A$. We calculate stabilizer R\'enyi entropies, non-local magic, entanglement-spectrum antiflatness, and entanglement entropy in shell-model ground states of more than 260 even-even, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei, using a bipartition into proton and neutron sectors. We find that the previously established bound $4{F}_A\leq{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ holds for every nucleus studied and approaches saturation in the limit of separable states. Odd-odd nuclei exhibit markedly different patterns of entanglement and magic compared with even-even and odd-even systems, revealing distinctive signatures of proton-neutron quantum correlations and providing new insight into the complexity generated by nuclear interactions.

authors.name: James W. T. Keeble, Caroline E. P. Robin, Federico Rocco, Martin J. Savage

papers.title: $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge and exact solution of the $\pm J$ Edwards-Anderson model in a transverse field
papers.summary: Using the Majorana representation of spin-1/2 operators, we study the $\pm J$ Edwards--Anderson model in a transverse field at $T=0$. We show that, in this representation, the quantity describing the coupling between neighboring spins commutes with the Hamiltonian and, unlike in the Kitaev model, is not subject to any Gauss law. The resulting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge freedom allows the disorder in the signs of the exchange integrals to be eliminated by an exact gauge transformation, so that the spectrum of the system coincides with that of the model with uniform couplings. The resulting theory is quadratic in the Majorana fields. Computing the local Green's functions, we find that the Edwards--Anderson order parameter vanishes for $\Delta>J\sqrt{Z}$ and equals $1/4$ for $\Delta<J\sqrt{Z}$, which signals a second-order transition from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass ground state that is degenerate over spin configurations and replica symmetric at $T=0$.

authors.name: Mikhail Vasin

papers.title: Local Correlations Determine the Dephasing Threshold of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology
papers.summary: In this work, we try to understand the question of how to address the survival of band topology in the presence of dephasing. We investigate this question in the Kane-Mele $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological insulator. To determine the stability of the topological invariant we construct a single particle Hamiltonian that also provides identical correlation at the single particle level. The phase transition from topological to trivial is determined by the gap closing of this correlation Hamiltonian. This gap closing is related to purity gap. As a diagnostics we calculated the invariant directly and as a complementary diagnostic, coherent two-terminal transport through the auxiliary correlation Hamiltonian exhibits quantized conductance in the nontrivial region. This does not establish physical conductance under dephasing. Our results identify a predictive local criterion for the survival of single-particle topological structure under a specified noise channel.

authors.name: Rishith Reddy V, Ashutosh Dubey, Partha Sarathi, Ankur Das

papers.title: A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
papers.summary: Aaronson and Ambainis conjectured that every bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. They showed that the conjecture implies that the acceptance probability of every quantum algorithm making $T$ queries can be approximated on most inputs by a classical algorithm making $\mathrm{poly}(T)$ queries. We prove their conjecture: every function $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ of degree at most $d\ge1$ has a variable of influence at least $c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^{5/2}/d^{6}$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. In the original formulation, for polynomials of degree at most $d$ with values in $[0,1]$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ and variance at least $\varepsilon$, this gives a variable of influence at least $(\varepsilon/d)^{7}$. The proof is elementary, with steps inspired by works of others. Thus, as Aaronson and Ambainis anticipated, superpolynomial quantum speedups in the query model require structure, such as a promise on the inputs.

authors.name: David Turturean

papers.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
papers.summary: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.

authors.name: Josep Cabedo, Claudio Iacovelli, Leticia Tarruell, Alessio Celi

papers.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
papers.summary: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.

authors.name: Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, David P. DiVincenzo, Viatcheslav V. Dobrovitski

papers.title: Limit cycles in periodically driven open quantum systems
papers.summary: We investigate the long-time behavior of quantum N-level systems that are coupled to a Markovian environment and subject to periodic driving. As our main result, we obtain a general algebraic condition ensuring that all solutions of a periodic quantum master equation with Lindblad form approach a unique limit cycle. Quite intuitively, this criterion requires that the dissipative terms of the master equation connect all subspaces of the system Hilbert space during an arbitrarily small fraction of the cycle time. Our results provide a natural extension of Spohn's algebraic condition for the approach to equilibrium to systems with external driving.

authors.name: Paul Menczel, Kay Brandner

papers.title: Deterministic interconversion of the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state and Knill-Laflamme-Milburn state via Lie-transform-based pulse design in Rydberg atoms
papers.summary: Conversion between different types of entangled states is an interesting problem in quantum mechanics. But research on the conversion between Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state and Knill-Laflamme-Milburn (KLM) state in atomic system has not been reported. In this paper, we propose a scheme to realize the interconversion (one-step) between GHZ state and KLM state with Rydberg atoms. By utilizing Rydberg-mediated interactions, we simplify the system. By combining Lie-transform-based pulse design, the evolution path is built up to realize interconversion of GHZ state and KLM state. The numerical simulation result shows that the present scheme is robust against decoherence and operational imperfection.

authors.name: J. P. Wang, Y. Q. Ji, L. P. Yang, C. Q. Wang, L. Dong, X. M. Xiu

papers.title: Learning State Preparation Circuits for Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.summary: Many-body ground state preparation is an important subroutine used in the simulation of physical systems. In this paper, we introduce a flexible and efficient framework for obtaining a state preparation circuit for a large class of many-body ground states. We introduce polynomial-time classical algorithms that take reduced density matrices over $\mathcal{O}(1)$-sized balls as inputs, and output a circuit that prepares the global state. We introduce algorithms applicable to (i) short-range entangled states (e.g., states prepared by shallow quantum circuits in any number of dimensions, and more generally, invertible states) and (ii) long-range entangled ground states (e.g., the toric code on a disk). Both algorithms can provably find a circuit whose depth is asymptotically optimal. Our approach uses a variant of the quantum Markov chain condition that remains robust against constant-depth circuits. The robustness of this condition makes our method applicable to a large class of states, whilst ensuring a classically tractable optimization landscape.

authors.name: Hyun-Soo Kim, Isaac H. Kim, Daniel Ranard

papers.title: Concentration of ergotropy in quantum many-body systems
papers.summary: Ergotropy$\unicode{x2014}$the maximal amount of unitarily extractable work$\unicode{x2014}$quantifies the "charge level" of a quantum battery. We prove that, in large many-body batteries, it exhibits a concentration of measure phenomenon. Namely, the ergotropy almost coincides with its average for almost all states sampled from the Hilbert$\unicode{x2013}$Schmidt measure. Importantly, the average ergotropy is macroscopic, scaling with the number of particles in the system. This occurs despite the von Neumann entropy also concentrating around a macroscopic average, a surprising coexistence since high entropy is commonly associated with effective thermality and thus passivity. We establish these results by proving that ergotropy, as a function of the state, is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the Bures distance and by applying L\'evy's measure concentration lemma. Furthermore, we numerically extend our findings to the Bures measure, which represents the situation with the least amount of prior information about the state. Our continuity and concentration bounds open a new perspective on the noise-robustness of quantum many-body batteries and lay the groundwork for further rigorous studies of their charge stability and work extraction with limited prior knowledge.

authors.name: Karen Hovhannisyan, Rick P. A. Simon, Janet Anders

papers.title: Quantum-to-classical transition and the emergence of trajectory level Darwinism with measurements distributed in time: a path integral approach
papers.summary: We present a formulation for the emergence of classical dynamics in a quantum world using a path integral approach that incorporates continuous measurements. It complements decoherence and coarse-grained measurement frameworks. The formulation provides the joint statistics of a sequence of measurements, with each Feynman path picking up a random phase proportional to the measurement strength, and we give conditions under which trajectories near classical paths dominate the probability amplitude. Information proliferates across the environment, a key feature of quantum Darwinism, via plane-wave probe scattering. In the continuous limit, momentum kicks from the probes add a further phase to each trajectory--the origin of the back-action force. We provide conditions under which measurements yield enough ``which-path'' information while keeping the wave packet localized. This describes the quantum-to-classical transition at the level of individual measurement records, complementing the ensemble description by density matrices. The same scattering that decoheres a trajectory also heats it, tying decoherence and measurement back-action together. This bounds how redundantly a classical trajectory can be recorded before back-action randomizes it into Brownian motion. The bound is not restrictive for macroscopic systems. For a trapped particle, it is set by the resolution in units of the zero-point motion and collapses to a single record where the semiclassical description of the orbit fails; for a free coordinate it marks the loss of deterministic objectivity even while the classical action remains large. In both cases, it delimits the regime in which objective classical trajectories exist. The crossover is driven by photon recoil, already resolved in levitated optomechanics; the bound recasts it as the point where a redundantly recorded trajectory, still objective, stops being deterministic.

authors.name: Harsh Arora, Bishal Kumar Das, Baladitya Suri, Vaibhav Madhok

papers.title: Statistics of Strongly Coupled Defects in Superconducting Qubits
papers.summary: Decoherence in superconducting qubits is dominated by defects that reside at amorphous interfaces. Interaction with discrete defects results in dropouts that complicate qubit operation and lead to nongaussian tails in the distribution of qubit energy relaxation time $T_1$ that degrade system performance. Spectral diffusion of defects over time leads to fluctuations in $T_1$, posing a challenge for calibration. In this work, we measure the energy relaxation of flux-tunable transmons over a range of operating frequencies. We vary qubit geometry to change the interface participation ratio by more than an order of magnitude. Our results are consistent with loss dominated by discrete interfacial defects. Moreover, we are able to localize the dominant defects to within 500 nm of the qubit junctions, where residues from liftoff are present. These results motivate new approaches to qubit junction fabrication that avoid the residues intrinsic to the liftoff process.

authors.name: S. Weeden, D. C. Harrison, S. Patel, M. Snyder, E. J. Blackwell, G. Spahn, S. Abdullah, Y. Takeda, B. L. T. Plourde, J. M. Martinis, R. McDermott

papers.title: Orbit dimensions in linear and Gaussian quantum optics
papers.summary: We study the dimension of the manifold of quantum states (called orbit) that a given bosonic state can reach under linear or quadratic Hamiltonian evolutions. That is, we investigate how many directions in the Hilbert space a state can explore in these sub-universal regimes. After showcasing a simple way to compute orbit dimensions, we find that these topological quantities reveal fundamental insights into the structure of attainable state spaces (e.g., boson bunching does not increase the number of accessible directions) with multifaceted consequences. First, we illustrate how they can alone yield no-go results for some transformations. We then propose ways to probe orbit dimensions using homodyne/heterodyne measurements on pure states, or photon counters on two copies of general states. We also relate orbit dimensions to the number of directions accessible to bosonic variational circuits. Next, we study links between orbit dimensions and the resource theory of non-Gaussianity (resp. $P$-nonclassicality), and prove that free states coincide with a unique minimal-dimension orbit in the pure multimode case, under Gaussian (resp. displaced-linear) unitaries. We then extend this result to a mixed-state setting, provided that an alternative convex-roof-based definition of orbit dimensions is taken; however, we show that those fail to be fixed-mode monotones under the respective free operations. Our entire framework is proven to hold in both discrete and continuous-variable settings, and can be used with Fock as well as phase-space representations such as the Wigner or stellar representations. Overall, this work offers a new perspective on the structure of reachable quantum states of light, which can help practitioners understand limitations and sources of expressivity and non-Gaussianity (or $P$-nonclassicality) in bosonic quantum information protocols such as quantum machine learning.

authors.name: Eliott Z. Mamon

papers.title: Imprints of information scrambling on eigenstates of a quantum chaotic system
papers.summary: How are the spatial and temporal patterns of information scrambling in locally interacting quantum many-body systems imprinted on the eigenstates of the system's time-evolution operator? We address this question by identifying statistical correlations among sets of minimally four eigenstates that provide a unified framework for various measures of information scrambling. These include operator mutual information and operator entanglement entropy of the time-evolution operator, as well as more conventional diagnostics such as two-point dynamical correlations and out-of-time-ordered correlators. We demonstrate this framework by deriving exact results for eigenstate correlations in a minimal model of quantum chaos -- Floquet dual-unitary circuits. These results reveal not only the butterfly effect and the information lightcone, but also finer structures of scrambling within the lightcone. Our work thus shows how the eigenstates of a chaotic system can encode the full spatiotemporal anatomy of quantum chaos, going beyond the descriptions offered by random matrix theory and the eigenstate thermalisation hypothesis.

authors.name: Bikram Pain, Ratul Thakur, Sthitadhi Roy

papers.title: Quantum algorithms to detect ODMR-active defects for quantum sensing applications
papers.summary: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are a promising platform for quantum sensing. Simulating the defect's optical response and optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast is key to identifying suitable candidates. However, existing simulation methods are typically unable to supply the required accuracy. Here, we propose two quantum algorithms to detect an imbalance in the triplet-to-singlet intersystem crossing (ISC) rates between excited states with the same and different spin projections -- a necessary condition for nonzero ODMR response. The lowest-cost approach evaluates whether the evolution of an $S=0$ state under the spin-orbit coupling induces ISC to $S=1$, and also whether there is an imbalance in its intensity depending on the final state spin projection. The second approach works by comparing the emission spectrum of a spin defect with and without the spin-orbit coupling operator, inferring ISC intensity for different spin transition channels from spectrum intensity changes. Additionally, we present an improved scheme to evaluate the defect's optical response, building upon previous work. We study these quantum algorithms in the context of the negatively charged boron vacancy in hexagonal boron nitride. We generate an embedded active space of 18 spatial orbitals using quantum defect embedding theory (QDET) and show that the ISC rate imbalance can be detected with as few as 105 logical qubits and $4.41 \times 10^8$ Toffoli gates. By avoiding direct and costly rate calculations, our methods enable faster screening of candidate defects for ODMR activity, advancing the prospect of using quantum simulations to aid the development of high-performing sensing devices.

authors.name: Pablo A. M. Casares, Yanbing Zhou, Utkarsh Azad, Stepan Fomichev, Jack S. Baker, Chen Ling, Debasish Banerjee, Alain Delgado, Juan Miguel Arrazola

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Hermitian Special Functions and Dynamics via Contour-based Matrix Decomposition
papers.summary: Simulating non-Hermitian dynamics on quantum computers is often hindered by the decay of success probability and the instability of non-diagonalizable matrices. Here, we present contour-based matrix decomposition (CBMD), a rigorous and versatile quantum functional calculus framework for simulating non-Hermitian matrix functions. By generalizing the matrix Cauchy residue theorem, CBMD decomposes holomorphic non-Hermitian operators into an analytic infinite contour-residue identity, followed by finite truncation with controlled error to yield linear combinations of Hermitian components. For first-order dynamics, CBMD achieves optimal query complexity across all parameters, strictly matching the optimal performance bounds within the linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) paradigm. Beyond first-order systems, the framework naturally generalizes to complex operator functions, including second-order wave dynamics and non-Hermitian special functions such as Bessel and Airy evolutions. Furthermore, CBMD systematically suppresses the asymptotic growth of non-Hermitian components, yielding a significant reduction in the required number of amplitude amplifications compared to the naive scheme of combining monomials via linear combination of unitaries (LCU) after Taylor expansion. Notably, CBMD avoids explicit dependence on matrix diagonalizability, effectively mitigating the long-standing challenges associated with ill-conditioned eigenvectors and Jordan blocks. Our work establishes a systematic matrix calculus that bridges high-performance classical numerics and fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. It should be noted that CBMD inherits standard LCU overheads, and requires the target function to have a bounded growth order on the real axis.

authors.name: Chao Wang, Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Menghan Dou, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo

papers.title: Semi-device-independent channel identification with communication matrices
papers.summary: We look into the task of differentiating between any two quantum channels and reconstructing them from the obtained measurement statistics with possibly limited information about the experimental set-up. We employ the communication matrix formalism where the measurement statistics of a prepare-and-measure scenario is represented as a stochastic communication matrix. In order to differentiate between any two quantum channels, the informational completeness of the set-up is both necessary and sufficient. On the other hand, if we want to uniquely characterize any quantum channel, in addition we also need to have a complete description of the set-up. We show that in many important cases we can deduce this information directly from the communication matrix of the set-up before applying the channel. Given that we trust the dimension of the system, we show that we can deduce the information completeness of the set-up directly from the rank of the communication matrix. Furthermore, we show that another quantity of the communication matrix, called the information storability, can be used to self-test the set-up (up to unitary or antiunitary freedom) for an important class of states and measurements. This provides us a semi-device-independent way to identify quantum channels from the prepare-and-measure statistics. Lastly, we consider scenarios where we might have some additional information about the channels or additional resources at our disposal which could help us relax some of the assumptions of the proposed scenario.

authors.name: Samgeeth Puliyil, Leevi Lepp\"aj\"arvi, M\'ario Ziman

papers.title: Fully quantum algorithmic framework for partial differential equation-constrained optimization
papers.summary: Partial differential equation (PDE)-constrained optimization, where an optimization problem is subject to PDE constraints, arises in various applications such as design, control, and inference. Solving such problems is computationally demanding because it requires repeatedly solving a PDE and using its solution within an optimization process. In this paper, we first propose a fully quantum algorithmic framework for solving PDE-constrained optimization problems. The proposed method combines a quantum PDE solver that prepares the solution vector as a quantum state, and a quantum optimizer that assumes oracle access to a quantized objective function. The central idea is the explicit construction of the oracle in a form of block-encoding for the objective function, which coherently uses the output of a quantum PDE solver. This enables us to avoid classical access to the full solution that requires quantum state tomography canceling out the potential quantum speedups. We also derive the overall computational complexity of the proposed method with respect to parameters for optimization and PDE simulation, where quantum speedup is inherited from the underlying quantum PDE solver. We numerically demonstrate the validity of the proposed method by applications, including a parameter calibration problem in the Black-Scholes equation and a material parameter design problem in the wave equation. This work presents the concept of composing quantum subroutines so that the weakness of one (i.e., prohibitive readout overhead) is neutralized by the strength of another (i.e., coherent oracle access), toward a bottleneck-free quantum algorithm.

authors.name: Yuki Sato, Jumpei Kato, Hiroshi Yano, Kosuke Ito, Naoki Yamamoto

papers.title: Simulating Gaussian boson sampling on graphs in polynomial time
papers.summary: We show that a distribution related to Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) on graphs can be sampled classically in polynomial time. Graphical applications of GBS typically sample from this distribution, and thus quantum algorithms do not provide exponential speedup for these applications. We also show that another distribution related to Boson sampling can be sampled classically in polynomial time.

authors.name: Konrad Anand, Zongchen Chen, Mary Cryan, Graham Freifeld, Leslie Ann Goldberg, Heng Guo, Xinyuan Zhang

papers.title: Enhancing Long-distance Continuous-variable Quantum-key-distribution with an Error-correcting Relay
papers.summary: Noiseless linear amplifiers (NLAs) serve as an effective means to enable long-distance continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD), even under realistic conditions with non-unit reconciliation efficiency. Separately, unitary averaging has been suggested to mitigate some stochastic noise, including phase noise in continuous-variable states. In this work, we combine these two protocols to simultaneously compensate for thermal-loss effects and suppress phase noise, thereby enabling long-distance CV QKD that surpasses the repeaterless bound, the fundamental rate-distance limit, for repeaterless quantum communication systems.

authors.name: S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, Timothy C. Ralph

papers.title: Quantitative Universal Approximation for Noisy Quantum Neural Networks
papers.summary: We prove a quantitative universal approximation theorem for noisy quantum neural networks (QNNs), with explicit non-asymptotic error bounds in terms of the number of accuracy blocks, the qubit count, the number of two-qubit gates, and hardware noise parameters. Motivated by quantitative finance, where target functions are expectations of payoffs, we first extend existing noiseless bounds to expectation functions and derive explicit constants for exponential Levy models, covering the Black-Scholes price of (truncated) European Put options. We then formulate the noisy circuit via quantum channels, obtain a fidelity-based bound for general noise models, and specialise to depolarising noise with readout error, calibrated to real hardware. Finally, we provide a detailed numerical analysis for option pricing in the Black-Scholes model, testing our results on actual noisy quantum hardware.

authors.name: Lukas Gonon, Antoine Jacquier, Marcel Mordarski

papers.title: Low-rank geometry of two-qubit gates
papers.summary: We present a framework based on the determinantal geometry of two-qubit gates. Combining the Weyl chamber representation with operator Schmidt theory, we interpret gate synthesis as a distance problem to determinantal varieties. This gives an operational geometry to the Weyl chamber, quantifying nonlocal complexity. We show that the square root of iSWAP gate is the closest perfect entangler to the variety of local operations, and that no perfect entangler can be approximated by a local gate with average gate fidelity above 78.3%. The three different determinantal costs form a synthesis-adapted coordinate system that encodes nonlocal complexity and generally reconstruct the Weyl coordinates in the reduced sector.

authors.name: Lloren\c{c} Balada Gaggioli

papers.title: Multi-Objective Optimization with Quantum-Annealing-Inspired Algorithms
papers.summary: Combinatorial optimization is widely regarded as a primary application for near-term quantum processors, although a definitive demonstration of a practical quantum advantage remains elusive. Recent studies have reported that both gate-based quantum circuits and quantum annealers can outperform state-of-the-art classical heuristics on multi-objective optimization (MO-MaxCut) problems. However, these studies did not fully account for the substantial pre- and postprocessing overheads intrinsic to quantum solvers, leading to incomplete comparisons between quantum and classical approaches. In this work, we re-examine the same benchmark suite using GPU-based quantum-annealing-inspired algorithms (QAIAs), which generate probabilistic samples analogously to quantum processors and thus serve as formidable classical contenders. Our results show that QAIAs can sample candidate solutions approximately two orders of magnitude faster than the previously studied quantum processors, based on the reported sampling and device-access times. On the instances for which a complete pipeline can be compared, the measured end-to-end QAIA runtime, including model construction, sampling and Pareto filtering, is about an order of magnitude shorter than that of the exact objective-space baselines DCM and DPA-a, and the QAIA pipeline outperforms the tested evolutionary multi-objective heuristics under an equal wall-clock budget.

authors.name: Xian-Zhe Tao, Pavel Mosharev, Zhaofeng Su, Man-Hong Yung

papers.title: Sub-shot-noise emission statistics of a CW-excited single photon source
papers.summary: Shot noise sets a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of classical optical measurements, with coherent emitters achieving the lowest possible shot-noise level. Emission from sub-Poissonian light provides a pathway to surpass this limit, and single-photon sources provide a natural platform for generating such light. However, it is commonly assumed that off-resonance continuously excited solid-state single-photon sources exhibit Poissonian statistics over large exposure periods, owing to their strong coupling to the host lattice. In this work, a theoretical model of a continuously driven two-level single-photon source is developed, treating both excitation and radiative decay as stochastic processes. The analysis demonstrates that photon emission can display sub-Poissonian statistics when excitation and decay rates are comparable, showing that continuous excitation does not inherently preclude nonclassical emission. The model is further extended to include finite detection efficiency and detector dead time, illustrating how these practical non-idealities can affect the experimental observation of sub-Poissonian statistics.

authors.name: G. Gavello, G. Petrini, I. Ruo Berchera, M. Gramegna, E. Moreva, P. Traina, M. Ziino, M. Genovese, P. Olivero, J. Forneris, I. P. Degiovanni

papers.title: Complementary quantum and classical records of qubit decoherence
papers.summary: Decoherence is usually viewed as the loss of local coherence, but it also writes information into the environment. Here we examine two complementary forms of this information. One is a recoverable quantum record: conditioning on a transverse qubit measurement reveals a Schr\"odinger-cat-like state in an occupation-selected collective bath mode. The other is a redundant classical which-path record distributed across physical frequency-band fragments. Using tensor-network simulations of the spin--boson model, we reconstruct the conditional bath Wigner function and resolve its negativity. At zero temperature, one natural orbital carries more than $97\%$ of the bath one-body occupation in the chain representation. For an initial $\ket{+x}$ qubit and a pure parity-even bath, a symmetry gives an exact nonperturbative identity between the remaining qubit coherence and the overlap of the two environmental branches. Exact pure-dephasing calculations establish both conditional nonclassicality and redundant pointer information in the same system--bath state. With tunneling, a detector that excludes frequencies below $0.1\omega_c$ resolves transient conditional negativity at the simulated temperatures $T/\omega_0=0.3,0.5,0.7,1$; its suppression reflects both uncollected modes and thermal effects. In pure dephasing, the conditional state of the displacement-matched mode is an exact thermal mixture of displaced cat states. These results connect decoherence to phase-space tomography and motivate a readout combining qubit measurement and collective-mode Wigner tomography.

authors.name: Jargalsaikhan Artag, Koki Awaya, Takumi Kanezashi, Haruya Nagata, Daisuke Tsukayama, Moe Shimada, Jun-ichi Shirakashi

papers.title: Classical Stochasticity Using Quantum Computers
papers.summary: We demonstrate that quantum algorithms can be used to model classical stochastic simulations as the measurement process is inherently random. To illustrate, we solve the classical Lorenz system with stochastic behavior using a Python random number generator. We compare the classical stochastic Lorenz system with the measured output of the quantum algorithm.

authors.name: Diego Campos, Narasimha Reddy Gosala, Arundhati Dasgupta

papers.title: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA for Joint Anomaly-Feature Selection
papers.summary: Selecting anomalous samples and explanatory features under fixed cardinalities defines a coupled optimization problem: feature-first selection can overlook features whose usefulness depends on the selected samples. In the analyzed model, joint calibration-error sensitivity is sample-count independent, while the sum-column feature-first rule's sensitivity grows linearly. To optimize this formulation, we introduce Coupling-Grouped XY Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CG-XY-QAOA), with constraint-preserving mixers and block-structured phase angles. On matched sparse IBM Heron R3 circuits, our implementation reduces circuit depth by 35.1%-54.8% against Qiskit's optimization-level 3 preset pass manager on the CZ-basis target and enables runs at 64 decision qubits (p=2) and 36 (p=3). At 20 decision qubits (p=5), fully grouped angles raise the fixed low-energy hit probability 25-fold to 3.7%, with 64.7% of measured samples satisfying both constraints. Benchmarks favor joint selection when feature usefulness varies across anomalies. Noiseless simulations show problem-structured grouping improves over same-depth XY-QAOA and parameter-matched type-preserving randomizations.

authors.name: Pauli Taipale

papers.title: Imperceptible measurement deviations can fake high-dimensional entanglement
papers.summary: Quantum entanglement is a central resource for emerging quantum technologies, but its experimental certification usually assumes that prescribed quantum measurements can be realized exactly. This assumption becomes increasingly restrictive in high-dimensional systems, where accurate measurement control is more challenging. Here, we show that arbitrarily small, adversarially tailored measurement deviations can lead to the false certification of high-dimensional entanglement in systems that are, in fact, separable, with the effect becoming increasingly severe as the dimension grows. We experimentally demonstrate this across a broad range of dimensions using classical photonic states encoded in the spatial degree of freedom. We report false certification of several tens of entangled dimensions in systems spanning up to 61 dimensions while exploiting measurement deviations as low as 0.23%. Our results reveal how imperceptible invasive attacks can critically compromise high-dimensional entanglement certification, motivating the development of new certification methods robust to bounded discrepancies between theory and experiment.

authors.name: Jaime Moreno, Elna Svegborn, Simon Morelli, Markus Hiekkam\"aaki, Lea Kopf, Robert Fickler, Armin Tavakoli

papers.title: On the generic structures of the protocols for quantum auction and quantum summation and their relation
papers.summary: Secure multi-party computation (SMC) addresses the problem of jointly computing global functions of private inputs while revealing minimal information about individual data. Two prominent examples of SMC tasks are sealed-bid auction and secure multi-party summation. Existing schemes for quantum auction and quantum summation have largely been developed independently, motivated by distinct applications and employing different computational primitives. In this work, mutual reductions between the two tasks are established for single-item sealed-bid auctions with first-price payment. In one direction, an auction used as a black box computes a secure sum: each party bids a private random key drawn from its input, so the clearing price depends on the inputs only through their sum $S$. The reduction is perfectly private against colluding semi-honest parties and uses $O(S^2\log(1/\delta))$ auction rounds, which is optimal, or $O(S\log(1/\delta))$ under coherent access. It can be instantiated with an existing auctioneer-free quantum auction after a one-line change to its disjunction subroutine, which as published leaks occupancy counts. In the other direction, summation with randomized inputs yields threshold disjunctions, and a single search over composite keys locates the highest bid and a winner, revealing nothing else. Because each query consumes the bidders' encodings, a bidder can adapt its effective bid undetected, while a fixed query set restores sealed bidding. Combinatorial auctions and general payment rules lie outside this framework. On a superconducting processor, one instance of each direction is executed, recovering the winner for four-bidder instances with ties and the sum of private inputs from repeated auctions.

authors.name: Kabir Sandhu, Sandeep Mishra, Anirban Pathak

papers.title: Controlling Waiting Time Statistics in Monitored Collective Spins: Mitigating Detector's Resolution Barrier in Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions
papers.summary: In collective dissipative spin systems, the postselection barrier can be partially mitigated; however, a further obstacle may be posed by the finite temporal resolution of detectors. In this work, we investigate how initial-state inhomogeneities can control waiting-time statistics between quantum jumps, thereby mitigating the detector-resolution problem. We consider a collectively monitored spin model with a boundary time-crystalline phase, introducing inhomogeneity by partitioning the ensemble into two subsystems rotated by an angle $\theta$. We find that the measurement-induced phase transition survives under inhomogeneities, with different entanglement scaling regimes. The waiting time increases with $\theta$, scaling as $1/N$ but with a prefactor strongly enhanced by orders of magnitude, and in the anti-aligned limit $\theta = \pi$ it remains finite, fully resolving the resolution barrier. This mitigation, however, comes at a cost: the entanglement saturation time becomes significantly longer, partially reintroducing the postselection barrier. Our results highlight a trade-off between detector resolution and postselection overhead, with direct implications for the experimental observation of measurement-induced phenomena.

authors.name: Tanbir Islam, Fernando Iemini

papers.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
papers.summary: Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum $XY$ model and the interacting disordered $XXZ$ chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.

authors.name: Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Yun-Jie Wang, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Chao Wang, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo

papers.title: Transferred QAOA Parameters Remember the Penalty Scale: A $\lambda$-Resonance Law for Constrained Quantum Optimization
papers.summary: Training the variational angles of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm once on a small instance and reusing them on larger ones, known as parameter transfer, is the standard route past the exact-simulation wall. Existing literature explains its success almost entirely through structural similarity. We identify a new, independent axis that governs transfer whenever constraints are encoded as penalties: the trained angles memorize the penalty weight $\lambda$ of their training instance. For any scalarized cost function with an integer-valued violation count, we prove that at arbitrary fixed QAOA angles $(\beta,\gamma)$ of depth $p$, the probability mass $F(\lambda)$ on the feasible subspace is a finite real trigonometric polynomial in $\lambda$ whose angular frequencies lie on an integer lattice generated by the trained $\gamma$'s. Three consequences follow immediately: transfer feasibility is a resonance peaked where the deployment penalty matches the training penalty; the resonance width scales as $1/(v_{max}\sum_k|\gamma_k|)$, so low-$|\gamma|$ angle sets are systematically more transferable; and the curve exhibits revival peaks at spacings $2\pi/\gamma_k$. We confirm all three predictions by exact statevector experiments on a 20-qubit multi-user resource-allocation QUBO. The theorem is independent of how the angles were obtained and applies to any integer-penalty QUBO, recasting a widely reported failure mode of penalty-based QAOA as deterministic, predictable phase interference rather than an energetic tuning problem.

authors.name: Krit Grover

papers.title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
papers.summary: We give an unconditional construction of information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption for one-bit messages, with efficient encryption and decryption and exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage. Previous work by Bhattacharyya and Culf (Nature Physics, 2026) and Bhattacharyya, Broadbent, and Culf (arXiv:2603.08916) either only showed inverse-polynomial security loss or required inefficient encryption/decryption operations; we avoid both of these caveats. Our scheme's key is a uniformly random non-identity phase-free Pauli on $n$ qubits, and bit $a$ is encrypted as a random $(-1)^a$ eigenstate of that Pauli. We prove that the probability that both receivers recover the bit is at most $1/2 + O\left(2^{-n/2}\right).$ By a lower bound due to Broadbent, Culf, and Rochette (IACR Communications in Cryptology, 2026), this is the best probability bound achievable with $n$-qubit ciphertexts while ensuring perfect correctness (up to the constant hidden in the $O(\cdot)$).

authors.name: Prabhanjan Ananth, Seyoon Ragavan, Amit Sahai

papers.title: A Kernel-Based Density of States Estimator for Quantum Computing
papers.summary: We introduce a quantum kernel method for estimating the density of states (DoS) of quantum many-body systems. The method exploits the Rodeo algorithm as a physical implementation, requiring no modification of its standard single-ancilla circuit. Averaging the Rodeo response over Haar-random input states reconstructs the DoS convolved with a spectral kernel whose analytical form is determined entirely by the probability distribution of the sampled evolution times. This establishes a direct quantum analogue of the classical Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM): Haar-random states perform stochastic trace estimation, while the temporal sampling distribution plays the role of the reconstruction kernel. We derive the estimator, quantify its statistical and systematic uncertainties, and establish an explicit correspondence between quantum reconstruction kernels and classical signal-processing window functions, enabling concepts such as spectral leakage, side-lobe attenuation, and main-lobe width to guide kernel design. The method is validated numerically on the one-dimensional transverse-field spin--$\sfrac{1}{2}$ and spin--$1$ Ising models, where the reconstructed density of states and the resulting thermodynamic observables agree with exact diagonalization within the estimated statistical uncertainties.

authors.name: Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha

papers.title: Best Annealing Path of Simulated Quantum Annealing via Efficient Adiabatic Phase Transition
papers.summary: Nested Simulated Annealing (NSA) is proposed for accelerating the classical simulation of Quantum Annealing (QA). NSA is based on two-spin interaction and exploits the causality of spin-flip, thereby significantly reducing computational cost. And through Unitary Coupled-Cluster (UCC) method, I establish a connection between NSA and XX interaction which is one of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians and demonstrate that NSA effectively utilizes a trivial degenerate state. Furthermore, by treating spins as continuous variables, I derive an energy formulation that incorporates both the problem Hamiltonian and the perturbation Hamiltonian induced by transverse electromagnetic field and show that the annealing path characterized by the lowest local-maximum exhibits the fastest convergence. Based on the result, I present a strategy for finding optimal annealing parameters for Simulated Quantum Annealing (SQA).

authors.name: Kiyotaka Murashima

papers.title: Multimode squeezed light generation and characterization
papers.summary: Nowadays, the realization of quantum computations and communications based on continuous variables has attracted significant attention due to a substantial expansion of the system dimensionality. The main progress in this area is attributed to the implementation of multimode systems based on squeezed states of light. One of the simplest ways to generate such states relies upon their producing in a single-pass optical parametric amplifier (OPA) under ultrafast pumping. However, for homodyne detection of such multimode states, the profile of the local oscillator (LO) must perfectly match the profile of the measured mode. Usually, this is not the case; therefore, a proper treatment of multimode squeezing is required. In this work, we study both theoretically and experimentally the multimode squeezed light generated in type-0 and type-II OPA. We characterize such sources using the Schmidt-mode representation and investigate the degree of squeezing depending on the LO spectral profile, employing a pulse shaping technique. In addition, we investigate cluster states that can be generated under the given experimental conditions. This work might have a significant impact on the realization of multimode quantum protocols.

authors.name: Alexander Chudakov, Vladislav Severin, Anastasia Poshevkina, Danil Malyshev, Kirill Kuznetsov, Olga Tikhonova, Dmitry Kalashnikov, Polina R. Sharapova

papers.title: qdmag: A Python package for simulating nonequilibrium magnetization of molecules using quantum master equations
papers.summary: We present qdmag, a computational utility for calculating the magnetization of magnetic molecules in a time-varying external magnetic field by solving a generalized Lindblad quantum master equation with spin-phonon coupling treated as a dissipation term. The package relies on the spin Hamiltonian formalism, which includes both the magnetic exchange interactions and the zero-field splitting (ZFS) interaction. Different types of magnetic exchange interaction and ZFS terms up to 12th order, which are written in terms of the extended Stevens operators, are supported. qdmag enables long-time evolution of magnetization for up to a few milliseconds, which is achieved through a staircase approximation of the magnetic field as a function of time. For high-dimensional spin Hamiltonians, a lower-dimensional effective Hamiltonian is constructed to make the calculations computationally feasible. Three case studies of one-spin, two-spin, and three-spin systems are presented to demonstrate the usage of qdmag. Our work offers a computational tool to bridge the gap between theoretical development and numerical calculations of spin dynamics in the presence of spin-phonon coupling.

authors.name: Shuanglong Liu, Xiao Chen, Andrew Cupo, James N. Fry, Hai-Ping Cheng

papers.title: Entangled measurements are necessary for optimal tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states and of bosonic Gaussian states near the vacuum
papers.summary: We prove that learning an unknown mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes to trace distance $\epsilon$ requires $\Omega(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies when measurements act on one copy at a time, even with arbitrary POVMs, fresh ancillas and classical adaptivity, but without quantum memory between copies. The bound holds for $0<\epsilon\le1/3600$ and separates this model from the known collective rate $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. It follows from a uniform single-copy Fisher-information budget and a dimension-independent comparison between trace distance and Gaussian parameters. On covariance matrices of operator norm at most $1-c$, we prove a Frobenius-to-trace-norm continuity bound with constant $[2c(2-c)]^{-1/2}$; matchgate shadows then attain $O(m^3/(c\epsilon^2))$ copies. This also gives explicit error certificates for thermal free-fermion states. For a class of mixed passive bosonic Gaussian states with total mean photon number at most one, a reduction to bounded-block qudit tomography gives a single-copy lower bound $\Omega(m^3/(\epsilon^2\sqrt{\log(m/\epsilon)}))$, versus collective complexity $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. These separations answer the mixed-state measurement-resource question posed by Chen et al. A two-mode example has optimal two-copy Fisher trace $5$, versus the separable ceiling $4$. An IBM replication gave a pre-registered witness lower bound $4.12$ at one-sided $95\%$ shot-noise confidence; its interpretation assumes the prescribed preparations and a common measurement channel and does not bound preparation systematics.

authors.name: Ron Rubin (Rubin Anders Scientific, Inc.)

papers.title: Quantum error mitigation from information dynamics
papers.summary: Overcoming experimental errors is a central challenge in quantum science. This challenge is particularly acute in large and complex quantum circuits, where quantum information spreads into exponentially many paths, foiling any direct attempt to understand errors' impact. In this work, we present a novel approach to understanding and mitigating experimental errors, based on a surprisingly compact representation of a quantum circuit's information dynamics, the reactivity function. The shape of a circuit's reactivity function governs its noise response, and its amenability to different error mitigation methods. From this viewpoint, we introduce two complementary such methods. The first, Pauli-path zero-noise extrapolation, fits a parameterized model to a circuit's reactivity function and uses it to accurately extrapolate to zero noise. The second, tunable error cancellation, filters a circuit's reactivity function to cancel noise on all information up to a threshold locality. Crucially, both methods feature a tuning parameter that allows one to systematically improve their accuracy until convergence. Across three circuit families from published experiments, our methods overcome conventional zero-noise extrapolation biases as large as 30%; at $\sim$$10^{-2}$ root-mean-square error, they reduce sampling cost relative to probabilistic error cancellation by up to a factor of $10^3$.

authors.name: Philippe Suchsland, Thomas Schuster, Manuel S. Rudolph, Nicholas Noll, Thomas E. O'Brien, Zlatko K. Minev

papers.title: Cycle Codes and Decoded Quantum Interferometry
papers.summary: Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) reduces optimization problems with two-variable constraints to decoding cycle codes. For one such problem, namely MaxCut, prior work showed that DQI achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee only on linear-girth graphs, for which MaxCut is classically easy. However, these no-go results rely on minimum distance assumptions that do not represent true decodability thresholds for common noise channels, thus underestimating actual DQI performance. To estimate the true performance, we derive DQI satisfaction guarantees in the presence of imperfect decoding for fixed instances and generalize prior results for random instances. We then study homological cycle codes over arbitrary finite fields and show that minimum-weight decoding is NP-hard for every field of size $q>2$, in contrast with known results for binary cycle codes. On the Linial--Simkin ensemble of regular graphs with logarithmic girth, we prove maximum-likelihood recovery bounds and a strong converse for a family of non-uniform additive noise channels. Moreover, linear programming (LP) decoders provide polynomial-time recovery of a positive fraction of randomly located errors with arbitrary values. These results allow us to prove upper and lower bounds on the approximate optima achievable by DQI when restricted to classical decoders. These bounds rule out quantum advantage in the regimes we analyze but also identify a family of regular Max-$k$-Cut instances on which DQI efficiently achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee.

authors.name: Anuj Apte, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Andi Gu, Stephen P. Jordan, Ojas Parekh, Ruslan Shaydulin, Jacob Watkins, Noureldin Yosri, Adam Zalcman

papers.title: Quantum Algorithms for OPI Variants Beyond Locality and Classical Decodability
papers.summary: Regev's reduction quantumly finds codewords satisfying nonlinear constraints by decoding the dual code. To date, applications that have not been dequantized have relied on efficient classical decoders and coordinate-wise constraints. We overcome these restrictions separately. Our first contribution uses a quantum decoder to find solutions $\mathbf{y}\in(\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\{0\})^m$ to $\mathbf{B}\mathbf{y}=0$, where $\mathbf{B}\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n\times m}$. For fixed prime $q>2$, Chen, Liu, and Zhandry solve this problem for random matrices with $m=\Omega(n^2)$, a regime now covered by classical algorithms. We adapt their template to codes (spanned by the rows of $\mathbf{B}$) that satisfy a "two-fold multiplication property": the coordinate-wise products of pairs of codewords span a space of dimension smaller than $m$. Under suitable distance conditions, this allows us to solve instances with $m\leq n^{2-\Omega(1)}$, beyond the established guarantees of classical algorithms. We also give an efficient classical algorithm under a stronger three-fold multiplication property, leaving intermediate regimes as candidates for quantum advantage. For Reed-Muller codes punctured at random points, our algorithm finds a word in the unpunctured dual code supported exactly on those points. This works beyond known efficient classical decoding regimes. Our second contribution retains classical decoding but allows global constraints on symbol frequencies.
