For the parallel magnetic field, one can see standard Fraunhofer-like $I_c(B)$ suppression pattern. In contrast, $I_c(B)$ is qualitatively different in normal magnetic field, indicating non-trivial distribution of the Josephson current within the junction plane. From this anisotropy, long-range supercurrent and fast aperiodic fluctuations in $I_c(B)$ we conclude that Josephson current is transferred by the chiral surface states, which emerge along the domain walls in topological compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl. The conclusion on the domain walls is supported by magnetization data for small Ti$_2$MnAl flakes.

authors.name: V. D. Esin, N. N. Orlova, A. R. Banschikova, Yu. S. Barash, D. N. Borisenko, N. N. Kolesnikov, E. V. Deviatov

papers.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
papers.summary: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. In a search for phonon-mediated superconductors, density-functional perturbation theory on 45 structurally novel designs gives isotropic Allen-Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39; the highest is 24.0 K for ZrTiNb2CN3, and H4LiPd3 (23.2 K) lies on the static DFT hull. In searches for photovoltaic absorbers, SCAN calculations confirm ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull, and show that the systematic gap error of the training functional propagates into the designs unless the objective corrects for it. Quasiharmonic free energies from machine-learned potentials further show that finite-temperature competition with solid phases can reorder candidates relative to the static hull.

authors.name: Crist\'obal M\'endez, Justin Tahmassebpur, Tom\'as A. Arias

papers.title: Quantum Interference Control of Coupled Atomic Spins
papers.summary: We propose a protocol for the non-resonant electric control of quantum states in atomic-scale spin systems using Landau-Zener-St\"uckelberg-Majorana (LZSM) interferometry. We focus on a Ti-Ti-Fe trimer on a thin MgO layer, a platform that has recently emerged as a promising candidate for qubit realization using electron spin resonance combined with scanning tunneling microscopy (ESR-STM). We first analyze a Ti dimer in the absence of the Fe atom and show, through a detailed spectroscopic study, that avoided level crossings can be engineered by combining the in-plane component of the external magnetic field, the tip magnetic field, and the applied bias voltage, which allows the system to be tuned electrically through these crossings. Based on this, we develop LZSM protocols for coherent state control in the dimer using non-resonant LZSM-STM. We then consider the full trimer, where the Fe atom generates a local magnetic field at the remote Ti atom, enabling non-local spin control. We show that this remote and non-resonant manipulation reduces unwanted effects associated with tunneling electrons and enables quantum operations on short timescales. Our results show that quantum interference can be used as a resource for electrically driven, non-resonant, and non-local spin control in atomic-scale systems. This approach enables fast quantum operations while mitigating decoherence, offering a promising route toward scalable atom-based qubit architectures.

authors.name: Sergio Santiago Gomez, Gustavo Mauricio Meneses Ancalle, Daniel Dom\'inguez, Mar\'ia Jos\'e S\'anchez, Alejandro Ferr\'on

papers.title: Quantum-walk measurements with sequential imaging of the same atomic sample
papers.summary: We demonstrate sequential single-atom-resolved imaging of the same ultracold atomic sample and apply this technique to quantum-walk measurements in an optical lattice. In quantum gas microscope experiments, fluorescence imaging provides microscopic information on atomic distributions but induces motional heating through photon scattering, making it difficult to reuse the same sample for subsequent quantum dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we apply Raman sideband cooling with parameters optimized for post-imaging cooling, enabling sequential single-atom-resolved measurements of the same sample. By optimizing the cooling parameters with machine learning, we achieve high fidelity over multiple imaging cycles. To demonstrate the capability of this technique, we measure one-dimensional quantum walks of single atoms in an optical lattice. By determining the initial atomic positions from fluorescence images, we extract quantum-walk transition probabilities without requiring deterministic preparation of the initial atomic positions. The observed dynamics agree with numerical simulations of quantum walks of single atoms. Our method provides a route toward reducing experimental overhead in quantum gas microscope studies requiring repeated acquisition of spatially resolved correlation data.

authors.name: Ryuta Yamamoto, Takeshi Fukuhara

papers.title: Experimental Evaluation of High-Throughput Structure Predictions
papers.summary: High throughput computational databases such as Materials Project, the Open Quantum Materials Database, and Alexandria now each list on the order of 10^5 predicted stable compounds. However, the overall reliability of these predictions in terms of actual experimental synthesizability remains poorly understood. In this work we attempt to synthesize, via arc melting, 34 different predicted ternary compounds. The majority of these materials did not form in the predicted structure, instead resulting in disordered variants or multiphase mixtures. Four formed ordered structures not reported before, one of them at a composition reported earlier without a structure. We discuss both the failures and the successes, and identify simple filtering criteria that can help researchers avoid hypothetical materials that are unlikely to form.

authors.name: Gabriele D. Di Gianluca, James Grossmann, Jackson Niedel, Juan Esquivel, Molly Crossman, Tyler Miniati, Melchior Jean, Zhongwei Li, Pawan Prakash, Andrew Valentini, Jung Soo Kim, Benjamin Geisler, Richard G. Hennig, Peter J. Hirschfeld, Gregory R. Stewart, James J. Hamlin

papers.title: Theory of Optical and Magneto-Optical Properties of [111]-Oriented Site-Controlled Quantum Dots
papers.summary: Site-controlled [111]-oriented quantum dots (QDs) are promising sources of non-classical light, yet their optical spectra exhibit apparently conflicting symmetry signatures. At zero magnetic field, excitonic spectra are commonly interpreted as $C_{2v}$-like, whereas measurements in Faraday geometry display selection rules characteristic of $C_{3v}$-like symmetry. Here, we show that both regimes can be described consistently without invoking any change in the underlying structural symmetry. Combining 8-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ theory, a self-consistent Hartree-informed configuration interaction scheme, and group theoretical analysis, we introduce a controlled symmetry reducing perturbation that lowers the QD symmetry to $C_s$. At zero field, the optical response remains predominantly $C_{2v}$-like because the additional low-symmetry transitions carry only weak oscillator strengths. In Faraday geometry, the same reduced-symmetry structure produces four dominant, nearly circularly polarised trion transitions, reproducing the experimentally observed $C_{3v}$-like response. By contrast, an exact $C_{2v}$ description inferred from the zero-field spectrum permits only two such trion transitions and therefore fails at finite field. Our results thus provide a unified description of the zero and finite magnetic field optical response without any restoration or enhancement of the underlying structural symmetry. More generally, we demonstrate that a higher-symmetry-like optical spectrum does not uniquely identify the exact symmetry of a QD, therefore also providing useful guidance for other QD and nanostructure systems that lie beyond the ones studied here.

authors.name: N. D. O'Connor, G. Juska, E. Pelucchi, S. Schulz

papers.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
papers.summary: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. Because the trap moves with the skyrmion, excitons can be transported by current pulses, and small skyrmions accommodate a single exciton, which opens the door for potential hybrid applications in future information technology intertwining topological magnetic bits with optical excitations.

authors.name: Karim Rezouali, Selcuk S\"ozeri, Samir Lounis

papers.title: Reversible Interchain Associations Dominate Plateau Elasticity in Conjugated Polymers
papers.summary: The modulus plateau is widely regarded as a hallmark of topological entanglement in homopolymer melts and has been used to identify entanglement in semiflexible conjugated polymers. Using regiorandom poly(3-alkylthiophenes) as a model system, we show that their plateau elasticity relaxes through an Arrhenius process decoupled from segmental and terminal dynamics, reorganizes persistently under mechanical perturbation, and varies systematically with side-chain length. These behaviors are hard to reconcile with a purely topological-entanglement picture and instead support a transient network dominated by reversible interchain associations, consistent with {\pi}-{\pi} interactions between conjugated backbone segments. The results thus demonstrate that plateau elasticity alone does not uniquely identify topological entanglement in conjugated polymers. More broadly, they identify the strength and lifetime of interchain association as molecular design parameters linking backbone packing to stress relaxation, viscoelastic properties, and processability in conjugated polymers, complementing their established role in electronic structure and charge transport.

authors.name: Juncheng Zheng, Xiaobing Zuo, Xiaodan Gu, Shiwang Cheng

papers.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
papers.summary: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. Applying this model to $1s$ acoustic polarons in an MoSe$_2$ monolayer, we reveal a distinct kink in the polaron dispersion, accompanied by a pronounced broadening of its spectral function. These spectral signatures mark a critical transition from a regime of well-defined bound exciton polarons, characterized by a renormalized energy, reduced group velocity, and enhanced effective mass, to a regime dominated by exciton-phonon scattering. Furthermore, by incorporating intervalley exciton-phonon interaction, we demonstrate that the energetic position of momentum-dark excitons strongly modifies the exciton-polaron lifetime. Overall, our work provides a microscopic framework for determining renormalized properties of exciton polarons and establishes experimentally accessible polaron signatures in 2D semiconductors.

authors.name: Carlos Maciel-Escudero, Giuseppe Meneghini, Jamie M. Fitzgerald, Ermin Malic

papers.title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
papers.summary: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.

authors.name: Henry Amir, Jack Zwettler, Ka Ho Wong, Genda Gu, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jorge Noronha, Dirk K. Morr, Fahad Mahmood

papers.title: Unraveling square and kagome lattice frustrated magnetism by scalable tensor networks
papers.summary: We extend the scalability of variational infinite two-dimensional tensor network methods with application to investigate frustrated magnetism of the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model and kagome-lattice Heisenberg model. In the sign-problem-free limit of the square-lattice model, we achieve high ground-state energy precision comparable to quantum Monte Carlo methods. With no obstruction beyond this limit, our method obtains direct estimates of order parameters. For the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model, we determine isotropic plaquette order in the valence-bond solid region. For the model near $J_2/J_1=0.5$, and the kagome lattice Heisenberg model, our data indicate linear-dispersion gapless states. To probe the candidate spin-liquid nature of the highly frustrated cases, we go beyond inferring the absence of symmetry-breaking orders and analyze susceptibilities that characterize gapless spin liquids. By estimating scaling dimensions, our data indicate a stable gapless spin liquid on the kagome lattice, and competing scenarios for the intermediate regime of the square-lattice model. Our developments include parallelization and randomized low-rank methods and largely expand the frontier of high-precision variational numerics for quantum phases of matter.

authors.name: Xing-Yu Zhang, Jutho Haegeman, Yuchi He

papers.title: All Symmetries and Boundaries of the Two-Dimensional Free Scalar from Continuous Flat-Gauging
papers.summary: We propose a remote detectability criterion for two-dimensional conformal field theories, which asserts that any local operator outside of the product of the left- and right-moving Virasoro algebras can be detected by some topological line defect. We discuss its relationship to existing results in the conformal net literature. We then use this criterion to argue that the known $SU(2)$ moduli space of unitary conformal boundary conditions and the $SO(4)$ moduli space of unitary topological line defects of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model completely capture all unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological lines of the theory. Invoking the fact that the non-compact boson conformal field theory can be obtained from $SU(2)_1$ by "flat-gauging" a $U(1)$ symmetry, we are also able to completely classify the unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological line defects of the two-dimensional free scalar field. In particular, we find a 4-dimensional moduli space of topological line defects, most of which were not known previously. We support our proposed classifications by writing down concrete Lagrangian descriptions of all of the boundaries and lines of the non-compact boson. For every boundary condition, we calculate the corresponding boundary state, and for each pair of boundary conditions, we calculate the corresponding interval Hilbert space. We verify that the annulus partition functions of the theory respect open/closed duality. We also calculate the fusion rules of the topological line defects, their action on local operators, their action on the boundary conditions by parallel fusion, and their corresponding twisted-sector Hilbert spaces.

authors.name: Yichul Choi, Ho Tat Lam, Brandon C. Rayhaun

papers.title: Continuum mean-field theory of spatiotemporal pattern formation in a three-state active Potts model
papers.summary: We investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of a three-state active Potts model with a cyclic transition bias. Starting from microscopic Glauber-type dynamics, we derive macroscopic continuum field equations through a spatial mean-field approximation. Linear stability and weakly nonlinear analyses reveal that increasing the coupling strength induces a Hopf bifurcation, near which the critical amplitude dynamics is described by the complex Ginzburg--Landau equation. In the spatially homogeneous limit, the system exhibits limit-cycle oscillations and ordered states, with an intermediate regime of bistability bounded by a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric heteroclinic bifurcation. In two dimensions, the system sustains stable rotating spiral waves. Using perturbation theory based on one-dimensional traveling fronts, we semianalytically predict the curvature-dependent propagation velocity of circular fronts, as well as the rotational angular velocity and pitch of spiral waves. Finally, we compare the continuum model with discrete Monte Carlo simulations to clarify the role of thermal fluctuations and evaluate the validity of the mean-field approximation.

authors.name: Yuta Tateyama, Songhao Yin, Hiroaki Ito, Hiroyuki Kitahata, Hiroshi Noguchi

papers.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
papers.summary: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

authors.name: Sergey Matveev

papers.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
papers.summary: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions. Using numerical simulations, we show how parameters such as the size of the system, the average degree of the nodes and the strength of the interactions alter the behaviour of the transition to synchronization with respect to the known theoretical results that are derived for globally coupled infinite systems.

authors.name: Abhishek Sharma, Ayushi Suman, Mehernaz Anvari, Manish Dev Shrimali, Charo I. del Genio, Sarika Jalan

papers.title: Indirect optical manipulation of the antiferromagnetic order of insulating NiO by ultrafast interfacial energy transfer
papers.summary: We report the ultrafast, (sub)picosecond reduction of the antiferromagnetic order of the insulating NiO thin film in a Pt/NiO bilayer. This reduction of the antiferromagnetic order is not present in pure NiO thin films after a strong optical excitation. This ultrafast phenomenon is attributed to an ultrafast and highly efficient energy transfer from the optically excited electron system of the Pt layer into the NiO spin system. We propose that this energy transfer is mediated by a stochastic exchange scattering of hot Pt electrons at the Pt/NiO interface.

authors.name: Stephan Wust, Christopher Seibel, Hendrik Meer, Paul Herrgen, Christin Schmitt, Lorenzo Baldrati, Rafael Ramos, Takashi Kikkawa, Eiji Saitoh, Olena Gomonay, Yuriy Mokrousov, Hans Christian Schneider, Mathias Kl\"aui, Baerbel Rethfeld, Benjamin Stadtm\"uller, Martin Aeschlimann

papers.title: Numerical investigation of the equilibrium Kauzmann transition in a two-dimensional atomistic glass
papers.summary: Dense liquids gradually transform into non-equilibrium amorphous solids as they pass through the experimental glass transition. Experimentally, ergodicity is lost because measurements are conducted within a finite time window. More than seventy years ago, Kauzmann posed a fundamental question: If experiments could run indefinitely, would there exist a critical temperature at which an ergodicity-breaking phase transition occurs? Random first-order transitions represent the modern theoretical framework for this idea. However, theoretical calculations in finite dimensions are challenging, whereas experimental and numerical limitations on accessible timescales hinder direct observation of the putative Kauzmann transition. Here, we overcome this longstanding barrier by developing a computational strategy that properly combines three Monte Carlo methods to access the desired equilibrium thermodynamic properties of a two-dimensional atomistic glass-former down to zero temperature across a range of system sizes up to 77 particles. This enables us to directly measure thermodynamic and structural observables that provide unambiguous evidence that the system undergoes a finite-size version of the Kauzmann transition at a temperature that is much lower than other energy scales and decreases rapidly with system size, thus suggesting the existence of a zero-temperature Kauzmann transition for two-dimensional glasses. The transition is towards an ideal glass state characterized by a complex energy landscape and a hierarchical organization of low-lying states.

authors.name: Gerhard Jung, Misaki Ozawa, Giulio Biroli, Ludovic Berthier

papers.title: Dual topology and edge-reconstruction in $\alpha$-Sn
papers.summary: We formulate the tight-binding model for cubic $\alpha$-Sn based on the DFT calculations. In the model, we incorporate a variable bond angle, which allows us to simulate the effect of the in-plane strain. In the bulk, we demonstrate the presence of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological invariant and a non-zero mirror Chern number, making $\alpha$-Sn one of the rare cases where dual topology can be observed. We calculate the topological phase diagram of multi-layer $\alpha$-Sn as a function of strain and number of layers. We find that a non-trivial quantum spin Hall state appears only for compressive strain above five layers of thickness. Quite surprisingly, both in the trivial and non-trivial phases, we find a plethora of edge-states with energies inside the bulk gap of the system. Some of these states are localized at the side surfaces of the slab and some of them prefer top/bottom surfaces. We find that they can be adiabatically connected to topological states in the chiral limit, where the model supports multiple one-dimensional winding numbers that take different values in different directions in the Brillouin zone. Finally, around high-symmetry points their presence can also be explained by the mirror Chern number and Wilson-loop invariants

authors.name: Jan Skolimowski, Nguyen Minh Nguyen, Alicja Kawala, Giuseppe Cuono, Carmine Autieri, Wojciech Brzezicki

papers.title: Spin-density wave of ferrimagnetic building blocks masking the ferromagnetic quantum-critical point in NbFe2
papers.summary: In the metallic magnet NbFe2, the low temperature threshold of ferromagnetism can be investigated by varying the Fe concentration within a narrow homogeneity range. NbFe2 is one of a number of compounds where modulated order is found to mask the ferromagnetic quantum critical point. However, here we report the rare case where the masking modulated magnetic order has been fully refined. Spherical neutron polarimetry and high-intensity single-crystal neutron diffraction reveal the first case of a longitudinal spin-density wave masking the ferromagnetic quantum critical point. The spin-density wave is characterised by a large-wavelength incommensurate modulation of its low average moment. It is formed from ferrimagnetic building blocks with antiparallel ferromagnetic sheets. The existence of ferromagnetic sheets and cancellation of the magnetisation only over mesoscopic length scales show local similarity between the spin-density wave and the ferromagnetic parent phase and indicate the spin-density wave's unconventional nature as emerging from underlying ferromagnetic quantum criticality.

authors.name: T. Poulis, G. Mani, J. Sturt, W. J. Duncan, H. Thoma, V. Hutanu, B. Ouladdiaf, I. Kibalin, M. H. Lemee, P. Manuel, A. Neubauer, C. Pfleiderer, F. M. Grosche, P. G. Niklowitz

papers.title: AtomMOF: All-Atom Flow Matching for MOF-Adsorbate Structure Prediction
papers.summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising materials for applications such as direct air capture, where performance depends on how adsorbates bind within the framework. Accurately predicting MOF-adsorbate configurations is therefore important for screening candidate materials. However, traditional approaches are computationally expensive and require a known host structure, while existing generative models rely on rigid-body assumptions and do not explicitly model adsorbates. We introduce AtomMOF, a scalable all-atom flow-matching model that jointly predicts MOF-adsorbate structures from discrete building blocks and adsorbates. Built on a Diffusion Transformer with a building block-based pairwise attention bias, AtomMOF operates in an unconstrained all-atom space and exhibits clear scaling behavior. To improve the structural validity of flexible all-atom models, we also propose Feynman-Kac (FK) steering with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). On the BW dataset, AtomMOF achieves a 85.61% relative increase in match rate and a 34.32% relative reduction in RMSD compared with prior work. MLIP-guided steering further improves validity by 28.7% and reduces formation energy error by 86.5%. On ODAC25, AtomMOF generates adsorption configurations faster than GCMC and, when combined with MLIP relaxation, identifies lower-energy configurations than those in the reference dataset.

authors.name: Nayoung Kim, Honghui Kim, Sihyun Yu, Minkyu Kim, Seongsu Kim, Sungsoo Ahn

papers.title: Surface-Dominated Anomalous Hall Effect in Altermagnetic MnTe Films
papers.summary: Altermagnets have recently emerged as a new class of magnetic materials that combine compensated magnetic order with spin-split electronic band structures. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow MnTe thin films with controlled thickness on InP(111)A substrates. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a large spin splitting of $\approx 230$ meV for bulk bands well below the Fermi level and identify surface states that cross the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements show that a robust anomalous Hall (AH) effect persists down to 2 K and an AH sign reversal occurs near 175 K. By systematically tuning film thickness, growth conditions, and interfacial structure, we demonstrate that the AH response in MnTe films originates from surface states rather than bulk bands. Our first-principles calculations reveal that this surface-dominated AH effect is imprinted by the bulk altermagnetic order and remains unchanged for terminations with opposite Mn magnetic orientations. Our results establish a unique surface transport probe of bulk altermagnetism, demonstrate interface engineering as an effective route to generate and control the AH effect in altermagnets, and provide a unified understanding of the AH response in altermagnetic MnTe films.

authors.name: Ling-Jie Zhou, Zi-Jie Yan, Hongtao Rong, Yufei Zhao, Pu Xiao, Lok-Kan Lai, Zhiyuan Xi, Ke Wang, Tibendra Adhikari, Ganesh P. Tiwari, Zhong Lin, Pascal Manue, Fabio Orlandi, Dmitry Khalyavin, Alexander J. Grutter, Chao-Xing Liu, Binghai Yan, Cui-Zu Chang

papers.title: Computational discovery of cathode materials for rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries
papers.summary: Rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (RAZIBs) attract major interest for deployment in grid-scale energy storage due to higher safety and lower cost when compared to lithium-ion batteries. However, currently studied cathode materials suffer from capacity fade when cycling at rates appropriate for grid-scale applications ($<$ C/2). To address the present limitation on cathode material availability, more than 2000 previously synthesized oxides, chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanion materials were computationally screened for the discovery of highly stable RAZIB cathode materials. The structural, electrochemical, and chemical properties of the materials were respectively evaluated through an investigation of the available Zn$^{2+}$ percolation paths, the stability of the material in aqueous media under RAZIB operation conditions, and the attained transition metal oxidation state during cycling. The transition metal oxidation state and intercalating ion coordination environment were determined to govern the magnitude of the calculated Zn$^{2+}$ intercalation potential, with this finding guiding the development of batteries with high operating voltages. Additionally, the bonding character of Fe-O bonds was contrasted between olivine-FePO$_4$ and $\alpha$-FePO$_4$. The latter was successfully synthesized but was found to be electrochemically inactive as a cathode for RAZIBs. Finally, three previously synthesized materials, but unexplored as cathodes for RAZIBs (CaFe$_5$P$_5$O$_{22}$, RbV(PO$_4$)$_2$, and Mo$_2$P$_2$O$_{11}$), were identified to have high Zn$^{2+}$ intercalation potential, electrochemical stability, theoretical gravimetric capacity, and energy density, and are proposed here for further experimental testing. Overall, the materials identified in this study present a guide for the experimental development of stable next-generation cathode materials for RAZIBs.

authors.name: Caio Miranda Miliante, Yuzhen Deng, Brian D. Adams, Drew Higgins, Oleg Rubel

papers.title: Universal Pareto fronts and trade-off relations in multi-objective optimization of thermal machines
papers.summary: The performance of thermal machines is characterized with several, often competing quantities, such as power, efficiency, energy waste, and resilience to environmental noise. We employ multi-objective optimization to find the best thermal machines operating in the irreversible linear-response regime. We derive exact analytical parameterizations for the optimal (Pareto) fronts associated with mean extracted power, efficiency, entropy production and the amplitude of power fluctuations. These optimal fronts set the quantitative fundamental limits for the performance of linear-response machines, which are achieved under tight coupling conditions (endoreversible machines). The geometry of the fronts is universal: two-, three-, and four-objective trade-offs follow analytical formulae that do not depend on the value of any physical parameter of the machine. Furthermore, we test our results with existing experimental data from different physical systems operating also beyond the linear regime, ranging from atomic to macroscopic scales, and including single-atom engines, colloidal systems, macroscopic engines and power plants.

authors.name: Jos\'e A. Almanza-Marrero, \'Edgar Rold\'an, Gonzalo Manzano

papers.title: Electric toroidal octupolar symmetry in pyrite FeS$_2$ probed by Raman optical activity
papers.summary: In crystals with degenerate phonons, Raman optical activity (ROA), the difference in Raman scattering intensity between circular polarization channels, can arise when the scattering distinguishes components carrying opposite crystal angular momenta. In crystals it has long been associated with structural chirality and more recently with ferroaxial order, which are the electric toroidal multipoles of rank zero and rank one, but whether it can probe higher ranks has remained unknown. Here we report ROA in pyrite FeS$_2$, a centrosymmetric and nonmagnetic crystal whose $T_h$ symmetry forbids the electric toroidal multipoles of ranks zero, one, and two, so that the lowest-rank one it admits is the octupole of rank three. Using circularly polarized Raman scattering in a backscattering geometry, we observe a pronounced circular intensity difference exclusively for the doubly degenerate $E_g$ phonon, reaching about 85% of the mean intensity at an excitation wavelength of 633 nm. The difference reverses sign reproducibly between neighboring {111} facets and is strongly suppressed on {001}. Group theory shows that this difference transforms as the antisymmetric part of the self-product of the mode representation, which contains the octupolar $A_{2g}$ representation for the $E_g$ doublet but not for the $T_g$ triplets and that it must vanish for propagation along $\langle 001 \rangle$. First-principles resonant Raman calculations, evaluated at the three experimental photon energies within the electric-dipole approximation, reproduce the $E_g$ selectivity and the reversal of sign with excitation energy. These results extend ROA from rank-one to rank-three axial multipolar symmetry and establish it as a symmetry-selective, facet-resolved optical probe of symmetries that produce neither macroscopic polarization nor magnetization.

authors.name: Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Hitoshi Mori, Ryotaro Arita, Takuya Satoh

papers.title: Accurate description of the electronic states of the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center in hBN by wavefunction theory
papers.summary: Ensembles of negatively charged boron vacancy (V$_{\text{B}}^-$) centers in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) have emerged as a two-dimensional spin qubit system interfaced with optics to advance nanoscale quantum sensing. However, a comprehensive description of its optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) signal remains challenging due to the strongly correlated nature of the excited electronic states involved in its optical cycle. In this work, we model the energetics, structural relaxation, and transition rates of the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center using a high-level wave-function-based electron correlation method (CASSCF-NEVPT2). We provide a thorough analysis of the excited state fine structure and pseudo Jahn-Teller effects, singlet-triplet quasi-degeneracies, photoluminescence parameters, intersystem crossing pathways, and stress-dependence of the fine structure and decay parameters. Our findings not only clarify the fundamental behavior of the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center in hBN but also establish the theoretical foundation for advancing the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center's readout for integrated 2D quantum sensors.

authors.name: Zsolt Benedek, \'Ad\'am Ganyecz, Oscar Bulancea-Lindvall, Gergely Barcza, Viktor Iv\'ady

papers.title: Strain-Dependent Ionic Transport in Li3YCl6 Solid Electrolytes
papers.summary: Solid-state batteries require electrolytes that sustain high ionic conductivity under the mechanical environment of a functioning cell. Lattice strain, arising from stack pressure, lattice mismatch at interfaces, and more importantly electrochemical cycling, can either enhance or suppress Li$^+$ transport in solid electrolytes, yet how it couples to the underlying diffusion mechanism in Li3YCl6 remains poorly understood. Using Li3YCl6 halide superionic conductor, we address this with large-scale molecular dynamics simulations driven by an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning interatomic potential trained on first-principles data. The ACE model faithfully reproduces experimental and ab initio structural, mechanical, and transport properties of Li3YCl6. Extending the simulations to high temperature reveals a crossover from predominantly one-dimensional hopping at low temperature toward diffusion through a connected three-dimensional pathway network at high temperature. Strain substantially modulates diffusivity: tensile strain enhances it while compressive strain suppresses it. Free-breakpoint model selection resolves two Arrhenius regimes for most strain states, and the fitted $T_c$ varies nonmonotonically with strain. Strain modifies the effective activation energies and the accessibility of diffusion pathways in a temperature-dependent manner. These results quantify the strain sensitivity of ionic conductivity and diffusion pathways in Li3YCl6 solid-state electrolytes.

authors.name: Wei-Fan Huang, Jin Dai, Jiahui Pan, Mingjian Wen

papers.title: Effective increase of a superconducting critical temperature due to a configurational entropy of impurities
papers.summary: We show theoretically that a superconducting critical temperature can be effectively increased in a fine-grained superconductor, where impurities migrate along the grain boundaries. The distribution of impurities affects the spatial profile of the BCS condensate. Thus, BCS condensate acquires entropy equal to the configurational entropy of impurities. In order to employ this entropy into the superconducting phase dynamics, we suggest to use a quasiparticle trap that removes quasiparticle excitations from the superconductor. This makes the concentration of Cooper pairs a dynamic variable of the entropy, and thus influences the Ginzburg-Landau functional of the superconductor effectively reducing the first expansion coefficient or, in other words, increasing the critical temperature.

authors.name: Viktoriia Kornich

papers.title: Phonon-driven nodal surface superconductivity of Fermi arcs
papers.summary: According to recent observations, the topological surface states of Weyl semimetals may develop a superconducting gap, while bulk superconductivity remains absent. What drives the formation of this novel superconducting state is an open question. Here, we show that this phenomenon can arise from the interaction of Fermi arc electrons with both surface and bulk phonons in time-reversal-invariant Weyl semimetals. We identify two competing pairing channels, intra-arc and inter-arc, whose relative strength is governed by the efficiency of Coulomb screening at the surface. The combined effect of the Fermi arcs being disconnected and the weak screening of the Coulomb repulsion at the system's surface causes nodes to appear in the superconducting gap, as observed recently by photoelectron spectroscopy experiments on PtBi2. This suggests manipulation of the Coulomb screening, e.g. by a surface layer coating, as a pathway to engineer the critical temperature, as well as size and symmetry of the surface superconducting gap.

authors.name: Francesco Buccheri, Alessandro de Martino, Jeroen van den Brink

papers.title: Descriptor Non-Uniqueness in Symbolic Regression: Conditional Bayesian Analysis of SISSO Supports
papers.summary: Compact analytical descriptors connect materials properties with interpretable combinations of physical and chemical variables, yet different expressions can capture similar trends in small datasets. We present a conditional Bayesian framework for quantifying competition among symbolic descriptors retained by the Sure Independence Screening and Sparsifying Operator (SISSO) method. Exact enumeration of fixed-size supports within the screened feature union yields posterior support probabilities, feature inclusion probabilities, and Bayesian-model-averaged predictions. Applied to magnetic moments of 88 full-Heusler alloys, the framework reveals substantial descriptor non-uniqueness even when the maximum-a-posteriori support coincides with deterministic SISSO. At both two and three descriptor dimensions, eight supports are required to accumulate 95\% posterior probability. Two prominent two-dimensional coordinates exhibit a Pearson correlation of 0.943 despite their distinct algebraic forms. Five-fold validation with screening repeated within each training fold shows higher prediction errors for Bayesian model averaging and undercoverage of nominal predictive intervals, separating descriptor competition from predictive performance. By making statistically competitive expressions explicit, the framework complements deterministic symbolic regression and provides a probabilistic basis for interpreting composition-property relationships in materials modeling.

authors.name: Satadeep Bhattacharjee

papers.title: Thermodynamic Approach to Momentum Transport in Dense Fluids
papers.summary: We present a new framework for extending Chapman-Enskog theory beyond the hard-sphere fluid model. Rather than relying on effective hard sphere diameters, the approach makes use of on an exchange function which can be related to the thermodynamic properties of the system. We show that two existing extensions, including modified Enskog theory (MET), fit into this new framework. Based on our approach, we propose an alternative to MET that takes into account the potential interaction energy associated with the inter-particle interactions in the fluid. The proposed expression is applied to predicting the shear viscosity of several different simulated fluid models across a wide set of densities $0.05 \leq \rho^* \leq 0.8$ and temperatures $1.5 \leq T^* \leq 4.0$ in Lennard-Jones units. The fluid models considered include both the Weeks-Chandler-Anderson (WCA) fluid and the Lennard-Jones (LJ) fluid. At low and intermediate density, here taken to be $\rho^* \leq 0.3$, we report mean relative prediction errors between $2\%$ and $4\%$ for both these. Across all densities considered, the largest mean relative errors reported are $4.4\%$ and $8.1\%$ for the WCA fluid and LJ fluid respectively. We also investigate other interaction models, including a diatomic molecular model, in order to better understand the limitations of our approach.

authors.name: Christopher Devik Fjeldstad, Jonas Bueie, Astrid S. de Wijn

papers.title: Second-order dc conductivity in the velocity-gauge Keldysh formalism: gauge-invariant decomposition into nonlinear Drude, Berry-curvature-dipole, and quantum-metric responses
papers.summary: We derive a gauge-invariant clean-limit decomposition of the second-order dc nonlinear conductivity in multiband tight-binding systems within the velocity-gauge Keldysh Green's function formalism. In the constant-relaxation-time approximation, the dc response separates into four contributions with distinct lifetime $\tau$ scalings and physical origins: the nonlinear Drude term $\sigma^{\mathrm{ND}}_{ijk}\propto\tau^{2}$, the Berry-curvature-dipole term $\sigma^{\mathrm{BCD}}_{ijk}\propto\tau$, the intraband quantum-metric-dipole term $\sigma^{\mathrm{intra\text{-}QMD}}_{ijk}\propto\tau^{0}$, and the interband quantum-metric-dipole term $\sigma^{\mathrm{inter\text{-}QMD}}_{ijk}\propto\tau^{0}$. The intraband term is a Fermi-surface dipole of the ordinary band quantum metric, while the interband term is written, in the present representation, as a Fermi-sea-type response involving a band-normalized quantum metric. Working entirely within the velocity-gauge Keldysh--Kubo framework, we show that all connection-dependent commutator terms generated in the band-basis expansion cancel exactly between the covariant-quantum-connection sector $\sigma^{\mathcal{C}}_{ijk}$ and the three-Berry-connection sector $\sigma^{\mathcal{T}}_{ijk}$, making the role of the Peierls contact velocity vertices $V_{ij}$ and $V_{ijk}$ explicit; a complementary projector-based derivation appears in Ulrich et al., Phys. Rev. B 113, L201107 (2026), and our Fermi-surface dc-limit expression agrees with that reference after accounting for index and convention differences. As a diagnostic illustration, we introduce a real two-band model in which the Berry curvature and hence the BCD response vanish identically while the intraband quantum-metric dipole remains finite, establishing a practical route to quantum-metric dc responses not reducible to the Berry-curvature-dipole mechanism.

authors.name: Junya Shibata

papers.title: A modified Moss rule highlights underexplored classes of high refractive index materials
papers.summary: High refractive index dielectrics are central to photonic applications, yet the empirical Moss rule imposes a fundamental trade-off between refractive index and optical transparency. We introduce a modified Moss rule anchored to the optical absorption edge rather than the fundamental bandgap, capturing materials where various physical mechanisms suppress absorption well above the electronic gap. Screening the Materials Project database with this metric reveals recurring chemical compositions and structural prototypes in the materials with the most promising refractive index/transparency trade-offs. These materials include chalcopyrites, Zintl pnictides, and early transition metal multi-anion chalconitrides and oxichalcogenide compounds. Hybrid density functional theory calculations reveal that the chalconitride (Hf,Zr)2(S,Se)N2 family can achieve a combination of ultra-high refractive indices, low effective masses and transparency windows extending into the UV, potentially surpassing state-of-the-art TiO2. Our results establish (Hf,Zr)2(S,Se)N2 compounds as a unique and largely unexplored material family for next-generation photonic applications.

authors.name: Eug\`ene Bertin, Finja Tadge, Andrea Crovetto

papers.title: Tunable Signal Penetration and Response Plateaus in Bistable Mechanical Media
papers.summary: Dynamic processing of mechanical signals is crucial for soft robotics and mechanosensing, yet classical viscoelastic materials lack intrinsic tunability and quantitative design rules. We show that internal bistability provides a simple but powerful mechanism to tailor response and signal attenuation in mechanical (meta)materials. In our model, bistable elements switch discretely with an intrinsic timescale between states that differ in potential energy $\epsilon$, equilibrium length $\Delta l$, and spring constant $\Delta k$. We combine Brownian dynamics simulations with discrete Poisson switching at rate $\nu$ and a nonlinear continuum (field) theory for the macroscopic strain relaxation. The model yields closed-form solutions for the linear response and the spatial penetration depth, revealing two complementary phenomena: a universal screening mechanism (akin to the electrostatic `skin effect') that strongly reduces signal penetration when the driving frequency exceeds the internal relaxation rate, and a frequency-insensitive response plateau arising from timescale separation. The attenuation strength, expressed by a screening length, is controlled primarily by the conformational length change $\Delta l$, while the attenuation regime and plateau position are tuneable via $\nu$. A parameter study exposes a fundamental design trade-off: larger $\Delta l$ strengthen dissipation but also raise the elastic energy barrier for state transitions, eventually causing state-locking where damping vanishes. Optimal attenuation thus emerges from a compromise between pronounced bistability and a surmountable barrier. Owing to its analytical tractability and generic formulation, our framework yields explicit design rules applicable to systems from biopolymers to synthetic catch bonds and metamaterials, enabling the design of soft materials with frequency-selective mechanical response.

authors.name: Sven Pattloch, Joachim Dzubiella

papers.title: Quantum-classical crossover in finite spin-1/2 rings with Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction
papers.summary: We study finite spin-$\tfrac12$ rings with nearest-neighbor Heisenberg exchange, Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction, and an external magnetic field. We introduce a phenomenological interpolation parameter between the fully quantum Hamiltonian and a state-dependent mean-field description. Using dissipative Gisin-Schr\"odinger dynamics, we analyze the resulting quantum-classical crossover through local magnetization, connected spin correlations, single-site entropy, and the saturation field of the fully polarized state.

authors.name: Ra\'ul S\'anchez Gal\'an, Robert Wieser

papers.title: Stoner transitions beyond mean-field in two-dimensional electronic systems: a diagrammatic Monte Carlo study
papers.summary: Stoner instabilities for fermions with repulsive interaction have been well studied within the mean-field (ladder) approximation. In this study, we consider two-dimensional electronic systems with one or two valleys and discuss a Stoner transition beyond the ladder approximation. At weak coupling, the corrections to the ladder approximation come predominantly from the renormalization of the particle-hole vertex in the particle-particle channel, and the lowest-order corrections are logarithmically singular in the low-density limit. To investigate the problem beyond the lowest order, we apply the diagrammatic Monte Carlo algorithm and treat ladder and non-ladder renormalizations on equal footing. We find that in a one-valley system, a Stoner transition to a ferromagnetism occurs at low density only if there is a cutoff on the momentum transfer carried by the interaction. In a two-valley system, the restriction is less severe. Here we find either a direct Stoner transition into a spin- and valley-polarized state, or a set of two Stoner transitions via an intermediate valley-polarized state. The pathway is controlled by the anisotropy of the fermionic dispersion.

authors.name: Yueh-Chen Lee, Nikolay V. Prokof'ev, Andrey V. Chubukov

papers.title: Angular momentum splitter effect of $d$-wave axial phonons in orbital altermagnets
papers.summary: We theoretically demonstrate that axial phonons, lattice vibration quanta carrying finite angular momentum, can host a $d$-wave angular momentum texture in orbital altermagnets in the absence of spin-orbit coupling. We consider a minimal electronic tight-binding model with $d$-wave loop-current order that breaks time-reversal symmetry. Within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we incorporate electron-phonon coupling via the molecular Berry curvature and show that the underlying $d$-wave orbital magnetic moment texture of the electronic state is transferred to the phonons without requiring the relativistic spin-orbit coupling. Our results expand the range of platforms available for engineering axial phonons and point to functionality unique to $d$-wave textures, including angular-momentum Seebeck and splitter effects, corresponding to longitudinal and transverse angular-momentum currents driven by a temperature gradient.

authors.name: Dimos Chatzichrysafis, Alexander Mook

papers.title: A numerical study to analyze the interplay of Weissenberg number and viscosity ratio in a log-strain tensorial model for viscoelastic fluids
papers.summary: We present a computational study aimed at exploring the different and independent roles of the Weissenberg number and of the ratio between the polymeric and solvent viscosity contributions in a viscoelastic fluid model. The tensorial model under investigation, recently proposed, is based on a logarithmic relation between the elastic (or recoverable) strain and the elastic stress. In this model, the elastic strain plays the role of a conformation tensor and its evolution equation inherently preserves its determinant and positive definiteness. These properties are also enforced in the computational method employed in the study. A finite-difference discretization in time is combined with a stabilized mixed finite element formulation based on the Variational Multiscale method for the spatial discretization and with a generalized Lie derivative approach for the advection terms. The behavior of the model is analyzed in paradigmatic pressure-driven flows and we find that the value of the viscosity ratio is crucial in determining to which extent non-Newtonian flow profiles are observed upon increasing the Weissenberg number. By comparing the solutions of the log-strain tensorial model with those of a suitable Generalized Newtonian Fluid model, we show that flow-type dependence and memory play a significant role even in the simple planar flow past a cylinder.

authors.name: Nehal Dash, Ramon Codina, Giulio G. Giusteri

papers.title: Multiscale Quasiparticle Electronic Structure and Excitonic Properties of CdSe Nanoclusters
papers.summary: Quantum confinement in stoichiometric $\mathrm{Cd}_n\mathrm{Se}_n$ nanoclusters dramatically attenuates electronic screening, driving a delicate, size-dependent competition between quasiparticle self-energy corrections ($\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$) and exciton binding energies ($E_b$). Here, we present a $GW$/BSE study across a representative size series ($n = 3, 6, 13, 33$) and leverage it to validate a scalable atomistic tight-binding (TB) framework derived from first principles. Our results demonstrate that 1-2 eV spectral blueshifts previously reported in the literature arise from single-particle $GW$ convergence artifacts rather than deficiencies in the electron--hole kernels. We show that the near-perfect cancellation between $\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$ and $E_b$ breaks down as cluster volume increases, driven by the rapid onset of dielectric screening attenuating $E_b$ faster than $\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$ and leading to a pronounced divergence from mean-field predictions. Spatial inverse participation ratio analysis of the electronic structure reveals that optical suppression of fundamental pre-peaks stems from a severe spatial mismatch between localized valence orbitals and delocalized conduction states. Finally, we demonstrate that the confinement-induced scaling of the quasiparticle gap and the optical onset is accurately reproduced by a scissor-corrected, DFT-parameterized TB model. As such, this work provides a quantitative multiscale roadmap for embedding effective many-body effects kernels into computationally efficient models, enabling reliable optical predictions for realistic semiconducting nanostructures containing up to thousands of atoms.

authors.name: Surender Kumar, Martin Th\"ummler, Alexander Croy, Stefanie Gr\"afe, Caterina Cocchi

papers.title: Narrow-Sense Type-III Dirac Cones and Additional Flat Lines on a Honeycomb Lattice with Anisotropic Next-Nearest-Neighbor Hoppings
papers.summary: Critically tilted Dirac cones have attracted considerable attention because of their unconventional electronic properties in two-dimensional massless Dirac-fermion systems. Among them, the narrow-sense type-III Dirac cone is characterized by a flat dispersion along the direction connecting the two Dirac points. Using a tight-binding model on a single-orbital honeycomb lattice, we demonstrate that narrow-sense type-III Dirac cones can be realized by tuning anisotropic next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. Type-I and type-II Dirac cones emerge on either side of the critical point, enabling a systematic investigation of the electronic properties across the type-I, narrow-sense type-III, and type-II regimes. We further find that the present model exhibits additional flat lines in momentum space whose energy coincides with the Dirac-point energy at the narrow-sense type-III critical point. These flat lines lead to a pronounced enhancement of the density of states above the Fermi energy and, consequently, the electronic specific heat is substantially enhanced compared with that expected for an ideal narrow-sense type-III Dirac cone. Our results show that the honeycomb lattice with anisotropic next-nearest-neighbor hoppings provides a simple platform for exploring unconventional thermodynamic properties arising from the energy coincidence of narrow-sense type-III Dirac cones and additional flat lines at the Fermi energy.

authors.name: Keita Kishigi, Yasumasa Hasegawa

papers.title: Unraveling hidden Raman modes in ${\alpha}$-MnTe: Effects of long-range dipole-dipole interactions on phonon bands
papers.summary: In this study, we address the seemingly open question of disparity between the experimentally and theoretically observed Raman spectra for the altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe. We establish that the consideration of long range (LR) dipole-dipole interaction is crucial to accurately estimate the phonon band structure and thereby capturing each of the experimentally observed Raman signatures. The LR correction brings about substantial changes to the high-frequency optical modes and their group-theoretical representations. Specifically, for the highly debated Raman peak around 175 cm$^{-1}$, alongside the Raman silent B$_{1u}$ mode, the LR corrections introduce Raman-active longitudinal optical A$^{\prime}$ and A$_1$, and transverse optical A$_1$ modes. Overall, the calculated Raman spectra suggest that the intensity of these modes is weak in the pristine system, while certain prescribed distortions can increase their intensity. The Raman peak around 140 cm$^{-1}$, as observed experimentally, is identified to be emerging from a higher-order Raman process due to zone off-center contributions, while the other debated 120 cm$^{-1}$ peak has both the zone center and off-center contributions.

authors.name: Susmita Jana, Rajib Sarkar, Dhavala Suri, B. R. K Nanda

papers.title: Efficient Optimization of Tensor Rings with Low-Rank Environments
papers.summary: Tensor-ring (TR) decompositions provide a natural representation of periodic systems but are difficult to optimize because the closed geometry prevents a global canonical form and leads to costly, ill-conditioned environments. Existing periodic Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) methods alleviate this difficulty by compressing long environments to a low-rank representation, reducing local operations to $\mathcal{O}(p\chi^3)$, where $p$ is the retained environment rank. Here, we extend this approach to an efficient two-site Ring-DMRG algorithm and improve its numerical robustness through appropriate gauge transformations and a generalized Davidson solver. A central challenge in the two-site formulation is the truncation step, which must account for the surrounding environment. When this environment is sufficiently separable, a suitable change of frame reduces the truncation to an ordinary singular value decomposition. When it is not separable, we instead use an alternating optimization that retains the full environment. The computational advantage of tensor rings over tensor trains depends on the scaling of the required environment rank $p$ with bond dimension and system size. For critical systems, the divergent correlation length makes long-range observables remain sensitive to the periodic geometry as the thermodynamic limit is approached. In this regime, the environment rank required to reach a fixed accuracy in the observable does not grow with the system size. Ring-DMRG therefore retains the same cubic scaling with bond dimension as standard DMRG, but at a substantially smaller bond dimension. The low-rank environment construction also provides a systematic generalization of belief propagation (BP), with standard BP recovered in the rank-one limit.

authors.name: Matthieu Jeannin, Alessandro Chessari, Jan Von Delft

papers.title: Microscopic structure at the morphotropic phase boundary in lead-barium meta-niobate
papers.summary: Lead-barium niobate Pb$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$Nb$_2$O$_6$ is a tetragonal tungsten-bronze ferroelectric that exhibits enhanced functional properties near a morphotropic phase boundary separating orthorhombic and tetragonal phases. Using first-principles electronic-structure calculations combined with ab initio molecular dynamics, we investigate how Ba substitution modifies cation-site occupancy, local distortions, and polarization behavior across the solid solution. By explicitly accounting for vacancy ordering and the inequivalent $A$-site cages intrinsic to the tungsten-bronze framework, we identify the structural origin of the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition. Increasing Ba content progressively weakens the cooperative in-plane off-centering of Pb ions in the pentagonal channels and promotes out-of-plane displacements of Nb and $A$-site cations, leading to a rotation of the spontaneous polarization from [110] to [001]. The transition occurs near $x \approx 0.6$, in quantitative agreement with experimental phase diagrams. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of the morphotropic phase boundary in Pb$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$Nb$_2$O$_6$ and establish a clear structure-polarization relationship for tungsten-bronze ferroelectrics.

authors.name: Marco Fornari, Virginia Carnevali

papers.title: Multiple windows of eigenstate-selective delocalization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice
papers.summary: We investigate localization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice with a real quasiperiodic onsite potential of strength $W$ and a staggered imaginary quasiperiodic modulation of strength $\lambda$. Using the inverse participation ratio (IPR), normalized participation ratio (NPR), fractal dimension $D_2$, transfer-matrix Lyapunov exponent, and wave-packet dynamics, we find a strongly non-monotonic and state-dependent response. At fixed $\lambda$, varying $W$ yields two distinct delocalization windows, whereas varying $\lambda$ at fixed $W$ produces a single re-entrant delocalization window. These regimes arise within selected eigenstate sectors, where localized states coexist with extended or critical states, leading to mobility-edge-like behavior. The corresponding suppression of the Lyapunov exponent and enhancement of the dynamical RMS spreading are consistent with the IPR, NPR, and $D_2$ results. Finite-size scaling confirms the persistence of the re-entrant features, while the complex-energy spectrum resolves their state-selective structure. The resulting phase boundaries delineate distinct localization regimes in the $(W,\lambda)$ plane. Our results show that the interplay between quasiperiodicity and a staggered non-Hermitian modulation sharing the same quasiperiodic spatial structure can generate re-entrant, state-dependent localization, with implications for localization and dynamics in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices.

authors.name: Souvik Roy, Santanu K. Maiti

papers.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
papers.summary: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

authors.name: Zezhu Zeng, Xia Liang, Hengtai Zheng, Aron Walsh, David E. Manolopoulos

papers.title: Arctic-SAR: A Cross-Sensor RADARSAT Constellation Mission and Sentinel-1 Dataset and Fusion Benchmark for Multi-Task Sea Ice Mapping
papers.summary: Current sea ice mapping benchmarks are mostly built around single-sensor SAR products, limiting the evaluation of cross-sensor variability and the effectiveness of combining observations from different SAR platforms. Models trained on such datasets may also be sensitive to sensor-specific artifacts, radiometric characteristics, and acquisition conditions, which can reduce robustness and limit generalization. To address these limitations, this study introduces Arctic-SAR, a cross-sensor SAR dataset for Arctic sea ice mapping, constructed by matching RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) dual-polarization imagery with Sentinel-1 scenes from the AI4Arctic Sea Ice Dataset. The dataset consists of 221 co-registered scenes and supports multi-task prediction of sea ice concentration (SIC), stage of development (SOD), and floe size (FLOE). In addition to the dataset, we establish a benchmark for cross-sensor SAR sea ice mapping by quantifying the contribution of RCM imagery and evaluating single-sensor baselines alongside representative input-, feature-, and decision-level fusion strategies within a consistent multi-task U-Net framework. Across three independent runs, the test results show that the effectiveness of cross-sensor fusion is strongly dependent on the fusion strategy and prediction task. Decision-level fusion achieves the highest mean combined score of $77.28\pm0.29\%$, essentially matching the Sentinel-1-only baseline at $77.26\pm0.13\%$, while achieving the highest SIC \(R^2\) score. These findings show that Sentinel-1 and RCM provide task- and class-dependent information, but that simple joint cross-sensor fusion does not consistently improve generalization over a strong single-sensor baseline. Arctic-SAR therefore provides a benchmark for cross-sensor SAR fusion research in automated Arctic sea ice mapping.

authors.name: Niloofar Azad, Kyle Gao, Javier Noa Turnes, Youssef Nafea, Linlin Xu, David A. Clausi

papers.title: Destructive augmentations for prostate lesion segmentation on heterogeneous biparametric MRI data
papers.summary: Training prostate lesion segmentation models on biparametric MRI (bpMRI) is limited by small datasets with heterogeneous imaging acquisition protocols and annotations. In this work, we train a segmentation model on a combined cohort of 1,579 lesion-containing training cases from five datasets, representing, to our knowledge, the largest collection of prostate lesion annotations used for this task. Additionally, we investigate two complementary improvements to the widely used nnU-Net framework. First, we introduce a random wavelet augmentation and show that random sym4 (Symlet) wavelets outperform random convolution augmentation in terms of average Dice score, with only a modest reduction in F1 score due to lower precision. Second, we evaluate instance-level losses and show that Connected-Component-based Dice (CC-Dice)-CE loss complements BackSplit, yielding better performance than BackSplit alone. Together, these improvements achieve the best overall performance, reaching a Dice score of 0.614 on the public Prostate158 test set and establishing a new state-of-the-art on this benchmark. We publicly release our training code and model weights.

authors.name: Thibault Heintz, Rachit Saluja, Seungbin Park, Daniel Margolis, Timothy McClure, Mert R. Sabuncu, Heejong Kim

papers.title: SideAge-RiskNet: Predicted Mammographic-Age Features for Future Breast Cancer Risk and Laterality Prediction
papers.summary: Whether breast-specific mammographic aging provides information beyond chronological age for future cancer prediction remains unclear. We propose SideAge-RiskNet, a framework integrating predicted mammographic-age features with breast-specific representations for multi-year breast cancer risk and conditional laterality prediction. A side-aware DenseNet121 trained on never-cancer reference examinations estimates left and right breast ages. Age-adjusted residuals and bilateral age descriptors are subsequently fused with corresponding image representations, while clinical variables contribute through an image--clinical risk branch. The framework jointly predicts cumulative cancer risk over 1--5 years and the subsequently affected breast among unilateral cancer cases. Across 4,480 EMBED and 248 external examinations, pre-cancer scans demonstrated pronounced bilateral age asymmetry. SideAge-RiskNet established state-of-the-art performance in 1--5-year risk assessment over Mirai and AsymMirai with mean risk AUROCs of 81.73% on EMBED and 72.83% on CSMC. Furthermore, it enabled conditional cancer laterality prediction, achieving AUROCs of 73.26% and 82.53%, respectively. This demonstrates the critical utility of bilateral aging phenotypes in localized breast cancer risk surveillance.

authors.name: Haoyan Ding, Encheng Su, Chaowei Wu, Lixia Wang, Qian Wang, Garima Diwan, Linda Azab, Yibin Xie, Debiao Li

papers.title: CNVAE: Anatomically Correct Segmentation via Conditional Generative Modeling
papers.summary: Supervised deep learning segmentation models, although unparalleled in performance, are not immune to anatomical mistakes. We develop a segmentation-by-generation paradigm extending the Nouveau VAE (NVAE) generative framework for anatomically correct cardiac segmentation. In particular, we propose a novel conditional NVAE model (CNVAE) for conditional shape generation, and explore its capabilities for image segmentation in two scenarios: (1) direct image-to-mask CNVAE for one-step segmentation; (2) mask-to-mask CNVAE for refinement of segmentation masks produced by third-party segmentation models. Both models are lightweight and return consistently anatomically valid segmentation masks (> 98% success rate, an improvement of 15% above state-of-the-art segmentation models) on the cardiac segmentation/editing tasks of interest, without loss of accuracy in segmented contours.

authors.name: Freddy Jiang, Loic Le Folgoc, Elsa Angelini

papers.title: Volumetric Latent Diffusion for Brain Tumour Segmentation with Missing Modalities
papers.summary: Brain tumour segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging normally assumes that all four imaging sequences are available, but in clinical practice one or more are frequently missing. Existing methods for incomplete inputs learn modality-invariant representations or distil from a full-modality teacher, and return a single deterministic mask. Gen- erative formulations instead model a distribution over plausible masks, but the cost of sampling at full resolution has largely confined them to two dimensions. This paper proposes a three-dimensional conditional latent diffusion framework for whole-tumour segmentation from incom- plete multi-sequence MRI. Images and annotations are first compressed by two volumetric autoencoders, which makes diffusion over whole vol- umes affordable, and sequences are dropped at random during training so that a single model handles every combination of missing sequences. Because the model samples rather than predicts, repeated draws also yield a voxel-wise map of disagreement at no extra training cost. Evalu- ations on 2,601 studies from BraTS 2023 and 2024 show that the method reaches 0.955 Dice with all four sequences and 0.904 with FLAIR alone, and that it is the most accurate of the four methods compared in eight of the fifteen configurations. The disagreement between draws widens as sequences are withheld, giving a signal that accompanies the prediction rather than replacing it

authors.name: Toan Nguyen Hai, Hung Nguyen Tuan, Ba Luong Son, Huynh Trinh Ngoc

papers.title: RapidMitDet: Boosting Computational Efficiency for Mitosis Detection via Magnification Alignment
papers.summary: Automated mitosis detection is a critical research focus, enabling pathologists to rapidly assess mitotic indices for tumor malignancy evaluation. However, most of the existing detection approaches suffer from significant computational inefficiency due to the giga-pixel image resolution of Whole-Slide Images (WSIs), which greatly hinders their clinical applicability. In this study, we propose RapidMitDet, a computational efficient mitosis detection approach. Our method employs a coarse-to-fine framework, first identifying mitotic candidates at lower magnification and then confirming them at higher magnification. In the coarse-detection stage, we introduce magnification-aligned knowledge distillation to reduce the information gap between magnification levels while minimizing the performance degradation in the lower magnification detection model. In the subsequent fine-classification stage, we propose adaptive triplet learning (ATL) to optimize infomative sample selection, thereby enhancing discrimination between mitotic and non-mitotic instances. Experimental results show that RapidMitDet achieves the optimal accuracy-efficiency balance at 20x magnification, improving computational speed by up to 5.62 times over the latest state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Due to its lightweight model design, RapidMitDet can also deliver efficient detection at higher magnification (40x) while achieving even higher detection performance. In WSI-level evaluations, our method shows strong agreement with pathologists' diagnoses (ICCs: 0.879 (40x), 0.822 (20x)) while maintaining superior efficiency, highlighting its potential for clinical application. Code is available at https://github.com/logincat/RapidMitDet

authors.name: Longfei Wang, Jiatai Lin, Junyu Guo, Chaoqun Chen, Danyi Li, Lili Zhai, Jingqi Huang, Tianpeng Deng, Zhenwei Shi, Ying Wang, Changhong Liang, Xiaojing Guo, Li Liang, Zaiyi Liu, Chu Han

papers.title: EMT Modeling and Coordinated Mode-Transition Ride-Through Control of Modern Data Centers
papers.summary: Large data centers are emerging as power-electronic loads whose response to grid voltage disturbances can affect bulk-system stability. This paper presents the composition and control characteristics of a proprietary electromagnetic transient (EMT) model of a modern data center comprising an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) with battery energy storage, induction-motor cooling loads, a computer room air handler (CRAH) driven by a variable-frequency drive (VFD), and an aggregated server load. A voltage-based state machine coordinates three aspects of the facility response: the UPS operating mode (eco, double conversion, or battery), the supply path of the CRAH, and a ramped reconnection of the grid-side UPS converter after the disturbance clears. A 100 MW facility is implemented in PSCAD/EMTDC and benchmarked against the PSSE PERC1 aggregate data center model under a symmetrical three-phase fault and low- and high-voltage ride-through (LVRT/HVRT) events. The two models agree closely in their voltage and active-power trajectories, while the EMT model also resolves the converter and motor-reacceleration transients that the phasor-domain model cannot.

authors.name: Junyuan Zheng, Salish Maharjan, Min Lwin, Soummya Roy, Zhaoyu Wang, Wenlong Shi, Feng Qiu, Rajarshi Roychowdhury

papers.title: Multi-objective Electric Vehicle Charging Strategies at Energy Hubs with Justice-informed Profit Distribution among Users
papers.summary: This paper studies potential energy cost savings in electric vehicle (EV) charging hubs when users allow cooperative vehicle-to-grid (V2G), and how such savings should be redistributed. To this end, we present multi-objective operational strategies and justice-informed profit sharing methods for a charging energy hub equipped with a battery storage system and solar panels. Specifically, we first frame the dynamic energy hub operational problem aiming to minimize a combination of grid costs and emissions, accounting for time-varying prices and energy mix as well as storage system and EV battery degradation, which is especially relevant when considering V2G operations. We parse the problem as a second-order conic program that can be efficiently solved to global optimality. Our real-world case-study shows the importance of flexibility for hub operation: Equipping a charging station with a stationary battery and leveraging dynamic V2G can significantly reduce the total costs and emissions compared to conventional settings without a battery or dynamic charging by more than 10%. To redistribute these cost benefits to users, we compare standard Nash bargaining with a justice-informed sufficientarian version which caps charging prices to safeguard adequate access to affordable charging. Our results show that the sufficientarian approach better accounts for inequalities in flexibility capital without significantly affecting aggregate costs, highlighting how justice-informed pricing only marginally affects total revenues.

authors.name: Twan Stolwijk, Diego Fernandez-Zapico, Alessandro Piazza, Mauro Salazar

papers.title: Physical Sensing Verification for Cognitive ISAC against UAV Spoofing via Digital Twins
papers.summary: As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets 5G and 6G base stations detect drones, software agents will soon act on what they sense. This amplifies the threat of a relay replaying the base station's signal as a phantom drone. For such cognitive ISAC systems, this paper proposes a wall-based physical check. A digital twin (DT) predicts where a real target's wall echo must arrive; a relay can fake range, but not where its own reflections come from. The paper proves that line-of-sight beam steering cannot expose a matched relay, and that, under stated conditions, a single-antenna relay faking a wall echo leaves a telltale echo where a genuine target leaves none. In a pre-registered ray-tracing study, the twin's evidence separated genuine targets from replays perfectly (AUC 1.000) on held-out streets, and a later-registered passive check needing no extra transmission accepted every genuine target and no replay. The primary active probe was inconclusive, at 5.3\% false acceptances against a 5\% limit, for lack of threshold margin. At the evaluated relay positions, the conditional bound certifies 3 of 24 held-out streets, reproduced on fresh ones, against single-antenna relay signals meeting its conditions, adaptive or fixed, and 11 of 24 at double bandwidth.

authors.name: Seyed Bagher Hashemi Natanzi, Bo Tang

papers.title: A Gamma-Mixture Solution for Definite Noncentral Complex Gaussian Quadratic Forms
papers.summary: Finding exact solutions for the statistics of definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms (CGQFs) has long been a challenging problem. Among existing exact approaches, Raphaeli's formulation [1] remains the most computationally efficient.
